2026-09-05 (10)
- Added an [API-CALL-MIX] line to the end-of-cycle summary (build 25). coc_health has tracked
  cycle_calls_by_op since it was written but NOTHING ever logged it, so the actual per-cycle API
  call mix has never been observable -- every claim about "get_league_war() dominates during
  CWL" was inference, not measurement. Logged from the coc_stats snapshot already fetched at
  that point, sorted by volume, wrapped so a stats line can never break a cycle.
- Why it matters now: Stage 3 removed retention for exactly ONE object, the coc.ClanWar from
  get_current_war_from_api() -- the only uncached, exclusively-owned war object in the cycle
  (single call site, verified by sweep). Every OTHER war object comes from get_league_war(), is
  cached in _league_war_cache, and is therefore shared and correctly never severed. So Stage 3's
  benefit stops precisely where CWL, the heaviest period, puts most of its load. This line
  measures that ratio instead of assuming it.
- Sketched Stage 4 in plans/tracker-0009-phase1-war-payload-retention.md: converting
  _league_war_cache to hold payload dicts rather than coc.War objects. Three costs it would
  remove, not one: ~174k objects held live and walked by every sweep (1000-entry cap x ~174
  tracked objects per war, created post-startup so gc.freeze() never covers them); unsevered
  cyclic garbage on every eviction; and -- the part easy to miss -- the per-war-tag
  asyncio.Locks in process_orphaned_cwl_wars(), which exist ONLY because get_league_war()
  returns the same instance to both sides of a match and coc.War.attacks/.members are
  generator-backed ("ValueError: generator already executing"). Plain dicts are concurrency-safe
  to read, so those locks become unnecessary -- a throughput win at peak CWL load.
- The dominant consumer does not even want the object: process_orphaned_cwl_wars() (19,214
  [ORPHANED-CWL] finalisations on PROD today) passes final_war straight to save_war_object(),
  which immediately calls build_war_payload() on it. Highest volume AND simplest need, so it is
  the natural first slice.
- Deliberately NOT started. Stage 4.0 is the gate: read [API-CALL-MIX] over a full CWL day on
  PROD first. If league-war turns out to be a minority of load even during CWL, the stage closes
  as "measured, not worth it" -- which is a perfectly good outcome and the whole reason to
  measure before migrating ~29 call sites.
- 3063 tests pass. pyright clean.

2026-09-05 (8)
- Stage 3 exit-path audit (build 23). Walked every code path in the update cycle to check
  whether Stage 3 actually covers all of them, rather than sampling. Found one real functional
  gap and four stale comments; the payload contract itself is intact.
- BUG FIX: release_war_object() only ran immediately before `return _result`, so it silently
  missed every OTHER exit from fetch_clan_war_data(). Two live leak paths: (a) the
  `state == 'not_in_war'` branches return None while holding a REAL coc.ClanWar (coc.py
  sometimes returns a war object with empty clan/opponent instead of None) -- these fire
  regularly, they are part of the per-cycle no_war count; (b) any exception after a successful
  fetch propagates as WarDataFetchError with the graph unsevered. Both leave a cyclic graph
  nothing reclaims until a sweep walks it -- exactly the cost release_war_object() exists to
  avoid. Fixed by moving the sever into a `finally` on the function's existing outer try, so it
  is now a property of the function rather than of one branch. coc_war_obj/_war_obj_is_shared
  hoisted above the try so the finally can always reference them (an exception before the fetch
  would otherwise make the finally itself raise NameError).
- The build-21 ownership guard is preserved inside the finally: a §5.3 CWL fallback swaps in a
  CACHED league war shared by ~29 call sites, and severing that would corrupt the cache entry
  for every later reader. Safe to run after `return _result` is evaluated because _result holds
  only the payload dict and already-materialised strings, never the object.
- Verified the exit-path analysis is complete: get_current_war_from_api() (the only UNCACHED,
  owned war-object source) has exactly one call site in the whole cycle. Every other war object
  in the cycle comes from get_league_war() and is cached/shared -- correctly never severed. The
  codebase states this itself at QBhelperfunctions.py:8349 ("get_league_war() returns the same
  cached coc.War instance for both sides"), independently confirming the build-21 fix.
- Verified the war_data dict contract producer-to-consumer: fetch emits clan_tag, war_payload,
  end_time, opponent_tag, state; every consumer reads only those. An apparent mismatch
  (war_tag/type/league_group/is_cwl read but not produced) was a false alarm -- those reads are
  in build_war_summary(), whose parameter is also named war_data but receives the JSON payload.
- Stale comments corrected, all describing the pre-Stage-3 world and all now actively
  misleading: QapBot.py's del-fetch_results memory-hygiene comment and the Phase-3 slot-clearing
  comment both claimed fetch_results holds coc.War objects (it holds payload dicts now);
  fetch_clan_war_data()'s and process_clan_war_data()'s docstrings both still documented
  'war_obj: coc.War object' as part of the contract Stage 3 removed.
- FLAGGED, NOT CHANGED: _MAX_INACTIVE_PER_CYCLE = 1500 was chosen as a MEMORY bound justified by
  each polled clan's coc.ClanWar sitting in fetch_results. Stage 3 removed that retention, so
  the per-clan half of that cost model no longer holds and the cap has not been re-tuned. Left
  alone deliberately (needs measurement, and PROD is mid-backlog-drain), but the comment now
  says so instead of implying the old number is still justified -- raising it is the obvious
  lever if a deferred backlog ever needs to drain faster.
- Tests: 3 new in tests/unit/test_release_war_object.py::TestSeverCoversEveryExitPath (sever
  reached from a finally, not inline before the return; ownership guard survived the move with
  all 4 fallback markers intact; both flags hoisted above the try). The build-21 structural test
  correctly FAILED on the refactor and was updated to the new shape rather than deleted.
  3063 tests pass. pyright clean.

- The build-21 cached-war guard is still UNEXERCISED: [CWL-FALLBACK] and

- [CWL-CACHE-EVICT] correctly printed NO object-count suffix - the nightly measurement has not

- EDGE CASE 1, investigated and cleared: archive_differs jumped from 0/cycle (build 19) to
  9.4/cycle (build 22), which looked like Stage 3 changing computed values. It is not. Per-cycle
  it decays 60 -> 12 -> 0 -> 0 -> 9 -> 0 -> 4 -> 0 -> 0: restart backlog draining, then ordinary
  late-attack updates. Build 19's zero was a mid-run steady state whose backlog had already
  drained. Decisive evidence: all 85 of those wars are byte-identical to PROD across 30,000
  field comparisons.
- EDGE CASE 2, investigated and cleared: the orphan-REGULAR stratum
  ([FINALIZE-ORPHAN-REGULAR], "state=in_war, can't refetch from API") shows real differences -
  DEV state='in_war' where PROD reached 'war_ended', and lower attack counts. All are DEV
  observation gaps, not computation errors, and the invariant proves it: DEV's attack count is
  ALWAYS <= PROD's, never greater. DEV runs intermittently and missed those wars entirely;
  PROD ran throughout. The worst case (PRRCLVPJ_202609040922, DEV 0 stars / 0 attacks vs PROD
  30 / 18) was traced to its archived source file, which contains 0 attacks and 0 stars: DEV
  finalized exactly what it held. This path cannot refetch by definition, so build 19 given the
  same empty file would write the same zeros - Stage 3 is not implicated.
- Worth knowing but NOT a live problem: that path will write an all-zero war record into
  permanent history when its temp file is empty. Checked on PROD - of 140,138 rows written
  since 2026-09-04, 66 (0.05%) were finalized while still in_war and ZERO were empty. So it
  needs an instance to miss a war's entire duration, which is normal for DEV and has not
  happened on PROD. Recorded rather than fixed.

2026-09-05 (6)
- MEASUREMENT (build 22) for the GC exposure tracker-0009 Stage 3 did not remove. Stage 3
  stopped Phase 1 retaining a coc.ClanWar across the cycle; what remains is _league_war_cache
  (cap 1000) and _league_group_cache (cap 200), which hold coc.py graphs created AFTER startup,
  so gc.freeze() never covers them and every full sweep walks them. Evicted entries are cyclic
  and nothing severs them (severing is unsafe - they are shared, see Pitfall 61). Instrumented
  rather than guessed at, because the obvious fixes (shrink the caps, evict harder) trade API
  calls for GC time and that trade needs a number.
- CacheManager.measure_cwl_cache_gc_footprint(sample=N): counts GC-TRACKED objects reachable
  from both CWL caches. Counts tracked objects, not bytes, because a sweep's cost tracks the
  container objects it must walk - an untracked str or int is free to it. (Deliberately a
  different question from coc_cache.get_memory_usage_mb(), which measures bytes for the memory
  report.) Uses the same gc.get_referents() walk and the same seeded-roots boundary that
  walker proved necessary, so it cannot wander into coc.Client and charge the session,
  throttler and CacheManager once per entry.
- Runs in the NIGHTLY maintenance window only - the walk is far too expensive for a live cycle,
  and that window already holds the process's only full sweep with commands blocked. Sampled
  (120 entries) so a full 1000-war cache cannot stretch maintenance.
- The nightly sweep now also times a SECOND back-to-back gc.collect(). The first both finds
  garbage and walks the live set; the second has no garbage left to find, so its duration is
  the pure live-set walk cost. That is the total the CWL attribution is a fraction of - without
  it we would be scaling a number that includes work these caches are not responsible for.
  Logged as [NIGHTLY-MAINTENANCE] ... (live-set walk Xs) and [GC-ATTRIBUTION].
- Per-cycle, [CWL-CACHE-EVICT] now appends "~N object(s) now cyclic garbage awaiting a sweep",
  converting the eviction COUNT the line already had into the number that predicts GC cost,
  using objects-per-entry from the last nightly measurement. Costs nothing on the hot path, and
  prints NOTHING until a measurement has actually run rather than inventing a constant.
- FIRST DATA POINT (dev, synthetic, 200 realistic 15v15 war_ended CWL wars): 174 tracked
  objects per cached war, so ~174,000 objects held live at the 1000 cap. But the marginal
  live-set sweep cost measured only ~1.5ms for 200 wars, extrapolating to ~8ms at the cap -
  which would make this a NON-issue, not the follow-up it looked like. Do not act on that
  number: it is dev hardware, and PROD's memory-latency wall has already mispredicted twice in
  this plan, both optimistically (a 0.018s dev estimate came back as 2.050s on PROD). The
  percentage figure from a synthetic process is meaningless too, since total live objects there
  is tiny. The nightly [GC-ATTRIBUTION] line on PROD is the number that decides whether
  anything more is worth doing here.

2026-09-05 (5)
- BUG FIX (build 21), found by auditing every war-finalization and CoC-API path in the update
  cycle: release_war_object() could sever a CACHED, SHARED coc.ClanWar. fetch_clan_war_data()
  normally owns its war object (get_current_war_from_api() is explicitly uncached, "always
  single-use"), but all four §5.3 CWL fallbacks replace coc_war_obj with a war returned by
  _find_active_cwl_war_for_clan() -> CACHE.get_league_war(), which serves the SAME object
  identity out of CACHE._league_war_cache (TTL 2h, cap 1000, war_ended served from cache for the
  whole TTL). ~29 call sites outside cache_manager read that cache: CWL leaderboards, group
  stats, orphan processing. Severing one leaves the cache entry serving an object whose
  back-references are gone, so the next reader of member.war / attack.member /
  best_opponent_attack silently gets None. That is a wrong number in war history, not a crash.
- PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by Stage 3: build 14 added this call unguarded at the Phase-3
  site (release_war_object(war_data.get('war_obj'))), and Stage 3 moved it into
  fetch_clan_war_data() equally unguarded. It has never fired because the CWL fallback is rare —
  zero [CWL-FALLBACK] occurrences across every observed window. A latent correctness bug that
  logs nothing when it triggers.
- Fix: fetch_clan_war_data() tracks provenance in _war_obj_is_shared (False for the owned
  get_current_war_from_api() object, True at each of the four fallback reassignments) and severs
  only when it owns the object. Cached league wars are left to evict_stale_cwl_caches() and the
  collector: a shorter GC pause is not worth a silent wrong-data bug in CWL leaderboards.
- Tests: TestCachedWarsAreNeverSevered in tests/unit/test_release_war_object.py — a control
  proving severing really is destructive on a real coc.ClanWar graph, a guard test proving a
  shared war survives, and a structural test pinning the guard in the source (the function needs
  live API objects to run, and an unguarded sever raises nothing, so the source is what can be
  asserted). The count of 4 fallback markers is asserted so a NEW fallback that forgets the flag
  fails the suite.
- AUDIT RESULT for the rest of the cycle (the question was: do other paths still hold coc
  objects we forgot?). Long-lived coc object stores are _league_war_cache (coc.ClanWar, cap
  1000), _league_group_cache (coc.ClanWarLeagueGroup, cap 200) and coc_clan_cache (coc.Clan).
  All three are bounded, deliberately SHARED caches, so severing them is unsafe by design, not
  an oversight — they are the same category as the coc.Clan objects that maybe_chunk_collect()
  covers rather than severs. temp_war_objects was checked and holds payload DICTS, not coc
  objects (already migrated by §3 Step 2). History writes funnel through a single door
  (db_manager.add_war_records via flush_pending_war_writes), fed by two producers: the regular
  war_ended path and process_orphaned_cwl_wars(); both finalize from temp files, i.e. from the
  payload, which is why the DEV/PROD diff matched on both.
- Note on the remaining GC exposure: the 1000 cached league wars are ~195 objects each and are
  NOT in the frozen permanent generation (they are created after startup), so a full sweep walks
  them. Evicted entries (208 in the observed cycle) become cyclic garbage no one severs. Not
  addressed here; recorded so the next GC pass starts from a measurement rather than a guess.

- Combined Stage 3 cross-instance evidence: 80 wars, 1,554 attack rows, ~31,000 field
  comparisons, zero mismatches, across BOTH finalization paths.
- METHOD NOTE: the first pass sampled war_summary uniformly at random and reported "40 wars"
  without characterising WHICH code path produced them. Random sampling over a mixed population
  does not demonstrate per-path coverage — with 75% of rows from one path and 25% from another,
  an unstratified sample can silently under-represent either, and reporting it as though the
  population were homogeneous overstates what was checked. Stratify by code path first, then
  sample within each. Generalised as Pitfall 60.
- RETRACTION of the correction in 2026-09-05 (3): calling the earlier shadow-mode checkpoint
  "PROD" was CORRECT. c:\python\QapBot\data holds PROD's log and DB, routinely copied to DEV so
  that analysis does not need to touch PROD. The one-time direct PROD access (read-only) was
  granted specifically to compare build 19 and build 20 side by side. The 2026-09-05 (3) bullet
  claiming the checkpoint measured DEV traffic is withdrawn; that "correction" was an assumption
  about the environment made without asking, layered on top of the very data it misread.

2026-09-05 (2)
- tracker-0009 Stage 3 (build 20): the payload is now AUTHORITATIVE and the coc.ClanWar is no
  longer returned from Phase 1 at all. fetch_clan_war_data() returns war_payload + end_time only;
  process_clan_war_data() builds temp-war stats via stats_from_war_payload(). Retaining the war
  graph across Phase 1 -> Phase 3 was keeping it LIVE for the length of a cycle, and a sweep's
  cost tracks what it WALKS - that was the ~1.2s of per-cycle GC pause build 17 measured.
- release_war_object() moved from the Phase-3 site to the end of fetch_clan_war_data(), which is
  now the coc object's true last use. Safe because get_current_war_from_api() explicitly does not
  cache war data ("always single-use"), so no other holder can be reading it. The function is
  kept (CWL get_league_war() paths, and as the coc.py back-reference canary); only the call site
  moved. QapBot.py's Phase-3 finally now just does maybe_chunk_collect().
- QapBot.py's smart-backdating fallback to war_obj.end_time is gone; war_data['end_time'] has
  carried it since Stage 2 and is the same string form, so _DT_RE parses it unchanged.
- FOUND DURING THE FLIP, and shadow mode could never have caught it: the coc loop ABORTED the
  whole clan (logging.error + return False) on a member with no name/tag, while
  stats_from_war_payload() skipped the member. A return False happens BEFORE the shadow block is
  reached, so no amount of live divergence data could have surfaced it - it took reading both
  loops side by side. stats_from_war_payload() gained strict=True (returns None) so
  process_clan_war_data() reproduces the abort exactly. Typed via @overload so strict=False
  keeps a non-Optional return.
- Fixed while migrating that error path: the old message concatenated adjacent string literals
  where only the FIRST was f-prefixed, so it logged the LITERAL text {tag_m} and {clan_tag}
  instead of the values. It now interpolates.
- Removed: _compare_shadow_stats() and its TestShadowComparator suite. With one path left it
  could only compare the payload against itself. Cross-path parity is still covered offline by
  tests/integration/test_war_payload_parity.py, which reconstructs a coc.ClanWar from a payload
  and runs both extractions.
- Also dropped a dead _opp_clan local in process_clan_war_data() (assigned, never read).
- VERIFICATION: full 30,975-file temp corpus through the parity harness, zero mismatches; 3,040
  unit/integration tests green; pyright clean. Shadow evidence that gated this: ~2h24m on PROD
  build 19, 22,032 comparisons on CWL-dominated live data (5,136 of 5,424 finalised wars were
  CWL), zero divergence in any field, zero exceptions, DB row counts cross-checked against the
  log's own counters.
- CORRECTION to the Stage 3 gate recorded on 2026-09-05 (1): two of its three clauses were
  UNSATISFIABLE and I treated their non-satisfaction as evidence. (a) "observe a war_ended
  finalisation" - the shadow block sits inside `if state in ('preparation','in_war')`, so it can
  never see one; (b) "observe a 5.3 CWL fallback" - the payload is built at the return, AFTER
  any fallback has replaced coc_war_obj, so both paths read the same object and a fallback cannot
  produce a divergence. Lesson recorded in the plan: check that a gate condition is REACHABLE
  before treating its absence as a signal.

2026-09-05 (1)
- tracker-0009 Stage 2 (shadow mode) implemented. Phase 1 now carries war_payload and end_time
  alongside war_obj; process_clan_war_data() computes the temp-war stats BOTH ways, compares, and
  logs [PAYLOAD-PARITY] on divergence — while still writing the coc-object result. The payload is
  NOT authoritative, so corruption is impossible by construction. That is the point: §5.1's
  failure mode is a silent 0 reaching war history, which a code revert cannot undo.
- The payload is built at the RETURN statement of fetch_clan_war_data(), not at either
  save_war_object() call. §5.3's CWL fallback can replace coc_war_obj and re-save, so only the
  final object is correct to serialise; building at the return makes that automatic instead of a
  thing to remember. The clan/opponent swap mirrors save_war_object()'s and is duplicated — both
  sites must move together if it is ever factored out.
- Added: stats_from_war_payload() (the candidate replacement member loop, key names taken from a
  REAL temp file per §3 Step 3, not from §2's table) and _compare_shadow_stats(). Float
  comparison is epsilon-based so 1e-9 drift on Total_Dest_Pct cannot spam a warning every cycle.
  The shadow block is wrapped so a failure there can never affect the authoritative path.
- §3 Step 4 done early: QapBot.py's smart-backdating reads war_data['end_time'], falling back to
  the coc object only while Stage 2 carries both. The fallback goes at Stage 3.
- §5.4 respected: war_payload can legitimately be None (save_skip_no_clan) and Phase 3 just skips
  the comparison rather than treating it as an error.
- Offline replay deliberately proves nothing about the field that matters: 6,000 replayed wars
  gave 0 diffs, because reconstruction feeds our computed bestOpponentAttack back in as the API's
  field, so coc.py returns exactly what we computed. That circularity is unavoidable offline —
  Defensive_Stars has both values only on live data, which is precisely why shadow mode exists.
- How to read the first PROD logs (also in the plan): Defensive_Stars differences are EXPECTED
  and their DIRECTION is the signal. Payload higher than coc = the intended improvement
  (find_best_opponent_attack caught a late CWL attack the API field missed). Payload lower, or
  ANY other field differing, = a real problem, since Stage 1 proved those equal over 54,192 wars.
  No [PAYLOAD-PARITY] lines at all is also suspicious — check the payload is non-None.
- Added: tests/unit/test_shadow_stats_parity.py (17 cases). Half pin that the payload reader hits
  the right keys (including the legitimate-zero cases, so a silent 0 is distinguishable from a
  real 0); half pin that the comparator actually DETECTS divergence in every compared field — a
  comparator that cannot fail would make shadow mode worthless while looking green.
- Tests: 3049 pass. QBhelperfunctions.py and QapBot.py are pyright-clean.
- NEEDS PROD DEPLOY (build 19) to collect the [PAYLOAD-PARITY] evidence that gates Stage 3.

  have distinguished that from a broken temp file. Run pyright on the file after any move of
  this kind; it earned its keep here.
- previousBestOpponentAttack is excluded from the round-trip comparison, deliberately. coc.py
  derives it as the max over defenses EXCLUDING whatever best_opponent_attack returns;
  reconstruction has to feed our computed bestOpponentAttack in as the API's field (the API's own
  value is not retained on disk), so a different attack is excluded and a different "previous
  best" results — 76 of 54,192 wars, a fixture limitation not a defect. Same circularity that
  puts Defensive_Stars out of Stage 1's reach. Consumed only by scripts/recover_cwl_war.py,
  never by temp stats or leaderboards.
- Note for future edits: cache_manager.py carries a UTF-8 BOM. Read/write it with utf-8-sig, and
  never ast.parse() its contents read as plain utf-8 — the failure is a misleading "invalid
  non-printable character U+FEFF" pointing at an unrelated line. A first extraction attempt was
  reverted for a different reason (the function was inserted at the block's old indentation
  inside the method, and the call was never inserted) — git checkout of the single file restored
  it cleanly since it was committed.
- Stage 1 gate MET; Stage 2 (shadow mode) may begin, carrying Defensive_Stars and the state
  spelling as its primary targets. Plan updated with per-stage status.

2026-09-04 (23)
- Added: maybe_chunk_collect() — the per-cycle collection is now sliced into generation-0
  passes every 500 clans (GC_CHUNK_EVERY, 0 = off), called from Phase 1 and Phase 3 on one
  shared counter. Measured at cycle shape: max pause 5.8x lower than one end-of-cycle collect,
  with slightly LESS total GC time (dead objects stop being re-walked by later passes).
  Scaling PROD's measured 1.135s by ~5 lands ~0.2s — under the [LOOP-LAG] warn threshold and
  15x under Discord's 3s ACK deadline.
- Why slicing instead of severing the remaining garbage: it is ~669 coc.Clan graphs per cycle
  (103,687 objects / 155 each), cyclic via ClanMember.clan. But cached clans are HANDED TO
  CALLERS and live up to 600s — release_war_object() was only safe because a war's lifetime
  traced to exactly two consumers, and a cached clan's does not. A severed object still held by
  a caller is precisely the bug that surfaces far from its cause. Slicing needs no ownership
  analysis at all. (qaplop's proposal; it is the better trade here.)
- Interval is TUNED, not arbitrary: every-100 measured WORSE than every-500 because per-call
  overhead dominates once slices get small. Re-measure before lowering it.
- Correction to an earlier claim of mine: I had rejected mid-cycle collection outright, arguing
  it would walk live in-flight objects and promote them, reproducing the automatic collector's
  problem. That was wrong. The automatic collector's problem was generation DEPTH (gen-2 sweeps
  walking the whole heap), not timing; gen-0 is shallow and the in-flight population is
  semaphore-bounded (~50 clans), so each slice walks almost nothing live. Measured: no gen-2
  backlog growth across cycles. Documented in PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md so the reversal reads as a
  measured correction rather than a contradiction.
- Note on dev-measured GC numbers generally: PROD is Linux on a Celeron, dev is Windows on a
  fast CPU. The 0.018s -> 2.050s miss in (17) was attributed to memory latency, but allocator
  and platform differences plausibly contribute too. Treat any dev-measured GC TIMING as
  indicative only; object COUNTS (155 per clan graph, 132 per war) are structural and do carry.
- Still unexplained: why build 14's _gc_deliberate flag did not reach the pause logger. Verified
  the flag WAS in build 14's deployed code (git show 9a85b96). Not reproducible on dev — which
  may itself be the platform difference. (22)'s gc.isenabled() label is immune to either cause,
  so this is left as a known-unknown rather than chased further.

  _gc_deliberate flag from (18) did not reach the callback; the exact cause was NOT reproducible
  locally (the same flag-across-to_thread pattern works in isolation) and is most likely this
  file being loaded twice under two module names, a hazard already documented on the
  gc.callbacks dedup guard. Rather than chase it, the label now reads `not gc.isenabled()` as
  the authoritative signal — while automatic collection is off, ANY collection is by definition
  ours — which no module-identity confusion can affect. The flag is kept only for the
  GC_AUTOMATIC=1 case where both kinds can occur.

2026-09-04 (19)
- Fixed properly: the per-cycle GC pause is now removed rather than rescheduled. (17) moved
  collection onto our schedule, which cut stalls from 6/cycle to 1 — but that one still cost
  2.0s (508,769 objects at ~240K/s; the 0.1s dev extrapolation was wrong by 70x, the same
  memory-latency wall already documented for the categorize loop, not a CPU-clock gap).
- Root cause: coc.py's war graph is cyclic by construction — WarClan._war, ClanWarMember.war
  and .clan, WarAttack.war and .member, ClanWarMember._best_opponent_attacker all point back
  into the graph. Nothing in a war is reachable-but-unreferenced, so refcounting can NEVER
  free one; every war survives until a stop-the-world sweep walks it. ~195 objects per clan
  x ~2,600 clans = exactly the 508,769 observed.
- Added: release_war_object() (QBhelperfunctions.py) severs those back-references once the
  graph's last consumer is done, so it becomes acyclic and dies on the last reference drop,
  never reaching the collector. Measured on real coc.ClanWar objects: sweep-only garbage
  2,640 -> 0, and build+drop got FASTER (2.2ms -> 1.2ms per 20 wars) — immediate refcount
  release beats deferred collection.
- Called from Phase 3 in a finally around process_clan_war_data(), the last thing that
  NAVIGATES the graph. Traced the full lifetime first: built in fetch_clan_war_data(),
  returned inside {'war_obj': ...}, read for .end_time by the backdate check, consumed by
  Phase 3. Exactly two consumers, both verified. The finally covers the early-return and
  exception paths too.
- Safety contract, pinned by tests: scalars (state, end_time, start_time, team_size) and
  .clan/.opponent survive — the backdate check needs end_time. What dies is NAVIGATION:
  member.war, member.clan, attack.war, attack.member become None. If you add a consumer that
  walks upward from a member or attack, MOVE the call; do not weaken it. Only materialised
  state is touched (_cs_members/_attacks, never the lazy public properties), so an
  untraversed war is not built just to be torn down.
- Added: tests/unit/test_release_war_object.py (10 cases), using REAL coc.ClanWar objects
  rather than mocks on purpose — the question under test is which references coc.py actually
  holds, and a mock would confirm whatever we assumed while a coc.py upgrade silently brought
  the pause back. One test asserts the graph IS still cyclic, so if coc.py ever drops its
  back-references we find out and can retire this.
- Lesson (PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md): when a GC pause is the problem, "when should collection
  run?" is the second-best question. Ask "why is this garbage collectable-only at all?" first.
- Expected on PROD: [CYCLE-CLEANUP] freed= drops from ~500,000 toward near zero and its
  gc_collect time with it; no [GC-SCHEDULED] line should appear at all (that logger only fires
  above 0.5s). Falsifier: if freed= stays ~500,000, the sever is not reaching the objects.

2026-09-04 (18)
- Fixed (cosmetic, but it mattered): the GC pause logger labelled our own deliberate collects
  as "[GC-AUTO] Automatic gen-N ...". gc.callbacks fires for explicit collections too, so since
  automatic collection was disabled in (17) the log was reporting the exact behaviour the GC
  policy exists to prevent. Deliberate collects (per-cycle, nightly, startup freeze) now log as
  [GC-SCHEDULED]; [GC-AUTO] now means only what it says — CPython picked the moment — so any
  future [GC-AUTO] line is a real signal that the policy is not in effect.

2026-09-04 (17)
- Fixed (the longstanding one): Discord responsiveness during update cycles. Automatic GC is
  now disabled at startup; collection runs on our schedule instead — a young-generation
  gc.collect(1) per cycle in [CYCLE-CLEANUP], and the single full sweep in the nightly
  maintenance window where db_maintenance_mode already blocks commands.
- Why a young-gen collect is enough: the garbage is unavoidable (coc.py's war graph is cyclic
  by construction — WarAttack.war and WarClan._war point back at the ClanWar — so ~2,050 wars
  x ~150 objects per cycle can only ever be freed by a sweep, never by refcounting). But with
  nothing being promoted on CPython's schedule, that whole population is still YOUNG at cycle
  end, so a young-only collect reclaims all of it without walking the long-lived heap.
  Measured at PROD shape: 0.018s and 311,448 objects per cycle, vs the 0.5-2.4s automatic
  gen-2 sweeps it replaces. Over 14 cycles RSS stayed flat (116 -> 120 MB, no drift) and the
  nightly full sweep then found only 1,064 objects in 0.001s.
- Rejected on the way: putting the full sweep in the per-cycle SLEEP window. That only
  relocates the stall — the bot is idle then, which is exactly when a user is most likely to
  be interacting with it. Only the nightly window is genuinely free. (Thanks qaplop.)
- Also rejected: gc.freeze() every cycle. Freezing is right for the big static caches (the
  startup freeze makes a full collect measurably free, 0.056s -> 0.000s over 1M objects) and
  wrong for the war population, which is rebuilt each cycle — freezing it would make its
  garbage permanent, the exact pile-up we are avoiding.
- Removed: gc.set_threshold(700, 10, 20). Written against Python <=3.11 whose default really
  was (700, 10, 10); Python 3.12 raised the gen-0 default to 2000, so on PROD's 3.14 it was
  silently LOWERING gen-0 and tripling how often it ran (1,214 collections vs 425) while
  buying nothing — and 3.13's incremental collector means the gen-2 multiplier no longer gates
  full sweeps at all (threshold2 20 vs 1000: identical gen-2 count). Both halves were dead.
  Never carry a gc.set_threshold() across a Python upgrade without re-measuring — new
  Pitfall 57.
- Added: GC_AUTOMATIC=1 escape hatch (.env.example) to restore CPython scheduling for A/B or
  memory-retention debugging. [CYCLE-CLEANUP] now logs gc_collect freed= so the per-cycle
  collect can be verified from the log rather than assumed.
- Added: tests/unit/test_gc_policy.py (7 cases) pinning the properties the policy rests on —
  that war graphs really are cyclic, that a young collect leaves nothing for the full sweep,
  that repeated cycles do not accumulate, that freezing hides objects and unfreezing returns
  them, and that explicit collection still works while automatic is disabled.
- Docs: PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md ("Discord unresponsiveness during cycles is gen-2 GC") carries
  the evidence table and the three-part policy; Pitfall 57 carries the version-drift rule.
- Verification on next PROD run: [LOOP-LAG] stalls should stop appearing during cycles and the
  sleep window, [GC-AUTO] lines should vanish entirely outside nightly maintenance, and
  [CYCLE-CLEANUP] gc_collect should show a non-zero freed= at roughly 0.1s. If freed= is ~0
  while RSS climbs cycle over cycle, the policy is wrong — set GC_AUTOMATIC=1 and tell me.

2026-09-04 (16)
- Measured (build 11, unprofiled, matched load): the (15) round-trip fix bought NO measurable
  cycle time. Cold Phase-1 68.5s -> 66.0s at 2061 vs 2050 clans — inside noise. The fix stays
  (it removes real work and stops the cost scaling with a pool that only grows), but it is NOT
  a speed-up and must not be cited as one. Docs corrected accordingly; (15)'s "dominant cost of
  the cold cycle" claim was wrong.
- Why it was wrong: cProfile's overhead is proportional to CALL COUNT, so it skews the
  *distribution*, not only the absolute seconds. This bug was almost pure call count (418,000
  round-trips x several frames each), so it floated to the top of the profile on that basis
  alone. A profile ranks suspects; only two unprofiled cycles at matched load confirm one.
  Written up in PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md ("The trap") and as a scope correction on Pitfall 56.
- Also beware the reverse: that same cold cycle went 190.9s -> 150.0s, which is NOT the fix —
  the older cycle's post-Phase-3 tail did 19 extra CoC API calls and twice the [ROLE-SYNC] work.
- FOUND: Discord unresponsiveness during update cycles is gen-2 GC, all of it. 11 of 11
  [LOOP-LAG] stalls match a [GC-AUTO] pause to within the watchdog's 100ms probe resolution;
  p95 between collections is 0.046s. Not GIL contention, not blocking I/O, not our cycle code —
  so no amount of to_thread-ing or yielding can touch it. Longstanding, not a regression:
  [GC-AUTO] maxima are 2.70s (build 2), 5.27s (4), 5.82s (9), 2.44s (11), several of them past
  Discord's 3s interaction ACK deadline.
- Not yet fixed. The existing mitigations (startup gc.freeze of 620,316 objects, gen-2 threshold
  20, nightly unfreeze/collect/freeze) miss it on timescale: these pauses appeared 7 minutes
  after a restart, and the growth that makes sweeps expensive happens inside a single cycle.
  The lever is scheduling, not speed — the per-cycle gc.collect(1) costs 0.000s and the bot then
  sleeps 171-199s, while automatic gen-2 fires 6x mid-cycle at 0.5-2.4s each. See
  PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md ("Discord unresponsiveness during cycles is gen-2 GC").
- No BOT_BUILD bump: documentation and changelog only, no .py changes (still build 11).

- Fixed: the dominant cost of a cold update cycle — a ~418,000-round-trip SQLite storm on the
  event loop during Phase-1. `_save_user_impl()` called `_ensure_clan_exists()` once per player
  of the user being saved (2 queries each), and `_replace_user_players_rows()` issued one
  `await execute()` INSERT per player. The "UNASSIGNED" pseudo-user holds every unlinked player
  the bot has ever seen — 5,794 of 6,076 `user_players` rows on PROD — so discovering ONE new
  unlinked player during a clan poll rewrote the whole pool at ~11,600 event-loop round-trips
  a time. Measured: 17,383 -> 13 round-trips for a 5,794-player save (1337x), identical rows.
- Added: `_ensure_clans_exist()` (db_manager.py) — bulk form of `_ensure_clan_exists()`, chunked
  `WHERE ... IN (?,?,...)` at 400 tags (SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER is only 999 on the Synology
  system SQLite). Deliberately a live bulk query, NOT a "known clan tags" memo: `clans` rows can
  be deleted, and a stale positive would skip a needed insert and surface later as an FK
  violation. `_ensure_clan_exists()` is kept as a single-tag wrapper — it has many callers.
- Changed: `_replace_user_players_rows()` now uses `executemany()`. Atomicity is unchanged — the
  caller wraps it in BEGIN, so a batch failing on one row rolls back exactly as the per-row loop
  did, including the "FOREIGN KEY" retry with `null_clan_tags=True`. The 2026-08-21 duplicate
  player_tag guard is preserved and covered by a test.
- Added: tests/integration/test_ensure_clans_bulk.py (10 cases). These assert the ROUND-TRIP
  COUNT, not just the resulting rows: every correctness test passed throughout the period the

- Docs: found by the build-10 cProfile pass. See qapbot/docs/PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md ("Profiling
  Phase-1") for how to read a loop-thread profile — the `epoll.poll` CALL COUNT is the tell
  (840,029 on the cold cycle vs 7,565 warm) — and COPILOT_PITFALLS_COOKBOOK.md Pitfall 56 for
  the general rule. Not repeated here on purpose.

  bottlenecks, not the same one with a colder cache; profiling only one leads to the wrong fix.

2026-09-04 (14)
- Added: event-loop lag watchdog (QapBot.py). Probes every 100ms and reports any stall as
  a WARNING, plus a 5-minute INFO summary with max/p95 so 'responsiveness is fine' is
  evidence rather than an absence of complaints. This is the direct measurement of the
  long-standing 'Discord commands feel dead during update cycles' symptom: Discord drops
  an interaction that is not acknowledged within 3s, and log-gap analysis found 42 in-cycle
  gaps of 3-10s plus 7 over 10s. Log gaps OVERSTATE blocking though (a yielding loop that
  does not log looks identical), which is why a real probe was needed.
  Verified: fires on a 1.2s synchronous block, stays silent for the same 1.2s of work in
  asyncio.to_thread — which is exactly the distinction that tells us how to fix each stall.
- Added: opt-in cProfile pass over Phase 1 via PROFILE_PHASE1=<n> (QapBot.py), self-
  disarming after n runs. Writes data/logs/phase1_profile_<ts>.{prof,txt} and logs the top
  offenders by tottime. Needed because Phase 1 burns ~44-49s CPU/cycle at cores_busy up to
  1.01 and the obvious suspects are already excluded: coc.py parses responses with orjson,
  and our own serialization measures 0.13s/cycle. Scope note: cProfile instruments the
  calling thread only, i.e. the event loop — to_thread work is deliberately out of scope.
- Changed: temp-war-file serialization stdlib json -> orjson (qapbot/cache_manager.py).
  5.8x faster per call (69us -> 12us on a real 17 KB payload) and byte-identical: verified
  against 400 real temp files, 400/400 identical, zero errors. Honest scale: ~0.13s ->
  ~0.02s per cycle, i.e. ~0.1s of ~110s. Taken because it is free and safe, NOT because it
  moves cycle time. orjson was already present transitively via coc.py; now declared in
  requirements.txt so this module does not depend on another package's transitive tree.
- Docs: PROFILE_PHASE1 and TO_THREAD_WORKERS documented in .env.example.
  Files: QapBot.py, qapbot/cache_manager.py, requirements.txt, .env.example.
  Build 10. 2994 tests pass.

- Added: BOT_BUILD, a monotonic build counter bumped on every code change, plus
  QBcore.source_fingerprint(), logged together at startup as
  "Version: X.Y.Z  build N  src <8 hex>" and shown in /status
  (QBcore.py, QapBot.py, QBdiscordcmds.py).
  WHY: deployment to the server-machine is a file COPY, not a git operation, so "is it
  committed?" says nothing about what is running. This session alone got that wrong twice
  during the CWL performance work -- once analysing a deployed fix as "not deployed", and
  once attributing cycle timings to the wrong build -- and both times the wrong conclusion
  survived several steps before being caught.
  BOT_VERSION is untouched (release number, owner-managed); BOT_BUILD never resets, not
  even across BOT_VERSION bumps.
  The fingerprint is the safety net for the obvious failure mode of a hand-maintained
  counter: it hashes the shipped .py sources (repo-root modules + the qapbot package,
  path included so a rename counts) and cannot drift, so a forgotten bump still shows up
  as "same build, different src". It is diagnostics, so it returns "unknown" rather than
  raising if the tree is unreadable -- it must never be able to stop the bot starting.
  Measured at 5ms on a dev box, startup only.
  Routine documented as Cardinal Rule 17 in .github/copilot-instructions.md, wired into
  the "After Writing Code" checklist and the Changelog Management section so it is the
  same reflex as the changelog entry rather than a separate thing to remember.

2026-09-04 (3)
- Changed: the categorize loop now iterates a cached tracked-clan index instead of all
  ~458K clan_name_cache entries (QapBot.py, qapbot/cache_manager.py, qapbot/coc_cache.py).
  Justified by measurement: [CATEGORIZE-TIMING] reports cores_busy=0.99-1.00, so the loop
  really is one core pinned, and because the cost is dominated by touching scattered dicts
  through a small cache rather than by the arithmetic, the win is in touching fewer of
  them. track_war_updates=1 is 152,402 of 458,715 -> a 67% cut in entries walked.
  Safety design (the risk here is a clan silently never being polled again):
    * The index is a CACHE, rebuilt from clan_name_cache on the hourly full walk the
      passive-refresh scan already performs -- so reconciliation costs nothing extra.
    * Only the False->True direction is dangerous. Those 6 sites now call
      CACHE.note_clan_tracked(), so a promoted clan is polled on the very next cycle.
      True->False is left to expire at the next rebuild: it costs one wasted iteration
      and is never a correctness problem.
    * Each rebuild diffs ground truth against what the incremental path accumulated and
      logs [TRACKED-INDEX] drift naming the missing tags -- so a future mutation site that
      forgets note_clan_tracked() announces itself instead of parking a clan silently.
  note_clan_tracked() creates its set lazily: it is bookkeeping for a cache whose worst
  case is a one-hour delay, so it must never raise inside a real promotion path (and 17
  test fixtures build CacheManager via __new__, skipping __init__).
  Verified by simulating the full lifecycle -- build, indexed cycles, hooked promotion
  (polled next cycle), deliberately UNhooked promotion (missed, as expected), hourly
  rebuild (drift detected, self-healed).
  [CATEGORIZE-TIMING] now also reports scan=full|indexed.
  Expected ~6.5s -> ~2.2s. Note the honest scaling: that is 14% of a light 52s cycle but
  only ~2.6% of a heavy 164s one, where Phase 1 dominates instead.

  counter is still zero at upd=1,958, confirming at full scale that no rewrite is ever
  byte-identical (coc.py's Timestamp repr embeds a live seconds_until= countdown). The

  inside its 103.1s, i.e. 20% of the whole cycle. The two phases have opposite characters

- Fixed: the passive-refresh scan throttle added in (1) degenerated to scanning every cycle
  whenever the passive backlog was drained (QapBot.py). The gate was "rescan if the cache
  is empty", but once the backlog is burned down the scan legitimately returns an EMPTY
  list — so the cache was empty every cycle and it rescanned every cycle. It throttled
  correctly whenever a real backlog existed (PROD 11:04 and 11:09 logged
  passive_scan=skipped after a scan filled the cache), and misbehaved only in the drained
  steady state (10:13-10:53, passive_scan=yes on ten consecutive cycles).
  Now: rescan on the hourly interval, or early only when the previous scan filled at least
  a full _PASSIVE_REFRESH_BATCH_SIZE (i.e. we were limited by the batch, not the backlog,
  so more is probably waiting). Verified by simulation across backlogs of
  0 / 200 / 3,500 / 25,000: burn-down still runs at the full 1000/cycle, and the drained
  steady state drops from 20 scans per 20 cycles to 2.
  Measured saving, from PROD cycles either side of the transition: categorize
  7.34s (passive_scan=yes) -> 6.49s (skipped), i.e. ~0.85s, about 12% of the loop.
  (An earlier dev-box estimate of ~28% / ~2s was too optimistic — noted so the next
  estimate is calibrated against this.)
- Measured: [CATEGORIZE-TIMING] now reports cores_busy=0.99-1.00 at 15.6-16.8 us/clan.
  The categorize loop IS genuinely CPU-bound — one core pinned for its full 7.2-7.7s — so
  the decision in (1) to hold the tracked-clan-index rewrite was based on a bad profile.
  That profile timed only fragments (fast-reject, passive block, crc32) and missed the
  per-clan work for the 152K tracked clans; a faithful full-loop replay costs 0.78 us/clan
  on a dev box, 5x the fragment figure. The residual dev/PROD gap is consistent with the
  server-machine being memory-latency-bound walking 458K scattered dicts through a 2 MB
  cache, which also means the win comes from iterating FEWER entries (the tracked index,
  458,715 -> 152,402) rather than from optimising the loop body.
- Measured: the temp-write identical= counter from (1) reads ZERO on every cycle, including
  cycles with upd=1,518. Cause: the serialized payload embeds coc.py's Timestamp repr,
  which carries a live `seconds_until=` countdown recomputed at every serialization, so no
  two writes of the same unchanged war are ever byte-identical. A dirty-check as originally
  proposed cannot ever fire; it would need to compare with the volatile fields normalised

2026-09-03 (5)
- Added: per-phase CPU accounting, and sized the asyncio.to_thread pool off the workload
  instead of the core count (QapBot.py). First of the three improvements from entry (4);
  the other two (save_war_object dirty-check, incremental categorize) follow separately so
  each can be measured on its own.
- Instrumentation: new [PHASE-1-CPU] and [CYCLE-END] [CPU] lines log wall, cpu
  (time.process_time(), summed over all threads) and cores_busy=cpu/wall. On the 2-core
  server-machine cores_busy ~1.0 means one core pinned — the GIL ceiling for a
  single-threaded event loop, which shows in DSM's aggregate meter as only ~50% and is
  therefore easy to misread as "not CPU-bound"; ~2.0 means genuinely compute-bound; well
  below 1.0 means we are waiting on disk/network. Added because entries (2) and (3) were
  both deployed on inference rather than measurement and both did nothing.
- Changed: to_thread pool 6 -> 16 workers on the server-machine. asyncio.to_thread uses the
  loop's default executor, sized min(32, cpu_count+4) = 6 on 2 cores, shared by every
  to_thread call site (30+ in QBhelperfunctions.py: temp-file writes, sync sqlite3 reads).
  That heuristic assumes CPU-bound work; ours is disk-blocked, and a blocked thread costs a
  core nothing. Now max(16, cpu_count+4), env override TO_THREAD_WORKERS (set 6 to revert).
  Falsifier: if the Phase-3 tail (currently 17-36s/cycle) does not drop, the writes are
  CPU-bound rather than disk-bound and the dirty-check is the only path.
  File: QapBot.py. 2971 tests pass.

2026-09-03 (4)
- Changed: reverted _FETCH_CONCURRENCY 50 -> 20, and documented why the whole API-side
  tuning direction was a dead end (QapBot.py, qapbot/docs/PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md new).
  Both (2) and (3) were deployed to the server-machine and measured from log timestamps:
  concurrency 20 -> 50 moved throughput 25.6 -> 23.4 clans/s (i.e. not at all) while
  per-clan latency went 0.78s -> 2.14s, and the wall-clock throttler at 80 req/s never
  got above a ~53 req/s peak. ms/clan across ten cycles spanning both changes: median
  31.7, range 24-66 — invariant.
  Root cause: the update cycle is CPU-bound on the server-machine (2-core low-power x86,
  no SMT), not API-bound. Little's Law settles it — the fetch semaphore was 100%
  saturated at BOTH settings (25.6*0.78 = 20.0 in flight, 23.4*2.14 = 50.1), so the extra
  latency from more concurrency was spent queueing on the GIL and the to_thread pool
  inside the process, never on the network. Independent calibration: [CATEGORIZE-TIMING]
  does zero API work and takes a rock-steady 7.2-7.8s for ~458k clans every cycle.
  The (3) throttler fix is KEPT — coc.BatchThrottler really does gate on time.process_time
  (CPU seconds) rather than wall-clock, so throttle_limit never meant req/s; that is worth
  having correct, it just was not the binding constraint and buys no cycle time today.
  Real remaining wins are all "remove per-clan CPU work", not "add parallelism": a
  content dirty-check in save_war_object (~2,700 unconditional JSON writes/cycle),
  incrementalising the categorize scan (~35 min/day of pure CPU), and an explicit
  set_default_executor (to_thread is capped at min(32, cpu_count+4) = 6 threads on a
  2-core box, shared by 33+ call sites that are disk-blocked, not CPU-blocked).
  Files: QapBot.py, qapbot/docs/PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md. 2971 tests pass.

2026-09-03 (3)
- Fixed: CoC API throughput silently capped at ~35 req/s against a configured 100, which
  is why entry (2)'s concurrency raise produced no speedup (QapBot.py).
  Root cause: coc.py 4.0.0's BatchThrottler measures its sliding rate window with
  time.process_time() -- CPU seconds burned by this process, not elapsed time (coc/http.py).
  For an I/O-bound bot the CPU clock advances far slower than the wall clock, so
  throttle_limit=100 actually meant "100 requests per second of CPU consumed". Measured on
  a pure-I/O workload at rate_limit=100: upstream gave 2.6 req/s at 20 concurrent and
  5.5 at 50, against an ideal 100. In the live bot (which does burn CPU on JSON/DB work)
  it landed at ~35 req/s. That also explains entry (2): raising _FETCH_CONCURRENCY 20 -> 50
  left throughput unchanged (25.6 -> 23.4 clans/s measured from PROD log timestamps) while
  per-clan latency rose 0.78s -> 2.14s -- every request was queueing on the throttler, not
  the semaphore. Verified the semaphore itself was working (51/71/61 clans admitted in the
  first 0.5s at cc=50 vs 20/21/31 at cc=20).
  Fix: WallClockBatchThrottler, a BatchThrottler subclass using time.monotonic() for the
  window, and throttle_limit 100 -> 80. 80 rather than the full 10 keys x 10 req/sec
  because that ceiling is shared with /status, leaderboards and CWL discovery, and
  exceeding the real CoC limit blocks requests for 30-60s; 20% margin absorbs those bursts.
  Measured after the fix: 78.4 req/s at 20 concurrent, 87.2 at 50 (target 80).
  _FETCH_CONCURRENCY stays at 50 -- it only becomes useful now that the gate behind it is
  real. Revisit on the next coc.py bump in case upstream fixes the clock.
  Expected: Phase 1 ~97s -> ~40s, cycle ~130s -> ~70s. Watch the api_fail: buckets
  (Network / RateLimit) in [CYCLE-SUMMARY]; revert throttle_limit toward 60 if they move.
  File: QapBot.py. 2971 tests pass.

2026-09-03 (2)
- Changed: Phase-1 fetch concurrency 20 -> 50 (QapBot.py).
  With the orphaned-CWL battle-day gate in place (entry 1), Phase 1 became the dominant
  cost of the update cycle: 97s of a 131.8s cycle (74%) for 2,877 clans. Measured on the
  post-fix PROD cycles that is ~30 clans/s (~0.67s per call) and 3,736 CoC API calls in
  97s = ~38 req/s -- against a configured ceiling of throttle_limit=100 (key_count=10 x
  10 req/sec per key, QapBot.py startup_login). So the semaphore, not the throttler, was
  the binding constraint, and ~60% of the provisioned API budget sat unused. At 50 the
  expected steady state is ~76 clans/s = ~100 req/s, i.e. saturating the BatchThrottler
  rather than exceeding it -- the throttler still enforces the real ceiling, so this
  cannot overshoot into 429s. Zero HTTP 429s were observed across a full CWL day at 20
  (the "429" strings in the log are millisecond timestamps, not status codes).
  Expected: Phase 1 ~97s -> ~40s, cycle ~132s -> ~75-85s. Revert to 20 if SSL /
  connection-pressure errors show up in the api_fail: buckets.
  File: QapBot.py. 2971 tests pass.

2026-09-03 (1)
- Fixed: CWL update cycles degrading from ~40s to 250-526s over 41h, with the orphan pass
  reporting 0/2,156 successful for 24 hours straight (QBhelperfunctions.py).
  Root cause: `_scan_orphans()` flagged EVERY non-newest 4-part CWL temp file of a
  multi-file clan as an orphan with no state and no time check -- the function's own
  docstring described a `state != war_ended` condition that was only ever implemented in
  the single-file branch. CWL rounds overlap, so round N+1's preparation file is written
  while round N is still inside its 24h battle day; that demotes round N to "not newest"
  hours before its war can possibly end. Measured on PROD: 1,719 of 2,063 non-newest
  entries (83%) were wars still being fought. Each cost one get_league_war(), one
  get_league_group() (their war_tag is never in cwl_league_rounds -- verified 0/400), and
  a full save_war_object() JSON rewrite per cycle, then returned "still inWar, deferring"
  -- every cycle for up to 24h until the war actually ended. That waste is also what drove
  Phase-1 to 2,457 clans (stuck in_war metadata makes a clan war-critical, which is exempt
  from BOTH the re-check jitter and _MAX_INACTIVE_PER_CYCLE) and RSS to 8.8 GB.
  Fix: new `_orphan_ready()` applies the same gate the single-file branch already used, in
  two tiers -- filename timestamp (zero I/O, catches ~89%) then recorded end_time + 1h, so
  maintenance-extended wars are still handled correctly. Deliberately does not consult
  CACHE.temp_war_metadata: it is keyed by clan tag and holds only the newest war, so for an
  older round it describes a different war. Unreadable file / unparseable end_time keeps
  the old behaviour (treat as orphan) so nothing is stranded in temp/.
  Verified against the live temp/ tree: orphan pool 2,063 -> 224 per cycle (-89%).
  Files: QBhelperfunctions.py, qapbot/docs/WAR_FILE_MANAGEMENT_RULES.md,
  tests/unit/test_orphaned_cwl_battle_day_gate.py (new, 4 cases). 2971 tests pass.

2026-09-01 (7)
- Fixed: the nightly VACUUM trigger would have fired every single night once the rolling
  migration started deleting daily. Caught on the DEV verification run before it reached PROD.
  The trigger was a flat `freelist_count > 500` pages (8 MB at a 16 KB page size), which was
  right while the migration deleted a month of rows once a month -- the free list sat near zero
  the rest of the time. The rolling migration frees ~1.1 GB of pages EVERY night, so an 8 MB
  trigger fires unconditionally: ~7.5 min of EXCLUSIVE lock and hard db_maintenance_mode Discord
  block per night (measured 452s on PROD 2026-09-01), plus VACUUM INTO rewriting the whole
  24-40 GB file to a new one on NAS-attached SSD. A small nightly re-run of the exact outage
  class today's redesign exists to remove.
  It would also reclaim nothing: in steady state the migration deletes ~1.2M rows/day and the
  update cycle inserts ~1.2M rows/day, and SQLite reuses free-list pages for new inserts, so the
  file does not grow. The free list is churn, not waste.
- Added: CONFIG.vacuum_freelist_fraction (0.15, env VACUUM_FREELIST_FRACTION) and
  CONFIG.vacuum_min_freelist_pages (500, env VACUUM_MIN_FREELIST_PAGES) as an absolute floor for
  small/fresh DBs. Trigger is now
  `freelist > max(min_pages, page_count * fraction)`. On the real 24.0 GB PROD copy that is a
  3.61 GB threshold against 1.64 GB of actual free list, so VACUUM correctly does not fire where
  the flat rule would have. VACUUM_FREELIST_FRACTION=0 restores the old behaviour.
- Added: a skipped VACUUM now logs why at INFO with actual vs threshold sizes -- a VACUUM that
  silently stops happening is exactly the failure mode a proportional threshold introduces.
- Added: tests/unit/test_vacuum_freelist_threshold.py pins BOTH failure directions (too low ->
  nightly VACUUM; too high -> never compacts), plus a structural check that the production
  expression still matches the one the tests restate. Verified it fails at 0.001 and at 0.5.
- DEV verification of the migration itself (HISTORY_RETENTION_DAYS=45, 17 days of work):
  1,766,946 rows at 2,750-5,074 rows/s with per-day ETA logging. Interrupted with Ctrl+C
  mid-day-17, which tested resume for free -- 400,000 rows of that day in history, 179,465 still
  in hot, 0 duplicated in both, 0 left behind from the 16 completed days, and the marker
  correctly still at 2026-07-17 rather than advanced past an incomplete day.
- Note: the update cycles seen running during the DEV migration were a DEV artefact --
  NO_DEV_MODE_UPDATES=true takes a branch that `continue`s before the db_maintenance_idle_event
  gate. On PROD that gate holds the next cycle until the nightly routine finishes, as intended.
- Files: qapbot/config.py, qapbot/db_manager.py, README.md, .env.example,
  qapbot/docs/DATABASE_ARCHITECTURE.md (new entry 2026-09-01 (e)),
  tests/unit/test_vacuum_freelist_threshold.py. 2967 tests pass.

2026-09-01 (6)
- Removed: CONFIG.history_migration_enabled and the HISTORY_MIGRATION_ENABLED env var.
  It was this morning's stopgap, back when the migration was a multi-hour blocking campaign
  that had to be stoppable immediately. After the redesign it guards nothing -- the walk is
  non-blocking, budgeted, resumable, ~1.2M rows/night -- and its "off" position silently
  stops hot-DB retention with nothing to alarm on, which makes it a hazard rather than a
  safety net. HISTORY_MIGRATION_NIGHTLY_ROW_BUDGET=0 already is an equivalent no-op (the
  budget check is `rows_moved >= row_budget`, so zero breaks on the first iteration).

  and run_nightly_maintenance_routine()'s migration_time_budget_seconds override. /admin
  "Execute Nightly Maintenance" now runs the identical routine to the scheduled 03:00 UTC
  task -- same due-check, same budgets, same steps. The short admin budget existed because
  migration used to be a long campaign an interactive command should only nibble at; with a
  small nightly job it only made the two callers diverge. The ~15 min interaction-token risk
  it hedged is unchanged and still handled by the caller catching a failed followup and

  one that the migration step gets the CONFIG budgets, and a structural one asserting the

  parameter is how the two paths drifted apart the first time.
- Removed: dead `global _capital_districts_fixups` in apply_coc_library_patches() (the outer
  function never assigns it -- only the closure does, which has its own declaration).

  blocking-era value), HISTORY_MIGRATION_CYCLE_CHUNK_MINUTES (nothing reads it) and
  HISTORY_MIGRATION_ADMIN_BUDGET_MINUTES (removed here).

  so it cannot mislead code -- only a human reading the table. Clear it with

  * QapBot.is_history_migration_due() reached into two protected WarHistoryDB methods
    (_history_cutoff, _oldest_migratable_date). Fixed by layering, not suppression: the

  0 pyright errors under the project's strict config.
- Changed: history_retention_days 60 -> 75. Operator caught a real scheduling flaw: a row
  dated D migrates N days later, so N decides WHICH days of the month carry the heavy
  migration. CWL runs days 1-10 at ~2x normal volume, and at N=60 every CWL-data migration
  night landed inside a CWL season (227 of 235 over two years) -- the two heaviest jobs
  stacked on the same nights.
  Shortening to 50 (the proposal) would have been much worse, not better: below 61 the
  calendar floor binds, so the cutoff freezes for ~1/3 of all days and then jumps up to 12
  days at once -- landing on the 1st of the month, i.e. a ~24M-row night during CWL. That is
  exactly the cliff this redesign removed.
  71..78 is the only band that is both smooth (floor never binds, 1 day/night, 0 frozen days)
  and CWL-clean (0 CWL-data migration days inside a CWL window). 75 sits at its centre with
  4 days of margin either side; CWL data from month M then migrates around days 15-24 of
  month M+2. Cost: hot settles at ~92M rows / ~40 GB instead of ~74M / ~34 GB.
- Added: tests/unit/test_history_retention_cutoff.py now guards both properties against
  whatever the configured value actually is, and separately pins that 50 and 60 still
  reproduce their respective failures -- so a future "optimise it for disk" edit fails the
  build with the reason. Verified the guard fails at 50 and 60, passes at 75.

2026-09-01 (4)
- Changed: hot->history migration redesigned end to end (all six fixes from the 2026-09-01
  incident, in one pass). Plan of record: plans/implemented/history-migration-redesign.md; full writeup
  in qapbot/docs/DATABASE_ARCHITECTURE.md entry "2026-09-01 (b)".
- Fixed: the migration no longer blocks Discord interactions. New QBcore.db_migration_active
  (advisory) replaces db_maintenance_mode for the batched walk, which holds no exclusive lock
  -- short transactions on the async writer while user commands read through the separate
  sync pool in WAL mode, where readers never block on a writer. It only ever set the hard
  flag because it was copied from nightly_db_maintenance(), which genuinely needs it. That
  copy-paste cost 9.6h of refused commands on 2026-09-01 for a run that never needed to
  refuse one.
- Changed: retention is now rolling, not monthly. _history_cutoff() returns
  min(today - HISTORY_RETENTION_DAYS, first of previous month), default 60 days. The floor is
  load-bearing: the "current + previous calendar month" contract can require retaining a
  61-day-old row (day 31 of a 31-day month after a 31-day month), so plain `today - 60` would
  break it on 8 dates every 4 years. With the floor it cannot, for any retention value.
- Changed: run_history_migration() replaces monthly_history_migration(). Walks one calendar
  day at a time toward the target, persisting the reached cutoff after each COMPLETED day, so
  it resumes at day granularity with no rescan. Bounded by a row budget (primary, default 3M
  -- sized for a full CWL day) and a time budget (secondary, 90 -> 30 min). Bounded by rows
  rather than days because daily volume ranged from 37 to 2,191,245 rows/day on the real DB.
  Empty days are skipped via an indexed MIN() probe, so one stray ancient row cannot make
  every run crawl day by day from it to today.
- Removed: opportunistic per-cycle migration chunking and HISTORY_MIGRATION_CYCLE_CHUNK_MINUTES.
  Deleted outright rather than resized -- at ~1.2M rows/night there is nothing for it to do.
- Removed: is_monthly_migration_due()'s two modes, day==1 gate and in-process claim, all of
  which existed only to stop a monthly job re-firing. Replaced by is_history_migration_due()
  (reached_cutoff < target_cutoff), still the single enforcement point for
  HISTORY_MIGRATION_ENABLED.
- Added: idx_wa_date / idx_ws_date on `main` only (the migration never selects history by
  date, and building it there would overrun initialize_database()'s 1800s watchdog). Built
  inline at startup per the 2026-07-30 "Startup Ordering Fix (Final)" pattern -- safe because
  nothing else can write to the DB at that point. One-time ~5-15 min first build.
- Fixed: _migrate_date_window_batched() replaces _migrate_table_batch_by_date() -- date-window
  + keyset id bound instead of `id IN (5000 params)`. Removes 5000 rowid seeks per statement
  and the 32766-parameter ceiling that forced batch_size=5000 (now 20000, chosen by
  transaction duration). _explicit_column_list() hoisted out of the batch loop (~4,800
  needless PRAGMA calls on 2026-09-01). Progress logging now reports rows/sec and ETA.
- Fixed: the guards logged NOTHING when refusing a user -- a 14-hour outage produced zero
  [MAINTENANCE-GUARD] lines in a 596k-line log and surfaced only as complaints the next day.
  Both guards now log rate-limited at INFO (first refusal per episode, then every 25th).
- Fixed: fast_bulk_history_migration() rebuilt its indexes with wal_autocheckpoint=0 still in
  effect (restored only afterwards), so the largest write burst of the run -- ~28 GB across 10
  CREATE INDEX statements -- accumulated entirely in the WAL. Same shape as the 2026-08-01
  disk-full incident. The restore now happens before the rebuild.
- Note: there is no backlog to clear. Rows below a 60-day cutoff on the 2026-09-01 snapshot
  were 30 (war_attacks) and 0 for the other three tables -- the 2026-09-01 run was chasing the
  calendar-month cutoff, which on the 1st sheds everything older than ~31 days. Hot now settles
  at ~75M rows / ~35 GB (the peak the calendar rule already hit at month end) instead of
  sawtoothing to ~37M on the 1st.
- Verified against real PROD rows before shipping (40k war_attacks + 40k war_summary copied
  from the 2026-09-01 snapshot into a throwaway DB): query plan uses idx_wa_date as a COVERING
  INDEX (was SCAN war_attacks); a mid-day budget stop commits rows but correctly leaves the date
  marker unset; a whole-day budget stop advances it; the resumed run lands exactly on the target
  cutoff; rows below the cutoff all moved, rows at/above it all stayed, none lost or duplicated;
  column alignment intact; re-run is a no-op.
- Also: fast_bulk_history_migration() now stamps the new cutoff marker instead of the dead
  last_history_migration timestamp, and CACHE.last_history_migration (now unread) was removed.

- Fixed: `KeyError: 'districts'` failing every fetch of 438 clans since 2026-08-31 15:40.
  coc.py 4.0.0's `Clan._from_data` guards on `clanCapital` being truthy but then indexes

  at all. PROD 2026-09-01: 42,871 failed get_clan() calls, each retried 3x with 1s+2s backoff

  New idempotent `apply_coc_library_patches()` in coc_health.py, called from `startup_login()`,
  normalises the payload to `districts: []` before coc.py parses it -- lossless here, since
  Clan Capital data is not stored in any QapBot table. Fixup count exposed via
  `get_coc_stats()["capital_districts_fixups"]`; only the first occurrence is logged.

  library could not parse this response", so retrying reproduces the identical error). Makes

- Added: CWL retention purge -- guild_config.cwl_retention_months finally has a consumer. The
  column, its settings UI and its readout on the CWL Settings screen all shipped long ago, but
  nothing ever acted on them, so the setting was inert while telling admins their old seasons were
  being purged. New WarHistoryDB.purge_expired_cwl_events(), run as Step 0.6 of QapBot.py's nightly
  maintenance (before VACUUM, so freed pages are reclaimed in the same pass; wrapped so a purge
  failure can't cost the checkpoint/VACUUM/ANALYZE). 0 = keep indefinitely, the default, purges
  nothing.
- Scoped by SEASON AGE, not event status: there is no 'completed' status in this lifecycle
  (draft -> signup_open -> announced -> war, plus cancelled) -- a finished season just stays in
  'war' forever, so status can't identify what's over. cwl_season ('YYYY-MM', zero-padded, so
  lexical order is chronological) can.
- The two cross-guild tables (cwl_locked_clan_members, cwl_player_season_status) are season-keyed
  with no FK to cwl_events, so CASCADE never reaches them and purging them per-guild would destroy
  data another guild still retains. They are swept referentially instead: a season's rows go only
  once no cwl_events row anywhere references that season.
- Changed: the retention readout said "Completed/cancelled events are purged after" -- inaccurate
  on both counts (no 'completed' status exists, and drafts are purged too). Now reads "Past seasons

2026-08-30 (3)
- Fixed tracker #0078 ("Ausstehend Zahl oder symbol stimmt nicht"): the season overview's
  "Ausstehend" line said 2 while the Teams-verwalten board showed a single yellow question mark.
  The board draws its icons in a strict precedence -- Not Linked, then a real status, then
  "Not Invited Yet" -- and hasVisibleRealStatus() only treats a 'pending' row as a real status
  once its DM has actually gone out. A linked, pending, never-DMed player therefore renders as
  "Not Invited Yet" while the counter still called them pending.
  split_cwl_pending_signups_by_link_sync() now requires dm_sent for its linked half, so that line
  is exactly the number of question-mark icons on the board. Those players are not lost from the
  overview -- they are precisely who the "New players without DM invitation" line reports.
- Fixed tracker #0079 ("Zahl stimmt nicht ueberein"): "New players without DM invitation" said 1,
  but pressing "Notify New Pool Members" listed 2 that could not be contacted. The count and the
  action had genuinely drifted: tracker #0075 added a settled-status exclusion (confirmed /
  declined / auto_confirmed) to the COUNT only, while the action kept handing the raw pool to
  _send_cwl_enrollment_dm_batch, whose own dedup checks nothing but global dm_sent. So a pooled
  player with dm_sent=False and a settled local status was invisible to the number and still got
  DMed -- and, being settled, was someone who had already answered and should not have been
  re-invited at all.
  Extracted resolve_cwl_pool_tags_missing_dm_sync(), which returns the SET rather than a count;
  the overview line, the button's visibility and the button's send list are now the same set by
  construction rather than by intention. The narrowing deliberately lives in
  notify_new_cwl_pool_members rather than in the shared batch helper, because Start Enrollment
  shares that helper and must still contact an auto_confirmed member to tell them a standing
  preference enrolled them.
  Note for the record: notify_new_cwl_pool_members' docstring had claimed the two could not drift
  apart. That was true when written and quietly stopped being true when #0075 landed -- shared
  resolution beats shared intent.
  Files: qapbot/QBdiscocmdshelper_cwl.py, qapbot/web_bridge.py. Tests: 2 new regression tests
  (the exact reported shape of each ticket) plus one existing test updated for the tightened
  pending rule. 2888 tests pass.

2026-08-30 (1)
- Added: the CWL four-phase model -- Setup / Enrollment / Preparation / War -- with a step
  indicator at the top of the CWL Management message (done / current / upcoming, as
  checkmark / blue-dot-bold / hollow-circle). Phase is derived in exactly one place, so the
  indicator, the buttons and the freeze guards can never disagree. The War step carries its clan
  count ("War (2/8 started)") because a guild reaches War the moment its FIRST clan starts while
  the rest are still moving players.
- Renamed: "Start CWL" -> "Announce Rosters" (and "Send Roster Updates" once changes are pending).
  The real CWL start is a manual in-game action only a clan lead can take; a bot button must not
  claim to do it. start_cwl() became announce_cwl_rosters() rather than being left as a name that
  lies about what it does.
- Added: automatic War-phase transition. When the update cycle sees a participating clan's CWL
  actually started in-game, it snapshots that clan's real locked roster (via the league group,
  falling back to live membership), drops anyone who never transferred in back to the unassigned
  pool with a one-off explanatory DM, and moves the event to the new 'war' status.
- Added: per-clan roster freeze. A clan that has started can no longer be removed from the season,
  its settings are forced back to stored values, and no player can be dragged into or out of its
  column -- with the one exception the spec requires: anyone who WAS in the clan when it locked
  stays eligible and can still be placed there. Enforced server-side in the single assignment
  write path, with the board rendering a lock badge and non-draggable cards to match. Season
  deletion is blocked entirely once any clan has started.
- Added: batched roster-update DMs. Changing the board after players were told where they play no
  longer risks a DM per drag: "pending" is a comparison against what was last SENT, so a player
  dragged A->B->A cancels out and owes nobody a message. Flushed through three triggers sharing one
  implementation -- a button beside Close on the board, a DM to the admin who closes the board with
  changes outstanding, and a highlighted button on the Hub message.
- Added: removing a clan mid-season tells its already-announced players; adding one late sends
  never-contacted players ONE combined DM carrying both the assignment details and the
  confirm/opt-out buttons, instead of an enrollment DM followed by an assignment DM.
- Added: "Announce Rosters" now warns, in its confirmation dialog, which participating clans are
  still short of their configured roster size, and asks whether to proceed anyway.
- Added: 30 minutes before a clan's announced start, its CWL Coordinators get a status report --
  roster full or short, and who still hasn't joined. Coordinators also gained Teams Management
  access for clans participating in the current season.
- Changed: the T-2h coordinator escalation added yesterday was REMOVED in favour of the above. It
  fired 90 minutes earlier and said nearly the same thing; two near-identical leadership DMs is the
  same avalanche problem this feature avoids everywhere else. Players keep both of their own
  escalating alarms, so no lead time is lost.
- Fixed (real latent bug, found while building): set_cwl_event_clans_sync is a DELETE + INSERT that
  never carried locked_at (or created_at) forward, so every ordinary save of the clan-config screen
  would have silently un-frozen every locked clan and bounced the guild out of War phase. Fixed in
  the DB method rather than at the call sites -- its contract is "replace the configuration", not
  "reset facts the configuration does not own".
- Fixed: the "Still Missing" leadership section was gated on status == 'announced', so it vanished
  the instant war started -- exactly when leadership needs it, since the remaining clans are still
  waiting on transfers. Same trap the monitoring sweep's own status query had.
- Note on the spec: an ephemeral message when the Activity is closed is NOT possible (an ephemeral
  needs a live interaction token; discordSdk.close() is a client-side call with none behind it, and
  the original LAUNCH_ACTIVITY already consumed its one response slot). Delivered as a DM with the
  same button instead, via the existing /api/cwl/activity-closed hook.

2026-08-29 (31)
- Added: "Start CWL" (CWL_ROSTER_PLANNING_PLAN.md Phase 5) -- a new CWL Management button that
  announces the finished roster to every assigned player by DM. Each player's message is tailored
  to the same green/amber split the Manage Teams board shows: someone already in their assigned
  clan is told their CWL start time and to stay put; someone still elsewhere is told which clan to
  move to, that they must do it well before the start time, and gets a direct clashofclans.com
  join link for that exact clan. One grouped DM per Discord user (never one per account), so a
  main and an alt in two different clans with two different start times arrive as one coherent
  message. A player with no current clan on record deliberately gets the amber variant, since the
  green text would assert something the bot can't back up.
  Recipients are the union of cwl_assignments and a shared clan's cwl_shared_clan_players
  (assigned=1), restricted to currently-participating clans; a shared clan is announced ONLY by its
  owner guild, so two attached guilds can't both DM the same player about the same clan. Discord
  ownership is resolved live (get_player_links_sync), never from the enrollment-time snapshot
  (Pitfall 37). Refuses outright, naming the clans, if any participating clan still has no start
  time -- the surviving half of the never-built Phase 4 "Finalize" gate. Marks each announced
  placement notified, which makes the whole action re-runnable for late arrivals and makes the
  button self-managing: it disappears once everyone's been told and comes back on its own when a
  lead drags a new player onto the board. Transitions the event signup_open -> announced, the first
  and only writer of 'announced' in the codebase.
- Added: CWL switch verification + escalating alarms (Phase 6). A once-per-cycle sweep detects who
  has actually moved into their assigned clan, DMs escalating reminders to those who haven't (24h
  then 2h before that player's OWN clan's start time), and escalates at the urgent stage to that
  clan's standing CWL Coordinators (tracker #0046). A new "Still Missing" section in the CWL
  Management embed shows leadership the same list passively, in both entry points via the shared
  content layer. Monitoring stops per clan the moment its CWL roster locks -- detected from a real
  is_cwl war row, falling back to a cwl_league_groups row for private-warlog clans -- since nagging
  someone about a roster they can no longer join is actively wrong.
  Costs ZERO CoC API calls: "has this player moved?" is answered from user_players.current_clan_tag,
  which every regular clan poll already refreshes and which is the same signal the board's card
  colors use. The original plan's "force every participating clan into the every-cycle fetch bucket"
  was deliberately NOT built -- it would have re-created exactly the per-cycle load pattern trackers
  #0009 (the 6 GB RSS plateau) and #0017 (redundant mid-month CWL fetches) were fixed by removing,
  and buys nothing over a ~30 min staleness across a multi-DAY monitoring window.
- Fixed (found by test, not live): CACHE.get_clan_name() returns the literal "Unknown" for a clan
  that isn't in the name cache, so the missing-start-time error named "Unknown" instead of the clan
  an admin has to go fix. Every new call site now passes the tag as the default, matching this
  file's own existing convention.
- Schema: cwl_shared_clan_players gains notified/switched_at/alarm_stage_sent (the shared-clan
  counterparts of the identically named cwl_assignments columns, which existed since 2026-08-09 and
  had never been read or written until now). Each gets its OWN single-purpose writer whose UPDATE
  mentions no other column -- that table already learned the hard way (Pitfall 25, status vs
  assigned) that two independent facts sharing a write path is how one silently destroys the other.
  Auto-migrates on restart via _add_column_if_missing; verified against a simulated pre-existing
  database (columns added, existing rows untouched, second restart a clean no-op).
- Docs: CWL_ROSTER_PLANNING_PLAN.md substantially rewritten. Added a status-audit table at the top
