2026-08-29 (28)
- Fixed: live bug report (round 2) on the CWL Coordinators picker -- the round-1 re-entrancy fix
  (entry 27/26) replaced a missing guard with a busy-bool that silently DROPPED any selection
  change arriving while another was mid-flight. Live testing showed the cost of that: picking 3
  coordinators in quick succession got "Save successful", but only the first selection actually
  persisted -- later change events were dropped entirely, so CWL_COORDINATOR_LIMIT's own
  server-side clamp never even ran against the real final selection, and the picker kept showing
  Discord's own (never-corrected) 3-chip client state. Replaced the busy-bool with an
  asyncio.Lock: every handler now waits its turn instead of bailing out, so no selection-change
  event is ever lost and Save always reads state only after every earlier-queued mutation has
  actually applied. Also added a defense-in-depth clamp directly inside _on_save with an explicit
  "only the first {limit} were actually saved" warning message, in case this invariant is ever
  violated by some path not yet understood -- never silently truncate without saying so.
  Files: qapbot/ui_cwl_roster.py, qapbot/translations/{en,de}.json. Tests: tests/discord/
  test_ui_cwl_roster.py (1 rewritten, 2 new). 2822 tests pass (one pre-existing, unrelated
  order-dependent flake in test_cwl_clan_ownership.py, passes standalone).

- Fixed/Changed: CWL Coordinators live bug reports. A follow-up test showed removing a
  coordinator via the picker's own chip "x" then immediately clicking Save could persist the
  PRE-removal selection -- CwlCoordinatorConfigurationView had zero re-entrancy guards on any
  handler (Pitfall 49's class of bug: a fast second click starting while a still-in-flight first

  a persistence bug: clicking 'Save Configuration' while the coordinator dropdown is still open

  can override) -- the click never reaches the button, so nothing saves, easily mistaken for "it

- Fixed: tracker #0070 follow-up, the earlier fix only closed the /clan management -> anchored
  Hub message direction -- live testing showed the reverse (a change made through the anchored
  Hub message itself) still left an already-open /clan management CWL Settings session stale.
  Root cause: unlike the anchored Hub message (a stable, persisted channel_id/message_id this bot
  can always locate), a /clan management session is a plain ephemeral message with no persistent
  identity anywhere once its own interaction is gone -- there was nothing to push a refresh to.
  Fixed with a new lightweight in-memory registry (CACHE.cwl_settings_open_view, one slot per
  guild) tracking the most recently opened/refreshed session; all four CWL Settings mutation
  handlers (CWL Management Hub toggle, Player CWL Settings Hub toggle, Include All Linked
  Accounts toggle, Data Retention modal) now push a refresh to it, not just the anchored message.
  Single slot per guild is a deliberate simplification -- two admins with it open concurrently
  means only the more-recently-opened one gets the live push, the other still has its manual
  Refresh button. See Pitfall 50's follow-up section, qapbot/docs/COPILOT_PITFALLS_COOKBOOK.md,
  for the full writeup including why the first fix addressed the wrong direction.

2026-08-29 (11)
- Fixed: tracker #0056, corrected diagnosis. The earlier "probably already fixed by #45"
  conclusion (entry (8) below) turned out wrong once the reporter clarified the crash happened
  testing tracker #45's OWN just-deployed pagination, not before it -- ruling that theory out.
  Real root cause: #45 added several new AccountManagementView handlers (page-turn, select,
  verify, set-primary, unlink, unlink-all, and especially Refresh -- a real CoC API fetch across
  every linked account before its own edit, by far the widest window) that all edit the same
  ephemeral message with ZERO re-entrancy guard between them. A rapid second click -- exactly
  what a user exploring a brand-new 3-page UI (their ~60 accounts) would do -- could race two
  edit_message() calls against each other, badly enough to crash the reporter's Discord client
  ("Cannot read property 'label' of undefined"), not just double-write data the way this same
  bug class usually manifests. Fixed with a per-instance _busy flag + _guard_reentrant() helper
  guarding every state-mutating handler, checked before any await.

  show a stale value (#0058) or nothing at all (#0059) despite the player having a current
  standing preference. Root cause: cwl_signups.preferred_league_rank -- despite tracker #0057's

- Fixed: tracker #0066, two bugs in the CWL Management Hub / Player CWL Hub workflow.
  (1) The Hub toggle buttons' repost was fire-and-forget (QBcore.spawn_tracked) immediately
  followed by a foreground refresh of the SAME anchored message -- an intermittent race where

  in its pre-click state until a manual Refresh. Fixed by awaiting the repost before refreshing,
  plus a per-guild re-entrancy guard (module-level set, checked before any await) against a

  new". This gap predates today's #0061 fix (confirmed via git blame -- introduced when the CWL
  hub channel slots were added, the apply-trigger was never generalized past registration).
  Fixed by triggering the correct repost for every channel slot actually touched this apply, not

2026-08-29 (4)
- Fixed: tracker #0061 -- toggling ONE guild's CWL Management Hub, Player CWL Hub, or
  registration message setting (or changing its channel, or changing the guild's language) was
  deleting and reposting the SAME anchored message in every OTHER guild that had it enabled too,
  not just the guild whose setting actually changed. Root cause: all four settings-change
  handlers call the shared repost_anchored_message() driver (QapBot.py), which unconditionally
  sweeps every guild in CACHE.server_config -- correct for the periodic/startup maintenance
  sweep it was designed for, but wrong for a single-guild UI action, since only_if_not_bottom=
  False there meant every enabled guild's message got deleted and reposted immediately with a
  new message ID.
  Fix: repost_anchored_message() and its three wrappers (repost_playerregistration_messages(),
  repost_cwl_management_messages(), repost_cwl_player_hub_messages()) gained an optional
  guild_id parameter that, when given, restricts processing to that one guild. The five
  single-guild call sites (ui_cwl_roster.py's two hub toggles; ui_clan_management.py's
  registration toggle, channel-config apply, and language-change handler) now pass guild_id=...;
  every periodic/startup caller (main()'s bump cycle, on_ready()) omits it and keeps sweeping
  the whole fleet as before.
  Files: QapBot.py, qapbot/ui_cwl_roster.py, qapbot/ui_clan_management.py.
  2734 tests pass (2 new in tests/unit/test_repost_cwl_player_hub_messages.py: guild_id scopes
  to one guild, omitting guild_id still sweeps every guild).

2026-08-29 (1)
- Fixed: tracker #0009, memory consumption -- PROD sat at a ~6.1 GB plateau (peaks 7.1 GB) that
  was NOT a leak: daily averages after the first day were flat (6142/6082/6254 MB). Measured
  against the real PROD data on DEV, live cache content is only ~1.9 GB (temp_war_objects
  1195 MB, temp_war_stats 449 MB, clan_name_cache 263 MB); the rest was burst-driven.
  Root cause: INACTIVE_CLAN_UPDATE_INTERVAL_HOURS=22 is self-clumping, so clans polled together
  came due together forever -- 3000-4200-clan waves recurring at exactly 22h, drifting 2h
  earlier daily. Every clan polled in a cycle is held simultaneously (its coc.ClanWar in
  fetch_results pinning ~120-170 KB of raw API payload, its coc.Clan in coc_clan_cache at
  ~69-90 KB), so a wave cost +541 to +700 MB of RSS in ONE cycle while quiet cycles gave back
  only 10-40 MB -- each wave ratcheted the floor up.
  Four changes: (1) new compute_recheck_offset_seconds() adds a stable crc32-derived 0-2h phase
  offset per clan so waves disperse and stay dispersed (war-critical prep/in_war clans exempt --
  their backdated poll must land 8min before war end); (2) _MAX_INACTIVE_PER_CYCLE 5000 -> 1500
  (clips only the top ~8% of cycles; mean demand is 817/cycle); (3) coc_clan_cache gained a
  1500-entry FIFO size cap -- it was TTL-only and hit 5007 entries (~375 MB) inside one cycle;
  (4) Phase 3 now clears each fetch_results slot as it consumes it instead of holding the whole
  cycle's wars until after leaderboards/notifications.
  Files: QapBot.py, qapbot/coc_cache.py. 2729 tests pass.
- Fixed: tracker #0009, three bugs in the Memory Profile report itself that made the previous
  two investigations chase the wrong caches. (a) _estimate_dict_size_mb() reset its id()-based
  `seen` per sampled entry, charging shared dict KEYS to every entry -- clan_name_cache reported
  462 MB against a true 263 MB; now one `seen` per sample (reports 249 MB). (b)
  get_memory_usage_mb() recursed via hasattr(value, "__dict__"), but every coc.py model class is
  __slots__-based and has NO __dict__, so the walk returned a bare 360 bytes for a whole
  50-member clan (report showed ~0.1 MB for the entire cache); now walks gc.get_referents(),
  which also catches the raw API payload pinned by coc.py's un-exhausted _iter_members generator
  -- validated against tracemalloc at 73.4 KB/entry vs 67.2 KB actual. Note the earlier
  2026-08-22 "deepened it to walk League/Icon/Badge" fix never executed a single recursion.
  (c) [GC OBJECT COUNTS] is blind to the frozen permanent generation (gc.freeze() removes
  objects from gc.get_objects() entirely) -- it now reports gc.get_freeze_count() alongside,
  rather than silently omitting the ~1.9M objects nightly maintenance freezes.
  Files: qapbot/QBdiscocmdshelper_admin_command.py, qapbot/coc_cache.py. 2729 tests pass.
- Docs: new Pitfall 44 (deep-size estimators vs __slots__ and lazily-parsed library objects) in
  COPILOT_PITFALLS_COOKBOOK.md + short entry 33 in copilot-instructions.md;
  CLAN_AND_WAR_CYCLE_ARCHITECTURE.md gained the re-check-wave/jitter section, the coc_clan_cache
  size cap and its measured per-entry cost, and the Phase-1 gather retention note. Analysis
  write-up in plans/tracker-0009-memory-analysis.md.

- Fixed: positional DB row access (Cardinal Rule 14) in
  get_cwl_player_season_status_dm_refs_for_event_sync() and in get_guild_config()'s
  guild_clan_roles load -- both now read by column name. Neither was producing wrong results
  today: with an explicit SELECT list row[N] indexes the projection, not physical storage, so a
  migration reorder cannot break it (verified by reverting and watching a reorder test still
  pass). The real exposure is edit time -- adding or reordering one column in that SELECT shifts
  every index onto the wrong same-typed id, silently, and the only consumer feeds those values
  to bot.fetch_user()/channel.fetch_message() to DELETE a Discord message. Since the code is
  correct until such an edit, the regression guard is structural rather than behavioural.
  Rule 14 in .github/copilot-instructions.md gained a note on this distinction, since its stated
  WHY only covers the SELECT * case. Files: qapbot/db_manager.py,

2026-08-22 (27)
- Fixed: CWL league groups are now marked cwl_ended=1 by a periodic sweep, ending the redundant
  mid-month get_league_war() re-walks of finished groups (ticket #0017, option A). The flag
  previously had exactly one writer (update_cwl_group_stats, reached only from /cwlinfo or a
  cwlgroup subscription) and no periodic pass, so 8 of 25049 August groups were marked while
  136707 polled clans kept re-downloading long-finished wars. New sweep_cwl_ended_flags() runs
  5 sequential asyncio.to_thread batches of 500 groups per update cycle and marks a group on
  EITHER "every clan played all rounds" OR "the season window is definitively over"
  (cwl_season_window_closed, start + 14 days). The time-based condition is load-bearing: measured
  on real data only ~55% of groups can ever satisfy the completeness test, since the rest contain
  clans whose wars are never fetched. It does NOT freeze standings -- the sweep writes the flag
  only, and update_cwl_group_stats's freeze needs cwl_ended AND non-null stats, so a swept group
  still recomputes live. Keyset cursor ordered to match idx_cwl_league_groups_id (35x faster than
  the natural ordering: 0.036s vs 1.28s per 5 pages) and rotates, since ~45% of groups can never
  complete and would otherwise be re-checked forever. get_cwl_group_war_stats collapsed from two
  queries to one. Files: QBhelperfunctions.py, qapbot/db_manager.py, qapbot/constants.py,
  QapBot.py, qapbot/docs/CLAN_AND_WAR_CYCLE_ARCHITECTURE.md,
  tests/integration/test_cwl_ended_sweep.py,
  plans/implemented/tracker-0017-mid-month-cwl-war-fetches.md. 2522 tests pass.

  retracts the old DM, clears the global dm_sent record, re-points cwl_signups.dmed_discord_id and

  environments passed in its own (PROD-backup-seeded) copy of the same row, then failed with a
  403 ("Cannot edit a message authored by another user") refreshing PROD's message, and still

  assumption it'd be a harmless DEV no-op, copying the reasoning from the adjacent tracker

  interaction only to the owning bot application. A raw reaction-add event has no such routing:

  copy) actually has one. `handle_tracker_test_reaction()` now checks `CONFIG.tracker_enabled`
  (already hard-coded `not is_dev_mode`) as its very first line. Documented as Pitfall 39
  (COPILOT_PITFALLS_COOKBOOK.md) and in BUG_FEATURE_TRACKER.md's architecture section, since the
  same reasoning gap applies to any future raw-gateway-event listener touching tracker state.

- Fixed: `qapbot/mcp/tracker_mcp.py`'s stdio transport crashed instantly on Windows
  (`OSError: [WinError 6] Invalid handle`) before ever answering `initialize`, so the tracker
  MCP server never worked from VS Code Copilot Chat (`.vscode/mcp.json`) on this machine --
  only surfaced when testing "get an overview of open bugs/features" via Copilot Chat found no
  tracker tools available at all. Root cause: `run_stdio_server()` used
  `loop.connect_read_pipe(...)`, which on Windows requires an IOCP-registerable *overlapped*
  pipe handle; the anonymous pipe a host gives a child's stdin (VS Code/Node child_process
  included) isn't overlapped. Replaced with a plain blocking `sys.stdin.readline()` run in an
  executor thread each iteration -- works identically on every platform/host regardless of pipe
  type. Verified by spawning the server directly and driving initialize/tools-list/tools-call
  over its stdio transport by hand (list showed 16 real tracker items). File:

- Fixed: two bugs in the tracker #0009 memory-report instrumentation shipped yesterday, found by
  comparing its first live PROD numbers against reality. (1) _estimate_dict_size_mb() stopped
  recursing at depth 2, silently undercounting anything nested deeper than "dict of dict of
  list" -- exactly the shape of a war payload (payload -> clan -> members[] -> attacks[]).
  Verified against a realistic payload: the depth-capped version reported LESS than a pickle-size
  lower bound, which is structurally impossible for real heap cost. Replaced with a full
  recursive walk guarded by an id()-based `seen` set (cycle/shared-reference safe, reset per
  sampled entry so the per-entry average stays correct). (2) coc_clan_cache's report line was
  hardcoded to ~0.0 MB: _build_cache_summary() read `get_stats().get("estimated_size_mb", 0)`,
  a key get_stats() never actually sets. The real (pre-existing but unused) estimator,
  get_memory_usage_mb(), is now wired up -- and was itself deepened to recurse into each
  ClanMember's League/Icon/Badge objects via generic __dict__ walking, since a live profile
  showed ~40,000 such objects for barely 1,195 cached clans, almost entirely invisible to the
  old sys.getsizeof(member)-only version. Also corrects the record: the first live profile
  showed clan_name_cache steady at ~477 MB across a 2.9x RSS swing (7.1GB -> 2.5GB) while
  temp_war_objects/temp_war_stats entry counts dropped 3.4x -- clan_name_cache is confirmed NOT
  the incident's driver; the war caches remain the leading suspect, now measurable correctly.
  #0009 stays open pending a re-profile with these fixes during real war/CWL activity. Files:
  qapbot/coc_cache.py, qapbot/QBdiscocmdshelper_admin_command.py,
  tests/unit/test_memory_report_instrumentation.py. 2325 tests pass.

2026-08-21 (9)
- Fixed: linked accounts shown as grey/"not linked" on the CWL Manage Enrollment board
  (tracker item #0013). user_players' UNIQUE is (discord_id, player_tag), not player_tag alone,
  so one tag can hold both a real owner row and a stray 'UNASSIGNED' row — and since a plain
  /link never sets verified=1, the two are TIED on `verified`, leaving the dedup winner to
  undefined SQLite row order. When UNASSIGNED won, callers mapped discord_id to None and
  enrollmentBoard.ts's `discord_id == null` check rendered the player grey. Added an explicit
  `(discord_id = 'UNASSIGNED') ASC` tiebreak to all SEVEN affected queries in db_manager.py —
  and, critically, mirrored it in the FIVE Python re-sorts too: _chunked_in_query_sync's own
  docstring notes a per-chunk ORDER BY doesn't hold across chunks, and Python's stable sort
  would otherwise preserve chunk order among ties and silently discard the SQL preference
  (get_current_clan_tags_for_players_sync/get_cached_th_levels_for_players_sync gained
  discord_id in their SELECT purely to mirror it). Plus a new idempotent startup cleanup,
  _cleanup_stray_unassigned_duplicates(), removing UNASSIGNED rows whose tag already has a real
  owner — verified against a copy of the live PROD DB: removes exactly the known #GP9VJ0RGC

- Fixed: live PROD incident — a race in `coc_cache.py`'s `update_player_info_in_user_accounts()`
  (reachable both from the periodic poll loop and, on demand, from
  `QBdiscocmdshelper_cwl.py`'s `ensure_cwl_clan_membership_tracked()`, itself triggered by a CWL
  "Start Enrollment" DM blast) could append the same player twice to the shared in-memory

  SQLite's `UNIQUE(discord_id, player_tag)` constraint — and since nothing ever repaired the
  poisoned in-memory list afterward, every subsequent unrelated caller of that pseudo-account
  (including other players' legitimate self-service unlinks) kept failing identically for hours.
  Fixed with a per-clan_tag `asyncio.Lock` in `CoCClanCache` (same-clan_tag calls now serialize;
  different clan_tags still run concurrently) plus a defense-in-depth de-dup by `player_tag` in
  `db_manager.py`'s `_replace_user_players_rows()` before the INSERT. Also fixed a separate,
  related bug exposed by the same load spike: `UnlinkConfirmView._on_confirm`

  (qapbot/ui_clan_management.py) never deferred before their slow work (unlink + role sync),
  blowing Discord's 3s interaction-ack window under load and throwing "Unknown interaction"
  (10062) — both now `defer()` immediately and use `edit_original_response()`. Full root-cause
  trace + incident writeup: qapbot/docs/COPILOT_PITFALLS_COOKBOOK.md Pitfall 35. Files:

  have pending attacks. New table `guild_clan_custodians` (mirrors `guild_clan_roles` but allows
  multiple rows per clan_tag), loaded into `CACHE.server_config[guild_id]["clan_custodians"]`
  alongside the rest of guild config — no separate CACHE plumbing needed. Mention content is
  added to `_send_channel_war_notification`'s `channel.send()` call with an explicit
  `AllowedMentions(users=True, everyone=False, roles=False)` (first deliberate mention from an
  unattended periodic post); guilds with no custodians configured see byte-identical behavior to
  before. DM reminders are untouched. Files: qapbot/db_manager.py, qapbot/ui_clan_management.py,
  qapbot/war_notifications.py, qapbot/translations/en.json, qapbot/translations/de.json,

2026-08-19 (93)
- Fixed: the manual QA checklist's (`tests/cwl_enrollment_manual_qa_checklist.html`) own saved-
  progress restore only ever turned a checkbox ON (`if (state[id]) { checked = true }`), never
  explicitly OFF. These `<input>` elements carry no `name`/`id` attribute (only `data-id`), so
  Chrome's own "restore form values on reload" feature — which runs BEFORE this page's script and
  falls back to matching by DOM POSITION among same-type inputs when there's nothing else to key
  off — still applied its own stale, position-based checked/unchecked state on every reload.
  Inserting a new checklist item earlier in the list shifts every later item's position by one, so
  Chrome's restore then reapplied the old position's checked state to whichever item now sits
  there — visible as checkmarks "displaced" onto the wrong items after an insert (live bug report,
  project owner: "When new items are inserted into the qa checklist the checked items need to move
  along. Currently a insert leads to a displacement of the checkmarks."). Fixed by setting both
  branches (checked AND unchecked) unconditionally from the `data-id`-keyed `localStorage` state on
  every load, so it always wins over whatever Chrome's own restore had already set. No automated
  test runner covers this standalone file; verified with a syntax check plus a standalone
  simulation of the exact stale-native-state scenario.

2026-08-19 (90)
- Fixed (live bug report, project owner: "I added Hoehenloher Land as a guest clan but its members
  don't show up in the player pool"): a CWL guest clan that no guild on this bot tracks
  independently contributed ZERO players to the enrollment pool — an empty column, forever.
  - Root cause (NOT a regression from (84)-(89) — the affected code is untouched in HEAD): every
    pool seed in this feature ultimately reads `get_current_clan_members_sync()`, i.e.
    `user_players.current_clan_tag`. That table is only ever populated by `coc_cache.py`'s
    `update_player_info_in_user_accounts()`, which is deliberately gated on
    `clans.has_active_subscriptions` (the 2026-08-14 scope-bug incident: running it for every clan
    the shared `get_clan()` cache touches polluted `user_players` with thousands of CWL-opponent
    members and made every clan fetch slow). `has_active_subscriptions` is computed in
    `update_all_clan_subscription_statuses()` from channel subscriptions + guild `member_clans` +
    `member_families` ONLY — a CWL **guest** clan is in none of those sets. Confirmed against the
    live DEV DB: `#LGYLJQVP` (Hohenloher Land) has `has_active_subscriptions=0` and 0
    `user_players` rows, vs `#2C9UR9GJY` (StayCalm) with 1 and 47. That is exactly why the bug was
    invisible in every earlier round of guest-clan testing — StayCalm is another guild's own
    member clan and so was already tracked for unrelated reasons.
  - `qapbot/QBdiscocmdshelper_cwl.py`: new `ensure_cwl_clan_membership_tracked(clan_tags)` — for
    any clan on a CWL roster with no tracked members at all, fetches it once from the CoC API and
    runs the same population path the regular poll cycle uses, creating the UNASSIGNED-pool
    `user_players` rows (real name/TH/clan) the seeds then find. Scoped to clans an admin has
    explicitly put on a CWL roster, and only when they have no data whatsoever, so it never
    reintroduces the 2026-08-14 blanket-tracking behavior. Best-effort: an API failure logs and
    the save/Start Enrollment still completes.
  - Wired into BOTH entry points, which had the identical gap: `start_cwl_enrollment()` (guest
    clan already on the roster when enrollment starts) and `auto_assign_prior_cwl_members()`
    (guest clan added after enrollment is open).
  - Deliberately does NOT flip `has_active_subscriptions` for the guest clan: that would
    permanently ratchet `track_war_updates` on (one-way, by design) for a clan along for a single
    season. Tradeoff documented in the new function's docstring — the snapshot refreshes on the
    next add/Start Enrollment rather than on the poll cycle.
  - Two new tests in `tests/integration/test_cwl_guest_clan_live_scenario.py`, one per entry
    point, both verified via revert-confirm-restore (each fails on its own when only its own call
    site is reverted). Full suite: 2132 passed, 4 deselected. Python backend change — needs the
    DEV/PROD bot process restarted to take effect.
  - Recovery for the already-affected live season: after the restart, Remove the guest clan and
    re-add it. The re-add path is what re-runs the seed (an ordinary Save does not, since the clan
    is no longer "newly added to the roster").

  "unrelated individually-invited players"; corrected after re-checking the live dev log and DB:

    into this guild's own local `cwl_signups` as a `source='guest_invite'` placeholder the moment
    a shared clan is added — so its local pool has something to show — but writes no local
    `cwl_assignments` row and no `origin_shared_clan_id`. `_cleanup_local_pool_for_plain_clan_
    deactivation_sync`'s candidate set only ever looked at (a) live current members of the clan
    being removed and (b) local assignments pointing at it — a player who'd since left that clan
    in real life matched neither, so their mirror row became permanently invisible to Remove's
    cleanup and just sat there forever.

    once and threads its id into the local cleanup; `_cleanup_local_pool_for_plain_clan_

- Follow-up to (78): that fix only stops a FUTURE Delete Season from leaving orphaned
  `cwl_player_season_status` rows behind — it does nothing for a row already orphaned by an
  OLDER deletion that happened before (78) shipped, which is exactly what a live retest still

  dedup check itself self-healing instead of relying only on cleanup-at-delete-time.
  - `qapbot/db_manager.py`: `get_cwl_player_season_dm_status_bulk_sync()` (the actual gate
    `_send_cwl_enrollment_dm_batch` checks before DMing anyone) now only trusts a `dm_sent=1` row

    event that recorded a genuine response. An orphaned row (from ANY now-deleted event,
    regardless of when or how it was deleted) is excluded from the result entirely, which the
    caller's `.get(tag, False)` then reads as "never contacted" — no one-time backfill migration
    needed, this heals every existing orphaned row the next time it's checked.

- Added: CWL guest-player provenance — a guest player added because their clan was invited as a
  guest clan can no longer be removed individually (project owner's spec, verbatim: "Only removing
  the whole guest clan will remove that player"). Deliberately DERIVED from live current-clan
  membership on every check (`get_cwl_guest_clan_tags_sync`, new in `QBdiscocmdshelper_cwl.py`)
  rather than a persisted "how were you added" column/flag — this is what makes the spec's two
  race conditions fall out for free, with no write-time flag-flip logic anywhere:
  1. Adding a player individually who is already a current member of a guest clan already on the
     event roster is now rejected with a 409 (`POST /api/cwl/enrollment/guest`) instead of
     silently creating a redundant, independently-removable signup row.
  2. A previously individually-invited player is automatically reclassified as clan-derived the
     moment their clan is later added as a guest clan ("clan invitation beats individual
     invitation") — nothing has to notice and flip anything, the next classification check just
     starts returning a different answer.
  - `GET /api/cwl/enrollment/guest-players` (the "Remove Guest Players" panel's list) now excludes
    clan-derived players — only individually-invited ones are offered for individual removal.
  - `POST /api/cwl/enrollment/guest-players/remove` now classifies every requested tag and rejects
    any clan-derived ones with a clear reason instead of deleting them, returning
    `{"ok": true, "removed": [...], "rejected": [...]}` (previously just `{"ok": true}`) — still
    removes every valid tag in the same request. The Hub-message refresh/enrollment-version bump
    now only fire when something was actually removed.
  - New: right-click "Remove guest player" context menu on the Manage Teams (enrollment) board —
    shown for any guest-badged card; a rejection from the backend (clan-derived) surfaces as an
    inline error via the board's existing footer status line, same as any other failed action.
    `activity/client/src/enrollmentBoard.ts`, `main.ts`, new `.player-context-menu` CSS in
    `index.html`. The Configure Participating Clans panel's own remove flow
    (`clanConfigTable.ts`) now also surfaces any `rejected` entries from the same endpoint instead
    of assuming every requested removal always succeeds.

2026-08-18 (63)
- Fixed: CWL enrollment's DM-sending loop (`start_cwl_enrollment()`) could be silently aborted
  mid-batch by a single transient Discord 5xx error — `CacheManager.send_user_dm()` used to
  re-raise `discord.DiscordServerError` instead of returning `False` like every other failure
  path, and the CWL loop had no try/except of its own, so every recipient after the failing one
  never got DMed and the event stayed stuck in `status='draft'` (the transition to
  `signup_open` runs after the loop). Phase 1 of `CWL_ENROLLMENT_PLAYER_POOL_REDESIGN_PLAN.md`
  (multi-phase rework of the CWL player-pool/enrollment-DM flow, prompted by a live bug where a
  multi-account test user only got DMed for some of his linked accounts).
  - `cache_manager.py`: `send_user_dm()` is now a thin bool wrapper around a new
    `send_user_dm_detailed()`, which retries a `DiscordServerError` up to `DM_SEND_MAX_RETRIES`
    (3) with a short backoff and never re-raises, returning `(bool, "sent"|"blocked"|"failed")` —
    `"blocked"` (DMs closed/bot blocked/user gone) is never retried, `"failed"` is a transient
    error that didn't recover.
  - `QBdiscocmdshelper_cwl.py`: the DM loop extracted into `_send_cwl_enrollment_dm_batch()`,
    collecting `blocked`/`failed` recipient-name lists into `start_cwl_enrollment()`'s summary.
    `send_cwl_signup_template_dm()` now returns `(bool, outcome)` (its other caller,
    `web_bridge.py`'s `handle_post_cwl_enrollment_guest`, updated to unpack).
  - `ui_cwl_roster.py` + `en.json`/`de.json`: the Start Enrollment admin summary now reports
    blocked/failed recipients by name instead of the failure disappearing silently.
  - Tests: new `TestSendUserDmDetailed`/`TestSendUserDm` classes in
    `tests/unit/test_cache_manager_async.py` (retry-then-succeed, exhausted-retries never
    raises, Forbidden/NotFound never retried); new
    `test_one_recipients_dm_failure_does_not_abort_the_rest_of_the_batch` in
    `tests/integration/test_cwl_start_enrollment.py`; ~20 existing CWL enrollment tests and 2
    `test_web_bridge.py` guest-invite tests updated for the `send_user_dm`/
    `send_cwl_signup_template_dm` signature changes. Full suite: 2074 passed, 4 deselected.

2026-08-18 (61)
- Fixed: `get_global_db_statistics_sync()`'s ~20s cold scan (the `/status` global-stats query) —
  diagnosed live on PROD's `qapbot_PROD.log` after deploying (59): the fire-and-forget startup
  warm-up (`QapBot._warm_global_db_stats_cache()`, spawned via `QBcore.spawn_tracked` right as
  the first update cycle begins) shared `db_manager`'s 8-connection sync pool with that cycle's
  Phase-1 clan fetches, and the leftover multi-second stalls in the first cycle after a restart
  (14.5s, 11.2s×2, 6.1s, 6.1s, 6.0s, 5.7s, 5.5s — all clustered right on top of the
  `[DB-STATS-WARM] ... warmed in 20.4s` line) traced back to this, not to (59)'s change. Two
  independent fixes, both in `db_manager.py`'s `get_global_db_statistics_sync()`:
  - **Parallelized the 5 sub-queries**: they're independent reads against independent tables, so
    they now run concurrently (one `_sync_conn()` connection each, via a local
    `concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=5)`) instead of sequentially on one
    connection — cuts wall time to roughly the single slowest query instead of the sum of all
    five, with zero behavior/accuracy change.
  - **Persisted the exact result to `bot_metadata`** (new key
    `DatabaseManager._GLOBAL_STATS_METADATA_KEY`, JSON with a wall-clock `computed_at_utc`) every
    time an exact computation completes. New async method
    `preload_global_db_statistics_from_snapshot()` restores that snapshot into the in-memory
    `_global_stats_cache` at startup — converting the persisted wall-clock age back into an
    equivalent `_global_stats_cache_ts` so the existing `_GLOBAL_STATS_TTL` (25h) check still
    expires it at the correct time across a restart, same as if the process had never stopped.
  - `QapBot.py`'s `_warm_global_db_stats_cache()`: the plain startup call (`force_refresh=False`)
    now tries the snapshot restore first (a single tiny row read, effectively instant) and only
    falls through to the real scan if no snapshot exists yet (a brand-new DB's very first-ever
    startup). The nightly-maintenance call (`force_refresh=True`, after REINDEX/VACUUM/ANALYZE)
    is unchanged in behavior — always does the real (now-parallelized) scan and refreshes the
    persisted snapshot for the next restart. `/status`'s manual force-refresh option goes through
    the same `force_refresh=True` path and benefits identically.
  - Explicitly did NOT use SQLite's `sqlite_stat1` approximate-count tables (populated by the
    nightly `ANALYZE`, itself already capped to a 1000-row sample via `PRAGMA analysis_limit`) —
    an earlier option floated for this fix. Would have made the warm-up cost effectively zero,
    but only by trading exact `/status` numbers for approximate ones, with real format-parsing
    risk (distinct-count estimation from `sqlite_stat1`'s stat string is index-shape-dependent
    and untested against the live schema). The persisted-exact-snapshot approach gets the same
    "instant at startup" outcome with no accuracy tradeoff and no new fragile parsing logic, so
    it was chosen instead.
  - Tests: 11 new (`tests/unit/test_db_global_statistics.py`) against a real `WarHistoryDB.
    initialize()`-backed temp-file DB (both the sync pool and the async `bot_metadata` path need
    to be real for this) — exact count computation across main+history schemas, cache-hit vs
    force_refresh behavior, snapshot persistence shape, snapshot restore (including an
    already-stale-by-10h snapshot correctly restoring as 10h-aged rather than fresh), and
    unparseable/incomplete snapshot handling. 2068 tests pass.
  - Docs: `qapbot/docs/CODE_STRUCTURE.md` and `qapbot/docs/DATABASE_ARCHITECTURE.md` updated
    (the latter also had a stale "5-minute TTL" mention left over from before the 2026-08-03
    TTL raise to 25h — corrected while touching the same paragraph).
  - Needs a bot restart on DEV/PROD to take effect.

- Fixed: `coc_cache.py`'s `update_player_info_in_user_accounts()` — the per-clan-fetch step that
  keeps `user_players` TH/name/clan/role current — did two full O(len(user_accounts)) synchronous

  consecutive `[COC-API-CALL] Fetching clan data for ...` lines inside the same "20 concurrent"
  Phase-1 fetch batch — the scan doesn't just make its own clan's fetch slow, it blocks the whole
  asyncio event loop for its duration, stalling every other concurrently in-flight clan fetch too
  (network-bound tasks that could otherwise have proceeded). Only triggered for clans with
  `has_active_subscriptions=True` (guild member clans), so every "inactive 22h" member-clan poll
  paid this cost.

    by this path and a full-scan fallback (kept for when `db_manager` is unavailable — should not
    happen in a running bot, but a real reachable branch, not dead code). Departure detection
    re-checks `current_clan_tag` against the live in-memory value before clearing it, in case a
    concurrent cycle already changed it since the DB snapshot was taken.

    the DB-indexed path directly (TH update via owner lookup, new-tag UNASSIGNED creation,

- Added: Batch A (Steps 1-3) of `PLAYER_NAME_INDEX_RETIREMENT_PLAN.md` — migrates `/whois`'s

  have caused. `CACHE.player_name_index` itself is untouched (still loaded/written) — this batch

  - **Step 1** (`qapbot/db_manager.py`): refactored `search_player_names_sync`'s FTS5 MATCH query
    into a shared `_search_player_names_fts_sync(query, limit)` core, and added
    `search_player_names_full_sync(query, hard_cap=5000)` as a second thin wrapper over it — same
    trigram-floor guard and FTS5-literal-quoting, just a much higher cap for `/whois`'s "everyone
    else" fallback than the guest search's 25-row UX cap.
  - **Steps 2-3** (`QBdiscordcmds.py`): replaced the old `_search_player_name_index_sync()`

    (`user_accounts`/`temp_war_stats`/`coc_clan_cache`), small enough (a guild's own roster tops
    out in the hundreds) to run directly on the event loop, no threading needed — then
    `search_player_names_full_sync()` (threaded, since it's a real SQLite call) fills in
    non-member matches, deduplicated by tag. Guild matches are concatenated FIRST, so they can
    never be excluded by the `[:25]` UX slice regardless of how many unrelated global matches
    exist — a query matching thousands of players elsewhere can no longer push a guild's own
    member out of the results, the exact failure mode a naive "just raise the cap" migration
    would have reintroduced one order of magnitude later. Also replaces the old unconditional
    "<3 chars = reject" floor with one that only gates the global fallback — the guild pass has
    no trigram tokenizer and needs no floor, so e.g. a 2-character query that matches a guild
    member now returns a working result instead of an error (new i18n key
    `commands.whois.player_search_too_short`, `en`+`de`).

2026-08-17 (54)
- Fixed: (53)'s player_name_fts rowid-scheme migration was still too slow — on PROD it never
  finished at all. Live PROD log confirmed: migration started 22:03:27, no
  `[DB-SCHEMA] Backfilled ... row(s)` success line ever appeared, and QapBot.py's own 30-minute
  safety timeout (`asyncio.wait_for(db_manager.initialize(...), timeout=1800.0)`) fired at
  22:33:27 — exactly 1800s later — raising "Database initialization timed out - bot cannot
  start". DEV had measured (53)'s hash-based approach at 355.25s for the same ~6.6M rows; PROD's
  much weaker hardware pushed the identical work well past 30 minutes.
  - Root cause of the slowness: (53) derived player_name_fts's rowid by calling
    `hashlib.blake2b()` once per row in pure Python (6.6M calls) specifically to avoid a DB
    round-trip. That avoidance was the wrong trade — the round-trip is cheap (one bulk SQL
    query); 6.6M individual Python-level hash calls (each with its own encode()/digest()/
    int.from_bytes()) is not.
  - Fix: `qapbot/db_manager.py` — removed `_fts_rowid_for_tag()` and the `hashlib` import
    entirely. player_name_fts's rowid is now looked up from player_name_search's own
    SQLite-assigned rowid instead of computed — one bulk `SELECT player_tag, rowid FROM
    player_name_search` for the backfill, one small chunked lookup (reusing
    `_chunked_in_query_sync`) for the incremental writer. Stable across repeated upserts since
    `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` never changes a row's rowid. Bumped
    `PLAYER_NAME_FTS_ROWID_SCHEME_VALUE` to `player_name_search_rowid_v2` so any host already on
    `tag_hash_v1` (or with data from the incomplete PROD run) gets one more automatic rebuild —
    this time on the fast path.
  - Measured on DEV (identical ~6.6M-row dataset, a fresh copy of PROD's DB): **82.42s**, a 4.3x
    speedup over (53)'s 355.25s. Comfortable headroom under the 30-minute timeout even accounting
    for PROD's much weaker CPU.
  - Also found empirically while chasing this: because the backfill runs via
    `asyncio.to_thread()`, `asyncio.wait_for()`'s timeout cancels the *awaiting* coroutine but
    cannot stop the underlying worker thread — Python has no mechanism to forcibly kill a running
    thread. So a timed-out migration's actual DB work may keep running in the background
    independent of what the rest of the process does after the timeout error. Worth keeping in
    mind for any future long-running to_thread() work guarded by a wait_for() timeout.
  - Tests: replaced the 3 `_fts_rowid_for_tag`-specific tests with 2 tests asserting
    player_name_fts's rowid actually mirrors player_name_search's (including stability across a
    repeated upsert); updated the migration-marker test's rowid assertion accordingly. 2052 tests
    pass (net -1 vs (53), consolidating the rowid-behavior coverage).
  - PROD is currently mid-incident: its last startup attempt hit the 30-minute timeout and
    logged "bot cannot start" — check whether the process is still alive (the to_thread caveat
    above means it might be) before deploying this fix; safe to kill either way. Correction to
    an earlier claim (2026-08-17 review): whether the timed-out v1 thread reached its `commit()`
    is UNKNOWABLE from outside — per the to_thread caveat it kept running after the timeout and
    may have finished. Safety holds regardless, for a different reason: uncommitted → SQLite
    rolls back on next connection open; committed → the data is internally-consistent v1-scheme
    data, and the v2 marker mismatch forces a full rebuild on next startup anyway. Both branches
    end in the same clean place; no partial-data risk in either.

2026-08-17 (52)
- Fixed: first PROD update cycle after deploying (51)/Batch 7 stalled silently right after
  "[PHASE-3B] Completed" every cycle — confirmed via live PROD log analysis, not a deadlock (the
  process kept consuming CPU). Root cause: `player_name_fts` is an FTS5 virtual table with
  `player_tag UNINDEXED` — UNINDEXED only excludes a column from full-text `MATCH`, it does NOT
  give SQLite any index for a plain equality lookup on that column. The incremental writer
  (`_upsert_player_name_search_rows_in_conn`, called from every war-write flush via
  `_upsert_player_name_index_in_conn`) did `DELETE FROM player_name_fts WHERE player_tag = ?` once
  per changed player — with no index to use, each call degraded to a full table scan. Invisible in
  tests (tiny tables); catastrophic in PROD the moment the one-time startup backfill populated the
  table to its real ~6.6M rows — a single flush batch touching a few hundred players turned into
  hundreds of full-table scans back to back. Flipping `cwl_use_fts_player_search` back off would
  NOT have fixed this: that flag only gates the *read* path: the write-through into
  player_name_search/player_name_fts runs unconditionally regardless of it.
  - Fix: `qapbot/db_manager.py` — new module-level `_fts_rowid_for_tag(player_tag)` derives a
    deterministic FTS5 `rowid` from a blake2b hash of the tag (8 bytes, collision-negligible even
    at 6.6M+ tags). `rowid` is the one column FTS5 genuinely indexes, so DELETE/INSERT against
    `player_name_fts` now target `WHERE rowid = ?` (O(1)) instead of `WHERE player_tag = ?`
    (O(table size)) — computed independently by every caller, no DB round-trip needed.
    `_upsert_player_name_search_rows_in_conn` and `_backfill_player_name_search_if_needed` both
    updated to use it.
  - Migration: PROD's already-backfilled `player_name_fts` has old, SQLite-auto-assigned rowids
    that don't match the new hash-derived scheme. Added a `bot_metadata` marker
    (`player_name_fts_rowid_scheme` = `tag_hash_v1`) checked at startup — if unset,
    `_backfill_player_name_search_if_needed()` force-rebuilds `player_name_search`/`player_name_fts`
    from `player_name_index` even when row counts already match (the old guard's only check),
    then sets the marker so the rebuild doesn't repeat on future startups.
  - 6 new tests (`tests/unit/test_player_name_search_fts.py`): `_fts_rowid_for_tag` determinism/
    range, no stale duplicate FTS row after a re-upsert (rowid-delete actually finds the old row),
    the migration marker forcing one rebuild of old-scheme data, and the marker not repeating once
    set. 2053 tests pass.
  - Needs a bot restart on PROD to pick up the fix (and to let the one-time rowid-scheme
    migration run and finally clear the stalled state) — DEV has no accumulated
    `player_name_fts` data at PROD scale so was never at risk of this, but gets the fix too on its
    next restart.

2026-08-17 (50)
- Fixed: `QBdiscordcmds.py`'s `admin()` action-router function (~1400 lines, one `if
  action_norm == "X": ... return` branch per admin action) had three redundant `from
  qapbot.cache_manager import CACHE` re-imports scattered inside individual action branches —
  `CACHE` is already imported once at module level. Python scopes a name for a function's ENTIRE
  body at compile time: a `from X import Y` anywhere inside a function (any branch, any nesting)
  makes `Y` local for the WHOLE function, so any OTHER branch referencing `CACHE` earlier in
  source order than one of those three re-imports crashed with `UnboundLocalError` the instant
  it ran — confirmed at least the `BACKFILL_CWL_GROUPS` admin action was broken this way on
  every single invocation. Surfaced via the VS Code Problems panel (35 Pylance
  `reportUnboundVariable`/attribute-access errors) — not a false positive; Pylance was correctly
  predicting a real crash. Fixed by deleting the three redundant re-imports (plus a same-pattern
  `CONFIG` one in `/help`, and one more harmless-but-redundant `CACHE` re-import in an unrelated
  small function, removed for consistency). Also renamed `/help`'s local `AVAILABLE_COMMANDS`
  variable to lowercase `available_commands` (Pylance's `reportConstantRedefinition` — a
  naming-convention lint, not a real bug: it's a plain local, legitimately reassigned once for
  the DM-filtered case, just misleadingly ALL-CAPS).
  - Documented as a new Pitfall 28 in `qapbot/docs/COPILOT_PITFALLS_COOKBOOK.md` — this codebase
    deliberately favors local imports inside functions throughout (this session included), so
    this exact landmine is a real, recurring risk, not a one-off; includes a repro and an audit
    technique for finding other instances.
  - Also found and fixed a genuine test-isolation gap while investigating a DIFFERENT, unrelated
    report from this same live-testing session (enabling `CWL_USE_FTS_PLAYER_SEARCH_DEV=true` in
    `.env` to test Batch 7 on DEV): `tests/conftest.py` loads the same `.env` file the live bot
    does, so the local dev flag silently changed test-suite behavior too — broke every test that
    seeds `CACHE.player_name_index` in-memory without also seeding the real DB. Fixed the same
    way `PROD_DATA_DIR` already is in that file (existing precedent, same file): force the flag
    to a known `false` value in `conftest.py` before `qapbot.config`'s own `load_dotenv` runs, so
    test-suite behavior never depends on a developer's local `.env` state for this flag.
  - 2046 tests pass (`.\run_tests.ps1`) — unchanged count, this was a pure bugfix + test-harness
    hardening, no behavior/feature change. Needs a bot restart on DEV/PROD to take effect (the
    `admin()` fix is real functional behavior; the `AVAILABLE_COMMANDS` rename and the cookbook
    doc are no-ops at runtime either way).

2026-08-16 (36)
- Fixed: (34)'s own fix regressed the same screen it fixed — reported live on PROD right after
  deploying (34): the clan-config table's header row rendered, but every clan row underneath was
  gone. Root cause: wrapping `<table>` in the new `.table-scroll` div (`overflow-x: auto`)
  triggered a CSS Overflow spec rule most people never hit — when one axis's overflow is
  `visible` and the other isn't, the `visible` one's USED value is forced to `auto` too, even
  though nothing set it explicitly. That silently turned `.table-scroll` into the *sticky
  positioning containing block* for the `<thead>`'s `th`s inside it, instead of the page (which
  it was before this div existed) — but `.table-scroll`'s height was left `auto` (sized exactly
  to its content), so it never actually scrolls internally, meaning a sticky child inside it has
  nothing to react to and just renders at a permanent, fixed `top: <topbar's height>px` offset —
  which pushed the header down on top of the first couple of rows, hiding them behind its opaque
  background, on every render, at any window width or scroll position (not the (34) bug's
  narrow-window trigger — reproduced identically at 1400px wide). Confirmed root cause and the
  fix both empirically (Playwright against a throwaway harness rendering the real
  `renderClanConfigTable()` with mock data — DOM inspection alone can't see a layout/paint bug
  like this). Fix: `th`'s sticky `top` is now `0` (correct once `.table-scroll` — not the page —
  is its containing block), and `.table-scroll` now gets an explicit JS-computed `max-height`
  (viewport height minus the topbar's real height, recomputed on resize) so it becomes a genuine,
  independently-scrolling container — mirroring `enrollmentBoard.ts`'s own `resizeBoard()`/
  `.board` pattern, which solved this identical containing-block problem there first. This keeps
  every property (34) wanted: narrow windows still scroll the table sideways instead of wrapping,
  and the header still stays visibly pinned above the rows — just scrolling within the table's own
  bounded region now, rather than tracking the whole page's scroll. Frontend-only — deployed to
  both DEV (activity/client, https://e720b232.cwl-clan-config-dev.pages.dev) and PROD
  (activity/client, https://33a8356c.cwl-clan-config-prod.pages.dev); no bot restart needed.

2026-08-16 (35)
- Fixed: a PROD incident right after (34)'s deploy — clicking "Add New Season" while the periodic
  update cycle was mid-write produced "database is locked" and a `discord.errors.NotFound: 404
  Unknown interaction`, and simultaneously froze totally unrelated CoC API calls for other guilds
  (bunched at the exact same wall-clock timestamp). Root cause: `ui_cwl_roster.py`'s Add New
  Season callback called a sync SQLite write DIRECTLY on the asyncio event loop thread; that
  write acquires `db_manager.py`'s `_sync_write_lock` (a plain `threading.Lock`) then blocks up
  to `PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000`, and while blocked ON THE EVENT LOOP THREAD, nothing else in the
  whole bot process can run — not just this one interaction. Fixed the reported button, then
  audited the entire CWL subsystem (asked to check thoroughly, since this pattern doesn't fix
  itself) and found the same anti-pattern with zero `asyncio.to_thread()` usage anywhere in
  `QBdiscocmdshelper_cwl.py`/`web_bridge.py`. Fixed all of it: every sync DB write call in
  `ui_cwl_roster.py`, `ui_clan_management.py`, `QBdiscocmdshelper_cwl.py`, and `web_bridge.py`
  (season create/delete/carry-over, cross-guild sharing/detach/evict, signup/assignment upserts,
  Start Enrollment, the web Activity's clan-config save) now runs off the event loop thread —
  bundled into one `asyncio.to_thread()` hop per atomic unit of work where the function was
  already fully synchronous (to avoid introducing new race windows a per-call wrap would), or
  wrapped call-by-call where a real `await` already sat in the middle of the sequence. Also added
  `_respond_or_log()` so a response that arrives after Discord's 3s ack window logs a warning
  instead of crashing with an unhandled 404. Full writeup: Pitfall 26,
  `qapbot/docs/COPILOT_PITFALLS_COOKBOOK.md`. Backend-only — needs a bot restart on PROD to take
  effect. 1997 tests pass.

2026-08-16 (32)
- Fixed: root-caused why the hover pop-up (31) showed Skill Score/Avg stars but no Attacks/
  Missed-CWL-attacks/Attack-Defense-ratio for some players (reported: Butterblume). Not a pop-up
  bug — a real data-correctness bug in the DB layer. Every sync/async query that combines
  `main.<table>` and `history.<table>` into one result set via `WITH t AS (SELECT * FROM main.t
  UNION ALL SELECT * FROM history.t)` matched columns by POSITION, not name; `main`/`history`
  have identical column NAMES but a physically different on-disk column ORDER (confirmed against
  DEV's real history DB), so any row actually read from `history` (any war old enough to be
  archived) came back with `max_attacks`/`missed_attacks`/`defensive_stars`/etc. silently
  misaligned. This is the READ-side counterpart of the 2026-08-14 hot/history schema-drift
  incident (Cardinal Rule 1) — that fix only covered the migration WRITE path. The stored data
  itself was fine; only these read queries were misinterpreting it.
- Fixed ~20 call sites across `qapbot/db_manager.py` (sync + async), `QBhelperfunctions.py`
  (`/whois` reliability/activity/skill), and `qapbot/QBdiscocmdshelper_admin_command.py`
  (`/backfill_cwl_groups`) to name columns explicitly on both sides of every `main`/`history`
  UNION, via new `WarHistoryDB._explicit_column_list_sync()` (sync counterpart of the existing
  async `_explicit_column_list()`) + a public `explicit_column_list_sync()` alias.
- Also found and fixed a second, still-live WRITE-path instance of the original 2026-08-14 bug:
  `WarHistoryDB._bulk_move_chunk()` (the one-time/manual `fast_bulk_history_migration()` path,
  `run_history_migration_now.py --fast`) used a bare `INSERT INTO history.<table> SELECT * FROM
  main.<table> ...` — never covered by the 2026-08-14 fix, which only touched the normal monthly
  migration path. Fixed the same way.
- Added `WarHistoryDB.check_hot_history_schema_parity_sync()` — a standing guardrail, called once
  at bot startup (`QapBot.py`, logged at CRITICAL if non-empty) and regression-tested, that flags
  any of the 4 mirrored tables where `main`/`history` disagree on column SET (added/removed
  column — not automatically recoverable). Pure column reordering is deliberately NOT flagged —
  every affected query is now immune to it by design (explicit column names), so flagging it
  would just be CI noise for a harmless, expected divergence.
- Follow-up after being asked to confirm complete coverage: re-audited the ENTIRE repo (every
  `SELECT *` anywhere, plus a separate pass for positional/non-named row access) rather than
  trusting the original targeted grep. Found and fixed 3 more offenders, all in manually-invoked
  diagnostic/audit scripts previously left as "lower priority": `qapbot/scripts/

  (1). New shared `explicit_column_list_from_conn()` module-level helper in `db_manager.py`
  (next to `attach_history_db`) so standalone scripts don't each duplicate the PRAGMA logic.
  Confirmed via direct inspection that the only 2 other `history.`-touching scripts
  (`backfill_group_track_war_updates.py`, `repromote_mid_season_clans.py`) already use fully
  explicit column lists — no fix needed. Confirmed via `PRAGMA table_info` that only 4 tables
  are ever mirrored to `history` at all (war_attacks, war_summary, cwl_league_groups,
  cwl_league_rounds) — every other `SELECT *` in the repo targets a main-only table and is
  inherently immune to this bug class. Every remaining `SELECT *`/`UNION ALL SELECT *` in the
  codebase now targets either a single schema or a non-mirrored table.
- Updated `.github/copilot-instructions.md` Cardinal Rule 1 and `qapbot/docs/

  also fixed a second bug the `<tr>`-level version had even on desktop: the header row's own line

  point of a guest clan: it's explicitly NOT part of the family). A guest clan added BEFORE Start
  Enrollment runs (deliberately skipped by the separate "clan added after enrollment" auto-assign
  path, since Start Enrollment's own comprehensive seed is supposed to cover it) had its own
  current members silently excluded from the auto-assign CANDIDATE list entirely — no matter how
  much real prior-CWL-attack history they had for exactly that clan, they were never even
  considered, since resolve_prior_cwl_assignments() only resolves entries for player_tags it was
  actually given. Confirmed against real prod-copy data: roughly a quarter of the guest clan's
  current roster had a real, recent CWL attack recorded for that exact clan and should have been
  auto-assigned but weren't.
- Fixed by unioning `participating_clan_tags` into the candidate-pool clan-tag resolution — the
  exact same union `_build_enrollment_payload()` (web_bridge.py) already applies to its own player
  pool, for the identical underlying reason. `qapbot/QBdiscocmdshelper_cwl.py`. Tests: 1 new

  `.\run_tests.ps1`: 1967 passed, 4 deselected. Python-only change — needs the bot process

- Architectural fix, not just a display patch: split `cwl_shared_clan_players.status` (a shared
  clan's overloaded "confirmed IS the assignment" column) into two genuinely independent columns.
  Project owner's spec, verbatim, across several follow-up messages: "The confirmation status is
  player specific and unique per player. It must not be altered by any assignment process across
  clans and guilds! ... Confirmation status and assignment status should be treated completely
  separate. the one has a totally different meaning logically than the other! ... The symbols in
  the player tile should exclusively reflect confirmation status. The assignment status is
  obvious to the user from the column the player tile appears in." (15)'s display-layer patch
  (hiding the badge for source='auto_assigned' specifically) only band-aided the one reported
  symptom — the underlying DATABASE value was still being force-set to 'confirmed' by every
  placement decision (auto-assign, and even a deliberate admin_override drag-and-drop), which is
  the actual violation the project owner flagged.
- New `cwl_shared_clan_players.assigned` column (0/1), migrated with a one-time backfill
  (`assigned=1 WHERE status='confirmed'`, gated so it only ever runs once against a real
  pre-existing DB) so no currently-placed player silently drops out of their column. Two new,
  narrowly-scoped DB methods replace the old combined upsert: `set_cwl_shared_clan_player_status_sync`
  (touches ONLY status/responded_at — genuine player response, never touches `assigned`) and

  `status`). Every write path updated to call the correct one: drag-and-drop/auto-assign
  (`assign_cwl_player_sync`) now call the assignment-only method; confirm/withdraw
  (`handle_post_cwl_enrollment_signup`) and the visibility-seed step call the status-only method;
  the sharing-migration step (the one legitimate place both facts are genuinely known at once)
  calls both. `_build_enrollment_payload`'s placement check now reads `assigned` instead of
  `status == 'confirmed'`, and the displayed `signup_status` is simply the raw, always-honest
  `status` column — (15)'s source-based display override is no longer needed at all.
  `find_cwl_shared_clan_memberships_for_player_sync` (the conflict-detection query used by the
  eviction/purge logic) now queries `assigned = 1` instead of `status = 'confirmed'`, since every
  one of its callers only ever cared about placement, never response.
- `qapbot/db_manager.py`, `qapbot/QBdiscocmdshelper_cwl.py`, `qapbot/web_bridge.py`. Tests: DB-layer

  database, and ~20 existing tests across 5 files updated for the new seeding pattern.

2026-08-16 (8)
- Fixed (finally, hopefully): the Configure Participating Clans row-line-off-by-a-pixel saga —
  three prior rounds tried to make every cell's rendered height agree to the sub-pixel (vertical-
  align, line-height, explicit height, box-sizing) and it kept recurring. Reframed the actual
  mechanism instead of re-patching the symptom: with border-collapse: collapse, a row's divider
  is stitched together from N *separate* per-cell border-bottom segments merged at their shared
  edges — if any two adjacent cells paint even a fractional device-pixel apart at final
  rasterization (a real browser behavior for heterogeneous content like a <select> next to plain
  text, regardless of how identical their CSS box-model math is), that shared edge can visibly
  shift, because multiple independent things had to agree and didn't. Replaced every cell's own
  `border-bottom` with a single `box-shadow: inset 0 -1px 0 0` on the `<tr>` itself — one row,
  one paint operation, one line; nothing left for two cells to disagree about, since only one box
  is involved at all. `index.html`. Frontend typecheck/build clean, deployed to DEV.

2026-08-16 (7)

  bumped further (36px -> 64px) — still partly covered by Discord's own iPad Activity control

- Fixed: row lines still off by a device-pixel even after the fixed row-height fix — a
  <select>'s and an <input type="date">'s font-driven content height can round a sub-pixel apart
  even under identical CSS (different form control types, different internal browser rendering
  paths). Fixed with `box-sizing: border-box` plus an explicit `height: 26px` on every select/

  flow's existing Hub-message refresh happened to incidentally clear it (a genuine new message
  edit, not a response to the now-stale original interaction). Closing WITHOUT saving never
  triggered any refresh at all, leaving nothing to clear the stuck state. Best-effort with a
  1.5s client-side timeout so it can never meaningfully delay the actual close.
  `qapbot/web_bridge.py`, `activity/server/src/index.ts`, `activity/client/src/main.ts`,

2026-08-16 (1)
- Fixed: repeatedly opening/closing the CWL Activity in DEV eventually failed with "Setup
  failed: token exchange failed: 502" and stopped working. Root-caused via a live `wrangler
  tail` session during reproduction (after first fixing the Worker to actually log/return
  Discord's real rejection reason, which it always had but never surfaced): Discord's own OAuth
  token-endpoint rate limit ("You are being rate limited for requesting too many tokens"), not
  a bug producing malformed/duplicate requests — every launch really was exactly one legitimate
  authorize()+/api/token pair. Root cause was launch *frequency*: every single launch, even
  reopening the same view a few seconds after closing it, did a completely fresh OAuth
  round-trip, when `authenticate()` is documented to accept a previously-obtained access_token
  directly. Fixed: `main.ts` now caches the access_token in `sessionStorage` after a successful
  exchange and tries `authenticate()` with the cached token first on the next launch — skipping
  `authorize()`/`/api/token` entirely — falling back to the full flow only if the cached token
  is ever rejected. `activity/server/src/index.ts`, `activity/client/src/main.ts`. Frontend
  typecheck/build clean, deployed to DEV. Full details: `qapbot/docs/CWL_CLAN_CONFIG_ACTIVITY_PLAN.md`.

2026-08-15 (10)
- Fixed: live DEV testing of the cross-guild shared-clan feature (entry 9) surfaced a real
  ownership-resolution bug: `resolve_cwl_clan_owner`'s only tiebreak beyond role/verified was
  iteration order over `affected_guild_ids`, which always lists the ACTING (newly-joining) guild
  first — so a clan's real Leader/Co-Leader being a Discord member of more than one affected
  guild (plausible: same admin account in their real clan's server AND a personal/test server)
  let the acting guild win regardless of which one actually manages the clan. Fixed by ranking
  "does this guild track the clan natively (member_clans/member_families)" ahead of iteration
  order, plus a warning log when the bot process isn't even a member of one of the affected
  guilds (silently excluded a guild from consideration with no other signal).
- Fixed: the Configure Participating Clans screen (unlike Manage Enrollment, which already
  deferred to the owner) was still reading AND writing each guild's own local roster_size/
  cwl_start_at/target_league_rank for an already-shared clan. `_build_clan_config_payload` now
  sources from the owner's row; `handle_post_clan_config` overrides a non-owner's submitted
  values back to the owner's before saving; frontend shows read-only inputs + a "Managed by X"
  hint. Surfaced a second bug in the same payload builder: a guest/shared clan's tag was never
  unioned into `all_tags`, so it silently vanished from the table on every reload after the save
  that added it.

  that surfaced the ownership bug above: add -> save -> remove -> save -> start enrollment ->
  re-add -> save.
- Added: foreign-guest conversion + purge — if a guild cross-assigns a shared clan's REAL member
  into one of its own private clans, then detaches from that shared clan, the player now
  "becomes a guest player automatically" (`cwl_signups.source='guest_invite'`, new nullable

  came from; once the clan's real owning guild reassigns that exact player elsewhere, the
  foreign placement is now purged entirely (assignment + signup row), not just unassigned.
- Fixed (PROD-risk, caught same day): the `origin_shared_clan_id` migration above initially
  shipped with its `CREATE INDEX` placed inline right after `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS
  cwl_signups`, which is a no-op against any pre-existing database — so on any already-
  initialized DEV/PROD database the index statement ran before the column existed, throwing
  "no such column" and aborting the ENTIRE database initialization (bot couldn't start at all).
  Fixed by removing the inline index — the identical, correctly-placed one already existed right
  after the real `_add_column_if_missing()` migration call. Verified against a scripted
  pre-existing database that the fix migrates cleanly with zero data loss. General lesson
  recorded in `.github/copilot-instructions.md` Rule 12 and `CWL_ROSTER_PLANNING_PLAN.md`.

2026-08-15 (9)
- Added: Cross-guild shared CWL clans — a real-world clan can only actually play CWL for one
  roster, but nothing previously stopped two independent guilds from each configuring the same
  clan_tag into their own separate CWL events for the same season with zero coordination.
  Confirmed with the project owner: don't block this, share it — both guilds manage ONE real
  record instead of two fake independent ones. New tables `cwl_shared_clans`/
  `cwl_shared_clan_guilds`/`cwl_shared_clan_players` (`db_manager.py`) — deliberately separate
  from `cwl_event_clans`/`cwl_signups`/`cwl_assignments`, which are NEVER written on behalf of
  another guild, so a bug in the sharing code can't leak/corrupt a different guild's private
  roster. Ownership: whichever affected guild has a Discord-linked, guild-present account
  holding the clan's real in-game Leader/Co-Leader rank (Leader beats Co-Leader, verified beats
  unverified within a tier) is the "owner guild" (`resolve_cwl_clan_owner`, live CoC API lookup
  via the existing `coc_clan_cache.get_clan()`); unresolvable falls back to first-claimer, never
  blocks. Two trigger points call the shared orchestrator `ensure_cwl_clan_sharing`: adding a
  guest clan already claimed elsewhere (`handle_post_clan_config`, with a "already on X's
  roster — add anyway?" highlight+confirm in the Guests search) and Start Enrollment discovering
  one of its own clans is already claimed (`start_cwl_enrollment`). Both guilds get notified
  (new Hub-channel message + a DM to whichever admin actually triggered it — there's no
  addressable "guild admin list" anywhere in this bot). Owner-only eviction
  (`evict_guild_from_shared_clan`, `POST /api/cwl/shared-clan/evict`) removes another guild's
  participation without touching the shared roster itself; a new Evict button appears on
  Configure Participating Clans for the owner. Delete-season guard fixes a real data-loss risk:
  deleting a season used to be instant/unconditional and would have cascade-wiped a shared
  clan's roster out from under the other guild — now it repoints ownership (if the deleting
  guild was the owner) and preserves the shared roster whenever another guild remains attached,
  only actually deleting the shared record when the deleting guild was the last one left; the
  delete confirmation dialog now warns which clan(s)/guild(s) are affected first.
  Live merge (the actual "editing from either guild affects both"): `_build_enrollment_payload`
  sources a shared clan's roster_size from the OWNER's settings and its player pool from
  `cwl_shared_clan_players` instead of the per-guild tables; the signup-confirm and drag-and-drop
  assign endpoints branch the same way on write. `qapbot/QBdiscocmdshelper_cwl.py`,
  `qapbot/web_bridge.py`, `qapbot/ui_cwl_roster.py`, `qapbot/db_manager.py`. New Worker routes
  in `activity/server/src/index.ts`. Frontend: `clanConfigTable.ts` highlights an already-shared
  search hit and confirms before adding, shows a shared badge + owner-only Evict button per row.
  Tests: 40+ new across `tests/unit/test_cwl_clan_ownership.py` (new file — ownership
  resolution, orchestrator, delete-guard, eviction), `tests/unit/test_db_manager_cwl_shared_clans.py`
  (new file — full CRUD for the 3 new tables), `tests/discord/test_web_bridge.py` (search

  its self-exit harmless. Verified live: a hard `kill -9` of `cloudflared`'s own PID triggered an

  narrative and the supervisor script in `qapbot/docs/CWL_CLAN_CONFIG_ACTIVITY_PLAN.md` (Phase D)
  and `activity/README.md` ("Supervise it" step).

2026-08-14 (10)
- Fixed (`repair_history_schema_drift.py`, caught immediately from live user feedback): the
  default ("dry run") mode built the full `<table>_repaired` copy for real — writing real data
  and growing `history.db` by multiple GB — even without `--apply`. "Dry run" must mean
  literally zero bytes written, not "doesn't rename the originals". Redesigned into three
  explicit stages: (no flags, default) **preview** — 100% read-only, samples what the repair
  would produce via a live `SELECT`-only column remap against the original table, creates or
  writes nothing at all; **`--build`** — actually builds `<table>_repaired` for real (the only
  stage that writes substantial data) and verifies it, still never touching the original table's
  name; **`--apply`** — builds if needed, verifies, and swaps. New test proves preview mode
  leaves the history DB file's size completely unchanged. 1 new test; 1795 total tests pass.

2026-08-14 (9)
- Fixed (`repair_history_schema_drift.py`, caught on the first real run): building
  `<table>_repaired` was one giant unbatched transaction — against real `history.war_attacks`
  (tens of millions of rows) this grew the WAL file to 6.5GB+ within ~2 minutes with zero
  progress output, the same failure mode `_migrate_table_batch_by_date` was already hardened
  against after the 2026-08-01 incident, and had to be killed. Now batched (20,000 rows/commit
  by default, configurable via `--batch-size`), checkpoints every 20 batches
  (`--checkpoint-every-batches`), logs progress every batch, and resumes from `MAX(id)` already
  present in `<table>_repaired` if interrupted — safe to re-run the exact same command after a
  Ctrl+C or crash. Dry run semantics changed accordingly: it now builds `<table>_repaired` for
  real (still never touches the original table's name or values) instead of wrapping everything
  in a since-infeasible single rolled-back transaction. Also fixed a related resume-path bug the
  new resumability test caught immediately: the repaired table's `CREATE TABLE` didn't force
  `IF NOT EXISTS`, so re-running after a partial build failed outright instead of resuming.
  1 new resumability test (updated the dry-run test's assertions for the new semantics);
  1794 total tests pass.

2026-08-14 (8)
- Added: `qapbot/scripts/repair_history_schema_drift.py`, the repair tool for the hot/history
  schema-drift incident (see changelog (7) above). Detects drift per table by comparing `main`'s
  and `history`'s actual on-disk column order, builds a correctly-labeled `<table>_repaired`
  copy for any affected table, verifies it (row counts + random-sample plausibility checks —
  e.g. `war_tag` shaped like a real CoC tag, `stars` in 0-3), then swaps it in and preserves the
  original as `<table>_corrupted_backup` (never dropped). Defaults to a dry run that always
  rolls back — the DB file is provably untouched unless `--apply` is passed, and even then only
  if verification passed. `--db`/`--history-db` auto-resolve to DEV/PROD via `CONFIG.db_path`/
  `CONFIG.history_db_path`, matching the existing `run_history_migration_now.py`/
  `run_db_maintenance_now.py` ops scripts' convention. 5 new tests — including one against the
  exact real-world 11-column `war_summary` drift shape end to end, not just a simplified case.
  1793 total tests pass. **Not yet run against any real `history.db`** — written and verified
  against synthetic data only; running it for real (DEV first) is a separate, deliberate next
  step.

2026-08-14 (7)
- Fixed (CRITICAL — hot/history DB schema drift, found while investigating why the CWL board's
  player-skill score returned nothing): `main.war_attacks`/`war_summary` and
  `history.war_attacks`/`war_summary` had silently diverged in physical column order — same
  column names, different `cid` positions, because each schema's columns were added via
  separate `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` sequences over the project's history and `CREATE TABLE IF
  NOT EXISTS` never retroactively reorders an existing table. The monthly hot→history migration
  used a bare `SELECT *`, which matches by position, not name — so every row ever migrated had
  ~11-15 trailing columns (including `stars`, `date`, and `war_tag`) silently written into the
  wrong destination column, for the entire lifetime of the history DB, with no error at any
  point. `cwl_league_groups`/`cwl_league_rounds` (the other two migrated tables) were checked
  and are NOT affected. Fix: both migration functions now build an explicit, named column list
  at runtime (new `_explicit_column_list()`) instead of `SELECT *` — stops any further
  corruption immediately; a genuine future schema divergence now fails loudly instead of
  silently misaligning. New Cardinal Rule 1 in `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (hot/history
  schemas must never drift; existing rules renumbered 2-16) plus a full incident writeup in
  `qapbot/docs/DATABASE_ARCHITECTURE.md`. 2 new regression tests proving the fix survives a

2026-08-09 (36)
- Fixed: a real PROD-startup crash discovered during CWL_CLAN_CONFIG_ACTIVITY_PLAN.md Phase D
  (PROD rollout) — enabling Activities in the Developer Portal for the PROD application
  auto-creates a global `PRIMARY_ENTRY_POINT` command (type 4, the "launch" command), which
  `discord.py` 2.7.1 has zero awareness of. The bot's global command sync
  (`bot.tree.sync(guild=None)`) does a bulk overwrite that omits it, which Discord now rejects
  outright (HTTP 400, error code 50240: "You cannot remove this app's Entry Point command in a
  bulk update operation") instead of silently deleting it — `setup_hook` raised, uncaught, and
  the whole PROD process exited on startup. The same restriction hit `_clear_global_commands_after_ready`'s
  DEV-app cleanup path too (already non-fatal there, but silently failing to actually clear
  anything, since the DEV app also has Activities/an Entry Point command enabled since Phase A).
  Fixed with a new `bulk_sync_global_commands()` helper (`qapbot/discord_health.py`) that fetches
  the app's current global commands via a raw HTTP call, filters for any existing Entry Point
  command, and always re-includes it verbatim in the bulk-upsert payload — used in place of
  `tree.sync(guild=None)` at both call sites in `QapBot.py`. 3 new tests in
  `tests/discord/test_discord_health.py` (entry point preserved alongside tree commands, no-op
  when none exists, preserved even when clearing everything else) — 1636 total tests pass.

  typed-in earlier date, or an earlier time-of-day on the boundary day itself, can't slip
  through either.
  (2) Moved the Discord-side season select above the action buttons (was below) and gave it a
  static "Select CWL season:" caption — achieved by never marking an option as the select's
  default, so its placeholder always shows instead of the current value (which the embed's own
  "Season **{season}** — {status}" header already displays, so nothing is lost).

  (1) The Activity now actually closes itself after a successful Save. Earlier I'd concluded

  entirely, silently discarding its roster_size/cwl_start_at — reactivating it later (even
  within the same edit session on the Discord-side CwlEventSetupView) reset it to defaults.
  Root cause: "row exists" was the only signal for "participating," so deactivating had no way
  to remember anything about a clan except by keeping it as if still active. Added an explicit
  participating column to cwl_event_clans (idempotent migration for existing DBs) — a
  deactivated clan now keeps its row (and settings) with participating=0 instead of being
  deleted. Fixed in the data layer (set_cwl_event_clans_sync/get_previous_cwl_event_clans_sync,
  the latter still correctly excluding non-participating rows from next-season carry-over),

  start-time debug check) now explicitly filters to participating=1, since the raw row set can
  contain deactivated-but-remembered clans too.

  carry-over still excludes non-participating; 1 bridge: full deactivate/reactivate cycle
