2026-08-09 (18)
- Fixed: /leaderboard's own-player ANSI highlight rendered as literal garbage escape-code text
  ("[1;33mQaplop...[0m") in the second and later Discord messages whenever a DM leaderboard's
  output was long enough to split into multiple messages — worked fine on the first message, and
  worked fine in a guild channel regardless of length. Root cause: guild-mode posting
  (post_leaderboard_to_discord -> _split_and_post_leaderboard_helper, QBhelperfunctions.py) has
  always been ```ansi-fence-aware when splitting long content, but the DM path (send_and_track ->
  _split_message_into_chunks, QBdiscocmdshelper.py — the generic splitter, newly exercised by
  leaderboard's Phase 0b DM conversion) was not: it stripped exactly 3 chars off each end of a
  ```ansi\n...``` block, leaving "ansi\n" embedded as ordinary text in chunk 1 and silently
  dropping the ```ansi fence tag from every chunk after the first, so Discord rendered those
  later chunks' embedded ANSI color codes as raw, visible escape characters instead of applying
  them as formatting. Fixed by having _split_message_into_chunks detect and strip a leading
  "ansi\n" fence-language tag once, then re-prepend it to every split chunk's opening fence — a
  known, explicitly-flagged limitation from the original leaderboard DM conversion ((15)) that
  turned out to actually matter once a real multi-message DM leaderboard was posted. Non-ansi
  code blocks (the common case — /status, /list, /subscriptions, etc.) are unaffected.
  Files: qapbot/QBdiscocmdshelper.py, tests/discord/test_discord_helper_phase3.py.
  1573 tests pass (.\run_tests.ps1).

2026-08-09 (17)
- Fixed: four issues found while actually exercising Phase 0's DM commands live on the deployed
  bot (third follow-up to Phase 0b, (14)/(15)/(16), CWL_ROSTER_PLANNING_PLAN.md):
  (1) /subscriptions server_wide is now forced True whenever interaction.guild is None (including
  when the caller doesn't pass it, its own default is False) — "the current channel" is the DM
  itself in a DM, never a meaningful subscription scope.
  (2) /whois (both context menus and the slash command) is now DM-invokable. _whois_logic()'s
  interaction.guild.get_member(user.id) call turned out to be purely cosmetic (guild
  nickname/avatar override) with an already-working fallback for member=None — the actual blocker
  was a separate, unnecessary "if not interaction.guild: reject" guard sitting above that
  fallback. whois_slash's user parameter changed from Optional[discord.Member] to
  Optional[discord.User] — Member-typed options can't resolve outside a guild; _whois_logic()
  already accepted Union[discord.User, discord.Member]. Note: this does broaden who can be looked
  up from a DM (no longer implicitly scoped to "someone in a shared server") — worth a deliberate
  look if that scoping was ever load-bearing.
  (3) /leaderboard's and /analyse cwl_league_group's/cwl_opponent's clan= autocomplete previously
  keyed off the single interaction.guild_id (always None in a DM), so with no search text typed
  yet it silently returned nothing. get_clan_family_autocomplete_choices() (QBdiscocmdshelper.py)
  gained a guild_ids: Optional[List[str]] parameter for its "guild_first" mode to union clans
  across multiple guilds; a new get_dm_caller_matched_guild_ids() helper (factored out of
  resolve_guild_context() — same guild-matching logic, minus the interactive
  single-guild-or-picker resolution autocomplete handlers can't await) supplies the full list in
  a DM, so these three autocompletes now offer the union of clans across every guild the caller
  is linked to instead of nothing.
  (4) The "Ignoring exception in autocomplete... Unknown interaction (10062)" ERROR discord.py
  logs internally on every fast-typing autocomplete race (benign, already self-suppressed by
  discord.py — "can't be handled anyway") became newly visible once autocomplete-bearing commands
  like /list became DM-reachable. Suppressing it the way the pre-existing _DiscordReconnectFilter
  suppresses "Attempting a reconnect" surfaced that neither filter actually worked: both were
  registered via logging.getLogger('discord').addFilter(...), but the messages originate from
  child loggers (discord.client, discord.app_commands.tree) — Python's Logger.callHandlers()
  walks ancestor HANDLERS during propagation, not ancestor LOGGER filters, so a parent logger's
  own addFilter() never fires for a child's records. Fixed by attaching both filters to the
  actual handler objects instead.
  Files: QBdiscordcmds.py, qapbot/QBdiscocmdshelper.py, QapBot.py,
  tests/discord/test_dm_command_invocation.py.
  1571 tests pass (.\run_tests.ps1).

- Fixed: mid-season CWL tracking abandonment (entry 2026-08-08 (5)'s bug) was regrowing after
  being backfilled to 0. `repromote_mid_season_clans.py` was run on prod 2026-08-08 and confirmed
  down to 0 clans; a dry-run against the next day's prod backup found 2,332 fresh occurrences.
  Root cause: the 2026-08-08 guard (`clan_has_cwl_data_for_season()`) only blocks a demotion *at
  the moment it's evaluated* — a clan correctly demoted while it had zero season data can still
  pick up archived `war_summary` rows later the same season via `CWL-GROUP-EXPAND` (`QapBot.py`,
  ~line 1049), which force-fetches every member of any group containing an actively-tracked clan
  every cycle, independent of the fetched clan's own `track_war_updates`. That lands the clan back
  in the "demoted mid-season with partial data" bucket as a brand-new instance — and since its
  league itself never changed, `_sync_group_track_war_updates()`'s demotion-transition branch never
  re-runs to catch it. Fix: `_sync_group_track_war_updates()` (`qapbot/cache_manager.py`) now also
  checks, unconditionally for any non-subscribed clan currently `track_war_updates=False` and still
  correctly below Master III (no league mismatch), whether it already has season data — if so,
  force-promotes it back to `track_war_updates=True` for the rest of the season, self-healing
  instead of requiring another manual `repromote_mid_season_clans.py` run. The existing guard check
  was extracted into a shared `_clan_has_cwl_data_for_season_safe()` helper (same False-on-error
  fallback for both the demotion guard and the new self-heal check). Note: this only re-evaluates
  when the clan's group is next resolved via `get_league_group()` (Layer 1/2), not immediately when
  `CWL-GROUP-EXPAND` archives the row, so a regrown clan can still sit un-healed for a while — just
  no longer permanently. Documented in `qapbot/docs/CWL_ROUND_TRACKING_PLAN.md` and
  `qapbot/docs/CLAN_WAR_TRACKING.md` (write-path 7). Added 2 tests
  (tests/unit/test_cwl_league_rank_new_group_gate.py). File changed: qapbot/cache_manager.py.
  1521 tests pass (.\run_tests.ps1).

  players. Root cause: generate_cwl_group_analysis_embeds() fetches the CWL
  group's wars LIVE from the CoC API on every call (not from the local DB —

  report: running the command back-to-back on DEV and PROD, against a
  database backup confirmed byte-identical between the two, consistently
  (not randomly) showed 20 vs 24 of 28 group wars — DEV and PROD each log in

  COC_API_EMAIL), and the leading (unconfirmed) hypothesis is per-key/region

  wars. Fix: (1) log every failed/empty per-war fetch (coc.NotFound was
  previously not logged at all, in coc_retry()), (2) retry any war that came

  also recovers partial data from wars still in progress). Any war still

2026-08-08 (31)
- Fixed: Entries 29/30's fixes for /analyse league_group's RTL scrambling also
  had no effect live (confirmed identical on Discord desktop and iOS). Root-
  caused precisely this time by comparing a real browser render of the exact
  generated string against the row's actual raw text (copied out of Discord
  by the user) and the screenshot's visual output side by side: the raw text
  Discord stores is byte-for-byte correct in logical order — this was never
  a text-construction bug — but the DISPLAYED order was an exact mirror of
  the entire "player · clan → ⭐ total" span (both names swapped relative
  order AND the trailing "→ ⭐ total" jumped to before them), stopping only
  at "(atk info)" because that's unambiguous Latin text. That signature means
  Discord is merging everything from the RTL name through the arrow/star/
  total into ONE contiguous RTL run and reversing it as a block. Neither
  entry 29's FSI/PDI isolates (Discord doesn't respect Unicode bidi isolate
  characters at all — confirmed independently: even the python-bidi
  reference library throws on them, they're a newer/less-supported feature)
  nor entry 30's single leading LRM (only anchors the very start of the
  line — does nothing to stop RTL absorption of content *after* the names)
  addressed the actual mechanism.
  Fix: found and matched the ALREADY-WORKING pattern elsewhere in this same
  file — the CWL round-lines "vs. [opponent](url) `TAG`" builder (fixed
  previously, see the "#2TAG rendering as 2#TAG" entry earlier in this log)
  uses plain LRM (not isolates) bracketed around the name AND a second bare,
  non-bracketed LRM placed directly in the literal separator text right
  before the next field. Applied the exact same two-part pattern to
  QBhelperfunctions.py's CWL group analyse row builder (both the attackers
  and defenders loops): normalize_player_name() (qapbot/formatting.py)
  reverted from FSI/PDI back to plain LRM bracketing, and a bare "‎" was
  added at the START of each row and after player_link/clan_link — i.e.
  immediately before every " · " and " → " transition, matching the proven
  "vs. [LRM{name}LRM](url)  LRM`{tag}`" structure exactly. Updated the two
  RTL-marker unit tests in test_formatting_modes.py back to asserting on
  LRM. Corrected the qapbot/docs/CODE_STRUCTURE.md note (previously
  recommended isolates) to describe the two-part LRM pattern and point at
  both reference implementations for future RTL-name embedding.

2026-08-08 (30)
- Fixed: Entry 29's FSI/PDI isolate fix for /analyse league_group turned out to
  be necessary but not sufficient — user retested live in Discord after a
  restart and rows with Arabic names still scrambled identically. Diagnosed
  with a side-by-side browser test (real Chromium, same rendering family as
  Discord desktop/web): a plain browser renders the row CORRECTLY even with
  NO direction marks at all, because a browser only ever reorders text within
  the paragraph direction it's given, which defaults to LTR unless something
  requests auto-detection. Discord's client must be auto-detecting a per-line
  RTL/LTR direction from the line's first strong-direction character, and
  that scan does not respect FSI/PDI isolate boundaries — it still "sees"
  the Arabic name inside the isolate and flips the whole row's layout
  (medal/star/arrow position), even though the name's own internal character
  order is correctly isolated.
  Fix: prepend a bare, non-isolated LRM (U+200E) as the literal first
  character of each attacker/defender row string in QBhelperfunctions.py
  (before _rank_label(rank)), so Discord's line-direction scan finds LTR
  immediately, before it ever reaches the isolate. This is the same technique
  (LRM placed directly in the line, not just wrapped around a name) that
  already fixed the narrower "#TAG renders as TAG#" bug noted earlier in this
  changelog — applied here at the whole-row scope because this row has more
  content after the RTL name that also needs protecting from the flip.
  The FSI/PDI isolation from entry 29 is kept (still correct for the name's
  own internal RTL word order); this is an additive fix, not a revert.

2026-08-08 (29)
- Fixed: /analyse league_group embeds ("Best Attackers · CWL Group" /
  "Best Defenders · CWL Group") scrambled the display order of rows for
  clans/players with Arabic (or other RTL-script) names — the RTL name would
  visually swap position with, or absorb, neighboring LTR punctuation like
  the "·" separator, "→", markdown link parens, and medal/TH emoji.
  Root cause: qapbot/formatting.py normalize_player_name() wrapped detected
  RTL text with plain LRM (U+200E) marks. LRM is only a weak directional
  hint — it does not stop the bidi algorithm from letting the embedded RTL
  run influence how *surrounding* neutral characters in the same line get
  reordered, which is exactly what these embed lines are full of (multiple
  markdown-linked names + symbols on one row).
  Fix: wrap RTL runs with proper Unicode bidi isolates instead — FSI
  (U+2068, First Strong Isolate) ... PDI (U+2069, Pop Directional Isolate).
  Isolates make the wrapped run opaque to the outer LTR context (so it can't
  perturb neighboring punctuation/emoji ordering) while still rendering the
  RTL text in its own natural right-to-left order internally. Both marks are
  Unicode category Cf (zero-width), so text_display_width()'s existing
  ZERO_WIDTH_CATS handling already ignores them — no width/alignment impact
  on the ASCII-table code paths that also call normalize_player_name().
  Updated tests/unit/test_formatting_modes.py's two RTL-marker tests to
  assert on FSI/PDI instead of the old LRM mark. Documented the convention
  in qapbot/docs/CODE_STRUCTURE.md so future RTL-name embedding uses
  isolates, not manual LRM wrapping (QBhelperfunctions.py still has several
  pre-existing manual LRM-wrapped-name patterns for other embeds — those
  weren't reported broken and were left alone, but carry the same
  weak-LRM-mark limitation and are candidates for the same fix later).

- Fixed: found and fixed a real bug while investigating the above — every single [GC-AUTO] log line
  in prod appeared as an exact near-duplicate pair (same collected= count, timestamps a few ms
  apart). Root cause: QBdiscordcmds.py has a module-level `from QapBot import GLOBAL_GUILD_ID,
  run_nightly_maintenance_routine, is_monthly_migration_due`. Since QapBot.py runs as `__main__`
  (not under the module name "QapBot"), that import causes Python to load and fully re-execute
  QapBot.py a SECOND time under the name "QapBot" — running every top-level statement (imports,
  logging setup, the gc.callbacks.append(...) call) twice. The `if __name__ == "__main__":` guard
  correctly stops the second execution from starting a second bot connection, and `@QBcore.bot.event`
  decorators are safe by accident (setattr-overwrite semantics), but `gc.callbacks.append(...)`
  isn't idempotent — each execution's closure is a distinct object, so the list ends up with two
  entries that both fire on every real automatic collection. Fixed with a name-based (not
  identity-based) dedup guard before the append. Root cause (the circular import) left alone —
  a real fix needs moving those 3 names to a neutral shared module, which is a bigger, separate
  change. Documented as Pitfall 22 in qapbot/docs/COPILOT_PITFALLS_COOKBOOK.md and cardinal-rules
  item 21 in .github/copilot-instructions.md, since any future module-level code near the top of
  QapBot.py that mutates shared state (not just def/class/import) needs the same guard.
- Verified: zero ERROR/CRITICAL/Traceback/10062 entries across the full ~26,300-line session
  (last restart through nightly maintenance through 3 update cycles). Both post-maintenance
  cycles completed normally; RSS memory stayed in a normal ~3.1-3.3GB range.

  the whole operation failed. Root cause: on_submit never deferred, so the FIRST response to the
  interaction was whatever came after verify_and_update_player() (CoC API round-trip) +
  assign_member_role() + sync_roles_for_user() (Discord role sync) — routinely exceeding

  found) and before the slow verify+role-sync work, then using followup.send() for every
  subsequent reply (success-with-notifications-check, success-into-AccountManagementView-refresh,
  and verification-failed) instead of response.send_message(). Updated
  tests/discord/test_ui_registration_phase13.py's two VerifyAccountModal tests to match the new
  deferred/followup behavior.
- Fixed: diagnosed why [GC-AUTO] gen-2 pauses (added in changelog (20)'s diagnostic logger) were
  still firing in prod (5.45s pauses, collected=6162) despite the startup gc.freeze() from that
  same fix. Root cause: gc.freeze() only froze the CACHE baseline that existed at startup; every
  cycle since then has promoted new long-lived growth (new clans, new war metadata — substantial
  during the current CWL season, e.g. 7000+ active wars) into gen-2, which automatic sweeps still
  have to walk in full since it was never frozen. Fix (QapBot.py run_nightly_maintenance_routine,
  new Step 5): during the nightly maintenance window (Discord commands already blocked via
  db_maintenance_mode) — gc.unfreeze() + a real, unscoped gc.collect() (catches any genuine
  reference cycles that the per-cycle scoped gc.collect(1) intentionally skips every single time,
  so they need SOME real collection point or they'd become permanent floating garbage once
  re-frozen) + gc.freeze() again, folding that day's legitimate CACHE growth back into the
  permanent generation so tomorrow's automatic sweeps stay cheap. Offloaded via asyncio.to_thread
  (heartbeat-safety only, per Pitfall 16 — not a claim that gc.collect() itself is non-blocking);
  best-effort, logged but never fails the maintenance run. Also examined the reported single
  18.88s [COC-API-SLOW] get_clan() pause (no burst of concurrent calls this time, unlike the
  original incident) — evidence is consistent with the same automatic-gen-2-sweep phenomenon, though
  unconfirmed since the dev machine has no access to the live prod log to check for a co-occurring
  [GC-AUTO] line. By contrast, the per-cycle NOTIFY-TIMING gap reported alongside it is NOT a
  hidden block — its total=3.108s exactly accounts for the full wall-clock gap between the
  surrounding log lines, reflecting real work at CWL scale (7108 active wars) that was already
  fixed to yield/run in a thread in prior sessions.

2026-08-08 (20)
- Fixed: diagnosed a live prod incident (admin's /admin command got "The application did not
  respond") to CPython's automatic (implicit) gen-2 garbage collector, not CoC API latency.
  qapbot_PROD.log showed a 7.8s stretch with zero log output immediately followed by ~20
  concurrently in-flight [COC-API-SLOW] get_clan() calls all reporting ~the same elapsed time —
  the signature of the whole process (incl. event loop + Discord heartbeat) being frozen by a
  single atomic C call, not 20 independent slow HTTPS calls finishing in sync. Confirmed systemic
  (not one-off) via `qapbot/scripts/log_time_gaps.py --top 400` over the full day: dozens of
  multi-second gaps recurring at varying positions across cycles. Root cause: the existing
  Pitfall-16 fix (_post_cycle_cleanup's gc.collect(1) instead of a full collect) only scopes the
  bot's own EXPLICIT end-of-cycle call — CPython's automatic collector is still enabled at default
  thresholds and runs real gen-2 sweeps on its own schedule, including mid-Phase-1, walking the
  entire long-lived CACHE graph (~420K clan_name_cache entries, ~6.4M player_name_index entries).
  Fix (QapBot.py): (1) registered a gc.callbacks start/stop logger near the top of the file so any
  future automatic collection ≥0.5s logs as "[GC-AUTO] Automatic gen-N collection paused the
  process for X.XXXs" instead of masquerading as API latency; (2) after CACHE.load_all() completes
  at startup, run one full gc.collect() then gc.freeze() to move the startup CACHE baseline into
  gc's permanent generation, which automatic sweeps never scan — future automatic collections then
  only walk genuinely new post-startup churn. Both offloaded via asyncio.to_thread (one-time
  startup cost, before Phase-1/real traffic begins; per Pitfall 16 this keeps the heartbeat task
  schedulable but doesn't make the calls themselves non-blocking). Documented as Pitfall 21 in
  qapbot/docs/COPILOT_PITFALLS_COOKBOOK.md and .github/copilot-instructions.md cardinal rule #20.
  Full test suite (1523 tests) green after the change.

2026-08-08 (17)
- Fixed: entry (16)'s root-cause was INCOMPLETE — user compared prod DB against backup and
  confirmed the startup-window clicks did cause real data loss: exactly their own 5 user_players
  rows (the accounts linked to the clicking Discord user) were deleted. Corrected mechanism:
  every registration button starts with update_user_metadata_from_interaction() →
  CACHE.update_user_metadata(), which CREATED a skeleton entry {"players": []} for any user
  missing from the (not-yet-loaded) cache and write-through persisted it; save_user()/
  _save_user_impl() implements persistence as DELETE FROM user_players + reinsert-from-payload,
  so persisting the fabricated empty skeleton hard-deleted the user's real rows. The "no linked
  accounts" window the user saw was the after-image of the wipe, not a stale read.
  Hardened with three layers (entry 16's view-level fully_initialized gate remains layer 1):
  Layer 2 — new CacheManager.users_loaded flag (False until load_user_accounts() succeeds;
  class-level default False so even __init__-bypassing instances fail safe):
  update_user_metadata() now skips entirely pre-load (logs [STARTUP-GUARD], never fabricates a
  skeleton); set_user_account()/persist_user()/delete_user_account() raise RuntimeError pre-load
  — no user write-through can ever run against an unloaded cache, regardless of which future
  view/command forgets a layer-1 guard.
  Layer 3 — _save_user_impl() (db_manager.py) logs a WARNING whenever a save would replace N>0
  existing user_players rows with an EMPTY players list (legitimate only for an explicit
  last-account unlink), so any future wipe is visible in the log the moment it happens.
  New tests: tests/integration/test_cache_manager.py TestUsersLoadedDataLossGuard (5 tests,
  including a reproduction of the exact incident path asserting the DB rows survive).
  Test fixtures exercising post-startup behavior now set users_loaded=True explicitly
  (test_cache_manager.py, test_cache_coc_metadata_phase5.py, test_cache_manager_coverage.py,
  test_cache_writethrough_phase5.py, test_db_errors_phase5.py).
  Docs: Pitfall 20 rewritten with the confirmed data-loss mechanism + 3-layer fix;
  copilot-instructions.md short-list item 19 updated.
  Files: qapbot/cache_manager.py, qapbot/db_manager.py. 1517 tests pass.
  Note: the user's 5 links are being re-linked manually by the user; no data repair needed.

  buttons surviving a restart via bot.add_view()) but hit a regression: clicking an old message's

- Fixed: user found a prod log line — `[NOTIFY-TIMING] index_build=0.001s get_active_wars=15.680s

  building per in-war clan), called directly (not via asyncio.to_thread) from
  `check_wars_for_notifications()`. At CWL scale (17,302 in-war clans) this blocks the event loop
  for the full ~15.7s — no Discord heartbeat or interaction can be processed for that entire
  duration, exactly the suspected symptom.

  earlier changelog entry ("Performance: War notification check — eliminated 75-second event loop
  blockage") added it as defense-in-depth. It was later removed once the function was rewritten to
  be zero-file-I/O, on the assumption "zero I/O" also meant "fast enough to stay synchronous" — true
  at the population size measured then, not at current CWL-season scale (17k+ in-war clans).
  Fix: restored `await asyncio.to_thread(_get_active_wars)` at the call site. No signature change to
  `_get_active_wars()` itself, so no test updates were needed — confirmed via
  tests/unit/test_final_push_phase5.py's existing `patch(..., return_value=...)` mocks, which work
  transparently through `asyncio.to_thread()` since it accepts any plain sync callable.

2026-08-08 (1)
- Analysis: investigated a 43,194-war gap flagged by `qapbot/scripts/analyze_cwl_rounds.py
  --fetch-missing` for the 2026-08 CWL season. Root cause: archiving is strictly per-clan-
  perspective (one `war_summary` row per clan that was actually polled), and polling is gated by
  `track_war_updates` — a below-Master-III, non-subscribed opponent's own perspective is simply
  never fetched, so a war between a tracked and an untracked clan produces only one of its two
  rows. This is expected/by-design given the subscription-rooted tracking model, not a pipeline
  bug. Documented the mechanism (and its interaction with `process_cwl_recovery_batch()`'s own
  `track_war_updates=True` participant filter) in `CWL_ROUND_TRACKING_PLAN.md`.

2026-08-03 (7)
- Fixed: The actual primary root cause of intermittent duplicate registration messages (audited all
  11 `bot.get_channel()`/`guild.get_channel()` call sites after (6) below to look for more instances
  of the same class of bug). `repost_playerregistration_messages()` in QapBot.py runs every main
  loop cycle (bump/repost) and on channel-setting changes; in all three places it deleted the old
  tracked message with a blanket `except Exception: pass` (or, for the disable/channel-change
  cases, via a helper that silently did nothing on a `get_channel()` cache miss) and then
  unconditionally proceeded — posting a brand-new message, or clearing the tracked message ID —
  regardless of whether the old message was actually confirmed gone. Any transient failure
  (rate limit, network blip, permissions hiccup, cache-miss) during the delete step therefore left
  the old message alive while a new one got created/tracked on top of it — the visible "registration
  message shows up a 2nd time" symptom. Fixed by only treating a delete/channel-lookup as confirmed
  when Discord actually says so (`discord.NotFound`, or a `fetch_channel()` fallback confirming the
  channel is gone); any other outcome now skips reposting / keeps the old tracking for a retry next
  cycle instead of risking a duplicate. Also applied the same `get_channel()`-miss-≠-deleted fix to
  `cleanup_stale_ui_messages()` (startup `/clan_management` panel cleanup) for consistency, though
  that one leaks an orphaned panel rather than duplicating messages (no repost happens there).
  Documented as Pitfall 15 in qapbot/docs/COPILOT_PITFALLS_COOKBOOK.md.
  Files: QapBot.py.

2026-08-03 (6)
- Fixed: Likely root cause of intermittent duplicate messages (e.g. registration messages
  occasionally appearing a 2nd time). `/admin Cleanup Messages All`'s per-channel resolution used
  `bot.get_channel()` (a local-cache lookup) and treated any miss as "channel deleted", purging that
  channel's tracked message IDs from `CACHE.leaderboard_messages`. A cache miss isn't proof of
  deletion though — it can also happen on a transient gateway/cache gap — so a still-live channel's
  cache entry could get purged, causing the bot to post a brand-new message next time instead of
  recognizing the old one still exists. `handle_cleanup_messages_all()`'s `_cleanup_one()` in
  qapbot/QBdiscocmdshelper_admin_command.py now falls back to a live `bot.fetch_channel()` API call
  on a cache miss (skipped in dev mode as before) and only purges the cache entries on a confirmed
  `discord.NotFound`; any other outcome (`Forbidden`, `HTTPException`, network error, etc.) leaves
  the cache untouched and retries on the next run.
  Files: qapbot/QBdiscocmdshelper_admin_command.py.

2026-08-01 (9)
- Added: fast bulk history migration mode, for clearing a large backlog dramatically faster than
  the routine batched path. Root cause of the ~900-1000 rows/sec ceiling observed during tonight's
  incident recovery (despite the data being only ~10 GB, which should copy in minutes on SSD):
  `war_attacks` carries 5 secondary indexes on each schema plus a UNIQUE constraint — every row
  moved was paying 12 B-tree updates (6 inserting into history, 6 deleting from main), and that
  per-row index-maintenance cost, not disk I/O, was the actual bottleneck.
  New `WarHistoryDB.fast_bulk_history_migration()`: temporarily drops war_attacks' 5 secondary
  indexes on BOTH schemas (never the UNIQUE constraint, which INSERT OR IGNORE's idempotency
  depends on), moves data in large single-commit chunks (default 1M rows, still individually
  checkpointed) instead of 5000-row batches, then rebuilds every dropped index in one efficient
  bulk pass. Indexes are always rebuilt in a finally block even on a mid-run error. Strictly
  requires the bot to be stopped (drops main.war_attacks' own query indexes for the duration,
  unlike the routine path which never touches main's indexes).
  New CLI flag: `run_history_migration_now.py --fast [--fast-chunk-size N]`.
  Files: qapbot/db_manager.py, qapbot/scripts/run_history_migration_now.py,
  tests/unit/test_fast_bulk_history_migration.py (new, 4 tests). 1478 tests pass.

2026-08-01 (5)
- Fixed: a continuously-running bot would NOT automatically advance a chunked history migration one
  night at a time as expected — it would only ever auto-fire the migration ONCE per calendar month

  in-memory once-per-process claim. Found by directly answering an operator's question during the

  via `_maint_due`. The rare standalone safety-net fallback deliberately keeps the default (claiming)
  check, since it has no other throttle and bypassing it too would make it re-fire every ~5-minute
  cycle instead.
  Net effect: a bot left running now genuinely completes a large migration backlog one bounded chunk
  per night, fully unattended, on top of the `/admin`-triggered manual option from earlier today.

2026-07-30 (6)
- Fixed (final): reworked bot startup ordering instead of special-casing the composite-index
  build again. (5) below deferred `idx_wa_player_tag_date` creation to `nightly_db_maintenance()`
  to avoid the "database is locked" storm from (4) — technically correct, but it meant a fresh
  deploy wouldn't get the leaderboard perf benefit until the next nightly run (or a manual
  `/admin Optimize DB`), and split "ensure schema is correct" across two places for one index.
  Root insight: the *only* reason building this index inline was ever unsafe was that other code
  was already writing to the DB concurrently (PHASE-1 clan fetches) by the time it ran. Fix that
  at the source: sequence DB init strictly BEFORE anything else can touch the DB, not around it.
  - Added `QapBot.initialize_database()`: calls `WarHistoryDB.initialize()` under its own generous
    30-minute `asyncio.wait_for` (not the 60s CoC-login one) and sets
    `QBcore.db_maintenance_mode=True` for the duration (same flag `nightly_db_maintenance()` uses
    — blocks Discord commands with the existing friendly message; Discord's gateway connection is
    already up by `on_ready()`, so the bot still shows online).
  - `on_ready()` now calls this as a new "Step 1.5", strictly before Step 2 (CoC login) and before
    `periodic_main()` can start — so nothing else in the app can be writing to the DB while a rare
    first-run schema migration builds. `startup_login()` no longer does DB init at all (split
    cleanly into auth-only).
  - `idx_wa_player_tag_date` moved back inline into `_create_schema()`/`_create_history_schema()`
    (main + history) — same as any other index, now safe because of the ordering above, not
    because of any special-casing. Every restart after the first is a cheap IF-NOT-EXISTS check;
    logs the build time only when it exceeds 5s so a normal restart stays quiet.
  - Removed `nightly_db_maintenance()`'s "Step 1.5" create-if-missing block from (5) — redundant
    now that `initialize()` always ensures it exists; maintenance's existing REINDEX-if-exists
    loop (which already includes `idx_wa_player_tag_date` in `major_indexes`) is enough.
  - `_create_history_schema_sync()`'s `build_expensive_indexes` flag stays (defensive: pool-fill
    runs synchronously on the event-loop thread and must never attempt this build itself, even
    though in the current ordering `_create_schema()`/`_create_history_schema()` always beat it to it).
  Files: QapBot.py, qapbot/db_manager.py.

2026-07-30 (5) — SUPERSEDED by (6) above, kept for the incident trail
- Fixed: the background-task fix in (4) below solved the startup timeout but caused a worse,
  live incident — right after the fixed bot came up, PHASE-1's clan-fetch writes started failing
  with "database is locked" (`[DB-WRITE-THROUGH] Failed to persist clan ...`), because
  `CREATE INDEX` holds SQLite's single writer lock for its *entire* build duration regardless of
  which thread runs it. `asyncio.to_thread` only kept the build off the event loop — it did
  nothing to stop it from blocking every other write in the app for however long the build took.
  There is no way to make a large `CREATE INDEX` non-blocking for other writers in SQLite; the
  only real question is whether that lock window is coordinated or not.
  Fix: removed the fire-and-forget background task entirely.
  `initialize()` now only does a cheap read-only existence check and logs a warning if the index
  is missing (`_warn_if_composite_index_missing()`) — never a write. The actual `CREATE INDEX` was
  moved into `nightly_db_maintenance()`'s existing Step 2 (new "Step 1.5"), which already
  `self._pool.drain()`s (waits out in-flight writers, blocks new ones with a clean
  `RuntimeError` instead of a raw `OperationalError`) and sets `QBcore.db_maintenance_mode=True`
  (blocks Discord commands) before touching anything — the one place in this codebase a
  multi-minute exclusive write is already coordinated and safe. Runs automatically on the next
  scheduled nightly maintenance, or immediately via `/admin Optimize DB` /
  `qapbot/scripts/run_db_maintenance_now.py` if you don't want to wait.
  Removed `WarHistoryDB._build_composite_indexes_background()` and the now-unused
  `_composite_index_build_task` attribute from (4).
  Files: qapbot/db_manager.py.
  Docs: qapbot/docs/DATABASE_ARCHITECTURE.md.
  Tests: 1467 passed (up from 1464; +3 net new — replaced the background-task test with one
  proving initialize() builds nothing, plus one proving nightly_db_maintenance() does).
  pyright: 0 errors.

2026-07-30 (4) — SUPERSEDED by (5) above, kept for the incident trail
- Fixed: bot failed to start on prod ("Startup login timed out after 60 seconds") — a direct
  regression from (3) below. `idx_wa_player_tag_date` was created inline inside
  `_create_schema()`/`_create_history_schema()`, awaited directly inside `initialize()`, which
  itself runs inside `startup_login()`'s 60s login timeout. Its FIRST build on the multi-
  million-row prod `history.war_attacks` table is a full table scan + sort that takes minutes,
  not seconds — every restart after the first would have been instant (`IF NOT EXISTS` is a
  cheap check), but that first build alone blew the login budget and the bot never came up.
  Fix: stopped building this index inline on the awaited startup path entirely. Added
  `WarHistoryDB._build_composite_indexes_background()`, scheduled via `asyncio.create_task`
  (fire-and-forget, NOT awaited) at the end of `initialize()` — builds the index on a dedicated
  `sqlite3` connection via `asyncio.to_thread`, using the same server-machine-safe pragmas as
  `run_nightly_maintenance()` (temp_store=FILE, 128 MB cache — avoids the OOM-kill risk of the
  hot-path pragmas' 8 GB mmap during a large external sort). Also added a
  `build_expensive_indexes` flag to `_create_history_schema_sync()` (the sync/pool-fill helper),
  defaulting True for tests/migrations but passed False from `_SyncConnectionPool._create_conn()`
  — pool-fill runs synchronously on the event-loop thread, so it must never attempt this build
  itself (that would freeze the whole process, not just time out a coroutine). Until the
  background build finishes, scope="all" leaderboard queries simply fall back to the slower
  `idx_wa_player_tag` single-column index — a temporary perf cost, never a correctness issue.
  Files: qapbot/db_manager.py.
  Docs: qapbot/docs/DATABASE_ARCHITECTURE.md.
  Tests: 1466 passed (up from 1464; +2 new). pyright: 0 errors.

2026-07-30 (3)
- Fixed: `/leaderboard` with the new `scope="all"` default took minutes to respond on prod
  instead of the sub-second DB query expected. Two causes, both fixed:
  1. `get_player_attack_history_sync()`'s `player_tag IN (...) AND date BETWEEN ...` query only
     had a single-column `idx_wa_player_tag` index to work with, so SQLite had to rowid-fetch
     every historical row for each player (across all time) just to filter down to one month.
     Added composite index `idx_wa_player_tag_date(player_tag, date)` (kept the old single-column
     index rather than dropping it — DROP INDEX on the ~5.6M-row war_attacks table is nightly-
     maintenance-only, never safe to run unconditionally at every connection open/startup).
  2. The real dominant cost: `QBdiscordcmds.leaderboard()` resolved scope="all" rosters by
     `await`ing `CACHE.coc_clan_cache.get_clan()` one clan at a time in a for-loop. With no
     clan/family filter (the common case — a channel's full set of subscribed clans/families),
     a cache miss/expiry means a live CoC API call per clan, sequentially — that's what actually
     produced the multi-minute delay. Switched to a single `asyncio.gather(...,
     return_exceptions=True)` batch across every distinct constituent clan (same pattern already
     used by ui_clan_management.py's guild-clan refresh).
  Files: qapbot/db_manager.py (composite index ×3 schema sites + major_indexes REINDEX list),
  QBdiscordcmds.py (parallel roster gather).
  Docs: qapbot/docs/DATABASE_ARCHITECTURE.md.

  code block instead of a plain ` ``` ` block. Plain code blocks ignore all markdown/ANSI, and

2026-07-26 (17)
- Added: `evaluate-promo-rules` subcommand to `qapbot/scripts/audit_cwl_league_rank.py` —
  empirically measures real CWL promotion/demotion counts per league (Supercell has never
  published these). For every fully-ranked, complete-data 8-clan group in a season whose
  league_rank is already known-correct, compares each clan's final rank against its CURRENT
  live league (fetched right after that season's promotions applied), aggregated per
  (league, rank) across the whole season for real sample sizes instead of 1-2 examples.
  Findings from season 2026-07 (26,467 groups; see `changelog.txt` (12)-(15) for why
  league_rank is trustworthy ground truth for this season specifically):
  - Gold League I through Champion League III: huge samples (hundreds to 5,000+ clans per
    league) cleanly confirm the existing (2, 2) assumption at ~100% consistency.
  - **Corrected** `_CWL_PROMO_RULES_FROM_2026_05["Champion League I"]` from (2, 2) to (4, 1)
    — n=66, unambiguous: ranks 1-4 100% promoted, ranks 5-7 ~89% unchanged, only rank 8
    (~89%) demoted, not the bottom two. Matches the two "disagreement" examples investigated
    with the project owner just before this.
  - **Left unchanged, genuinely inconclusive** (not a code fix — needs more data over time):
    Titan League I/II/III and Legend League show a much messier signal than every other
    league — even top-ranked clans show only a ~35/65 split between promoted and unchanged
    (every other league is ~100/0 at its rank boundary). Initially read this as "doesn't
    follow a rank-based model at all" (e.g. a broader trophy/medal-pool mechanic like Legend
    League's own global system) — walked that back after the project owner pointed out a
    simpler explanation and cross-checking confirmed it's plausible: 97.8% of these groups'
    recorded league_rank was never independently verified by `reconstruct` (all fell into
    "disagreement" under the old, too-conservative safe-rank band) — but that alone doesn't
    prove it, since Champion League I *also* had a 0% confirmation rate yet still gave a
    clean (4, 1) signal. Titan/Legend is a small, rarely-independently-verified population,
    so pre-fix historical corruption has had the most opportunity to accumulate there
    uncorrected — the likelier explanation, but not provable from today's data alone. Left

2026-07-26 (15)
- Fixed: root-cause fix for the CWL league_rank bug (7)/(11)/(12)/(13)/(14), replacing the
  `.state`-based gate with a correct-by-construction one. Prompted by the project owner asking
  why this happened in the first place and pointing out the actual fix: a league group's
  members are, by definition, all in the same league the moment the group is first discovered
  — so league_rank only ever needs deriving once, at that moment, using whichever member's
  cache is already fresh or (cheaply) one targeted get_clan() call if none are.
  The real defect: `cache_manager._process_league_group_response` had no notion of "first time
  seeing this group" vs. "re-processing an already-recorded one" — the same "trust any member's
  current league" logic ran on *every* fresh get_league_group() response, gated only on whether
  the API's live `.state` currently reported the season as active. That gate worked but treated
  a symptom, not the disease, and needed increasingly complex machinery (staleness windows,
  season-boundary arithmetic) to stay correct.
  Fix: added `db_manager.cwl_group_exists(group_id, cwl_season)` — a cheap indexed lookup,
  checked BEFORE `upsert_cwl_league_data` so it reflects pre-insert state. league_rank
  population (raw_data check, then fresh clan_name_cache entry, then one targeted get_clan()
  call) now only ever runs when this reports the group is genuinely new. An already-known
  group's league_rank is never touched again by this function afterwards, regardless of API
  state — update_cwl_group_stats's self-heal ((13)/(14)) remains the only other path that can
  correct it later, and only via a verified safe-rank cross-check.
  Kept the 8-day cache-staleness check on the fallback (a cached value can be stale from long
  before this brand-new group even without any season-timing concern — that's a general
  cache-freshness question, unrelated to the season-divergence bug this whole fix line was
  chasing). Removed entirely: the `.state` inspection, the season-window arithmetic, and the
  "season already ended, skipping" log line — none of it is reachable anymore since population
  never runs on an already-known group regardless of what state the API reports.
  Replaced `tests/unit/test_cwl_league_rank_season_gate.py` (tested the now-removed `.state`
  gate; 6 tests) with `tests/unit/test_cwl_league_rank_new_group_gate.py` (9 tests: new-group
  population from cache/API/raw_data, existing-group never-repopulates including the exact
  divergent-members production shape, and cwl_group_exists checked before the upsert).
  Tests: 1425 passed, 5 deselected. pyright: 0 errors.
  Files changed: qapbot/cache_manager.py (_process_league_group_response),
  qapbot/db_manager.py (cwl_group_exists new), tests/unit/test_cwl_league_rank_new_group_gate.py
  (new, replaces test_cwl_league_rank_season_gate.py), qapbot/docs/DATABASE_ARCHITECTURE.md.

2026-07-26 (14)
- Fixed: two follow-up gaps found while verifying (13)'s self-heal against real prod logs.
  1. Self-heal never got a chance to run for a group whose league_rank was *never* populated
     during its active season (still empty/NULL) — it only lived in update_cwl_group_stats'
     cwl_ended=1 short-circuit, not the initial "compute fresh" branch that first sets
     cwl_ended=1. Since the background auto-post loop (QapBot.py) skips calling
     update_cwl_group_stats again once cwl_ended is observed True, an actively-subscribed
     clan reached only through that loop would never get a second chance — league_rank would
     stay empty forever unless someone happened to run /leaderboard cwlinfo/cwlgroup manually
     for that exact clan. Fixed by factoring the self-heal application (log + persist with
     force=True + reflect in rows) into a shared `_apply_cwl_self_heal` helper and calling it
     from both branches — the short-circuit (as before) and the initial computation, right
     after all_ended is determined for the first time.
  2. `_process_league_group_response`'s "league_rank still unknown" log line (added in (7))
     was misleading: it fires purely based on THIS call's local derivation attempt coming up
     empty, regardless of whether the DB already has a correct value from earlier in the
     season (the common, harmless case) or is genuinely still empty (the rarer, real gap —
     now closed by fix 1 above). Observed on prod: "group 9457c3866f02bfcc ... league_rank
     still unknown" for a group whose league_rank was in fact already correctly "Crystal
     League III" in the DB — alarming-looking but harmless, since the guard only prevents
     *this call* from writing, it never touched the existing value. Reworded the message to
     be accurate (doesn't claim the DB value is unknown) and downgraded it from INFO to DEBUG
     since it's an expected, routine occurrence for any ended group being reprocessed, not a
     problem signal on its own.
  Added 2 tests to tests/unit/test_cwl_league_rank_self_heal.py: self-heal firing on the very
  first all_ended computation (reproduces the exact gap), and confirming it's NOT attempted
  while all_ended is still False (group_rank isn't final yet, so "safe rank" doesn't apply).
  Tests: 1422 passed, 5 deselected. pyright: 0 errors.
  Files changed: QBhelperfunctions.py (_apply_cwl_self_heal new, update_cwl_group_stats),
  qapbot/cache_manager.py (_process_league_group_response log message),
  tests/unit/test_cwl_league_rank_self_heal.py.

2026-07-26 (13)
- Added: permanent self-heal for cwl_league_groups.league_rank, closing the gap the (7)/(11)/
  (12) fixes and one-time repair left open — a frozen (cwl_ended=1) row's league_rank was never
  re-examined again, so any row corrupted before the write-time fixes landed would stay wrong
  forever without the manual `reconstruct` script.
  `QBhelperfunctions._cwl_self_heal_league_rank(rows, cwl_season, recorded_league, now=None)`
  (new): reuses the same league-independent "safe middle rank" reasoning validated in (12)'s
  `reconstruct` command — a clan ranked outside the top-3/bottom-2 band of its group (no
  promotion/demotion rule version seen in _CWL_PROMO_RULES_* moves anyone further) is
  guaranteed to have stayed in the same league the following season. If such a clan's current
  live league in clan_name_cache disagrees with the group's frozen league_rank, and the cache
  entry was refreshed within a bounded window after the season ended (roughly day 12 of the
  season's month through day 12 of the *next* month — past that, "current" league may already
  reflect a LATER season, not this one), the frozen value is corrected. In-memory only, no API
  or extra DB calls beyond the one write when a correction actually fires.
  Wired into `update_cwl_group_stats`'s existing `cwl_ended=1` short-circuit (QBhelperfunctions.py)
  — runs every time an ended group's standings are served (i.e. every /leaderboard cwlinfo /
  cwlgroup render), which is also the only point league_rank is ever shown to a user.
  `db_manager.update_cwl_league_rank` gained a `force: bool = False` parameter — the self-heal
  calls it with `force=True` to bypass the `cwl_ended` freeze guard for this one, already-
  verified corrective path; the original derivation path (_process_league_group_response) is
  unaffected and still frozen by the guard as before.
  Added `tests/unit/test_cwl_league_rank_self_heal.py` (11 tests): the pure self-heal function's
  window/band/disagreement/staleness logic, plus its wiring into update_cwl_group_stats
  (correction persisted with force=True; no-op leaves league_rank untouched).
  Tests: 1420 passed, 5 deselected. pyright: 0 errors on all 4 changed/added files.
  Files changed: QBhelperfunctions.py (_cwl_self_heal_league_rank, update_cwl_group_stats),
  qapbot/db_manager.py (update_cwl_league_rank), tests/unit/test_cwl_league_rank_self_heal.py
  (new), qapbot/docs/DATABASE_ARCHITECTURE.md.

2026-07-26 (12)
- Added: `reconstruct` subcommand to `qapbot/scripts/audit_cwl_league_rank.py` — bulk repair
  for cwl_league_groups.league_rank across a whole CWL season, without the ~200,000 live API
  calls a blanket clan refresh would cost.
  Context: found that season 2026-07 has 211,688 cwl_league_groups rows / 26,467 distinct
  groups, but only 6 groups had ever had group_rank computed (that only happens when a clan
  is actively queried via /leaderboard cwlinfo/cwlgroup — the other ~26,461 groups' league_rank
  values, however wrong, have never been shown to any user). The (7)/(11) fixes only stop new
  corruption; they don't repair what's already wrong.
  Approach (a clan finishing a "safe" middle rank — conservatively outside the top 3 / bottom 2
  of its group, a league-independent bound derived from every promotion/demotion count seen in
  QBhelperfunctions._CWL_PROMO_RULES_* — is guaranteed to have stayed in the same league the
  next season):
    1. Compute group_rank/total_stars for every group in the season directly from war_summary
       (already fully populated regardless of who queries a group) — zero API calls.
    2. For a safe-rank clan, cross-check its CURRENT clans.war_league against the recorded
       league_rank, but only trust it if last_checked_via_api is on/after a caller-supplied
       --fresh-after cutoff (the date this season's promotions/demotions applied) — otherwise
       the "current" league could itself reflect a LATER season's outcome.
    3. Where the fresh, safe-rank evidence disagrees with what's stored, correct it.
  Actively-subscribed clans refresh every cycle and passively-tracked Master III+ clans refresh
  every ~12-22h (see fetch_clan_war_data's TTL gate + CLAN_WAR_TRACKING.md's tier model), so
  clans.war_league is very likely already fresh for exactly the leagues this bug hit — meaning
  most of the season was resolvable with NO new API calls at all.
  Added `--refresh-missing`: for the remaining groups with no fresh cached evidence, fetches
  ONE safe-rank clan per group live (not all 8, and not the other ~20k irrelevant clans) via
  CONFIG.coc_email/coc_password, which already auto-select DEV/PROD credentials for whichever
  machine the script runs on.
  Validated against known-correct answers before trusting it: correctly reconstructed both the
  (7) and (11) incidents ("Champion League III" / "Master League III") from scratch. Spot-
  checked a sample of its "disagreement" bucket (cases where multiple safe-rank clans in a
  group disagreed on current league) and confirmed it correctly declines to guess — traced to
  incomplete per-war data skewing that clan's computed rank, not a flaw in the method.
  Results for season 2026-07 (data/qapbot.db, applied): offline pass found 6,465 confirmed
  corrections (0 API calls) + 7,081 already-correct; --refresh-missing resolved 957 of the
  961 remaining candidates for 939 more corrections (5 clans had no live match — deleted/
  private). Total: 7,404 groups corrected. Remaining unresolved: 11,686 groups with incomplete
  war_summary data (can't be ranked at all — a separate, unrelated data-completeness problem,
  not fixable by any API refresh) and 274 flagged as disagreement (left untouched).
  Writes a TSV audit trail (`cwl_reconstruct_<season>.tsv`, gitignored) before any write.
  Tests: 1409 passed, 5 deselected (script has no automated tests — one-time DB tool).
  Files changed: qapbot/scripts/audit_cwl_league_rank.py, .gitignore (ignore the TSV report).

- Fixed: confirmed and fixed a second, related instance of the 2026-07-26 (7)/(10) CWL
  league_rank bug for #2JYQ909PC "The Marines II" (group `e29562f5ac3ddc68`, season "2026-07"),
  found via the (10) audit and independently confirmed against the in-game war log (Kriegsliga-
  Verlauf screen), which shows the clan played July's CWL in "Meister-Liga III" (Master League
  III), not the recorded "Crystal League I".
  This exposed that the 2026-07-26 (7) fix was incomplete: the real flaw isn't just `cwl_ended`
  lag, it's that both the `raw_data` lookup and the `clan_name_cache` fallback pick a single
  "representative" clan's *current* league and write it for the whole group. That's only valid
  while the season is still active — all 8 group members share one league only by construction
  (grouping happens at that shared league). Once the real season ends, promotions/demotions
  apply almost immediately and members diverge to *different* current leagues (some promoted,
  some demoted, some unchanged) — so picking any single one is a coin flip. Confirmed root
  cause here: the two bottom-of-group clans (#292VRCJVU, #2QVGCQQPV, ranks 7-8, demoted after
  July) had "Crystal League I" as their current live league by the time the fallback ran, and
  that value got written for all 8 clans in the group — including the 6 that were promoted or
  stayed unchanged at "Master League III"/"Master League II".
  Fix: `cache_manager.py`'s `_process_league_group_response` — moved the `.state` gate (added in
  (7)) so it also covers the `raw_data` lookup, which previously ran completely unconditionally
  regardless of season state (only the `clan_name_cache` fallback was gated before). Now neither
  source is trusted once the league group reports anything other than "preparation"/"inWar".
  Data correction: corrected `league_rank` from "Crystal League I" to "Master League III" for
  all 8 clans in group `e29562f5ac3ddc68` / season "2026-07" in `data/qapbot.db`, using the
  (10) audit script (`fix e29562f5ac3ddc68 2026-07 "Master League III" --yes`).
  Added 3 tests to `tests/unit/test_cwl_league_rank_season_gate.py`: a divergent-group-members
  reproduction of this exact incident, plus two covering the newly-gated `raw_data` path
  (populates normally during an active season, skipped once the season has ended).

2026-07-26 (7)
- Fixed: `/leaderboard cwlgroup` could show a clan's post-promotion league instead of the
  league it actually competed in for the requested CWL season. Reported case: "The Marines"
  (#2J00L8YRU) competed in Champion League III for CWL 2026-07 but the generated standings
  image showed "Champion League II" (their league *after* the post-season promotion).
  Root cause: `cache_manager.py`'s `_process_league_group_response` falls back to
  `clan_name_cache` to learn a clan's league (the `get_league_group()` API response doesn't
  include `warLeague` per clan). This fallback was gated on the DB's own `cwl_ended` column
  via `update_cwl_league_rank`'s SQL guard (`league_rank IS NULL OR cwl_ended = 0`) — but
  `cwl_ended` only flips once `update_cwl_group_stats_batch` observes every clan's expected
  war count in `war_summary`, which can lag days behind the real-world season end. Clans get
  promoted/demoted almost immediately after CWL ends, so any reprocessing of the league group
  in that lag window (e.g. a delayed round/war file, or the command itself triggering a fresh
  `get_league_group()` call) wrote the clan's *new* league into `league_rank` — which then got
  frozen permanently once `cwl_ended` finally flipped to 1.
  Fix: gate the fallback on the league group's own live API `.state` field instead
  (`"preparation"`/`"inWar"` = season still active, safe to trust `clan_name_cache`; anything
  else = season already ended in-game, skip the fallback entirely and leave `league_rank`
  unset rather than risk recording the wrong league). This is a strictly more reliable signal
  than our own DB bookkeeping, which is derived data that can lag.
  Data correction: manually corrected `league_rank` from "Champion League II" to "Champion
  League III" for all 8 clans in group `8a56c4022a9b2d94` / season "2026-07" in
  `data/qapbot.db`.
  Added `tests/unit/test_cwl_league_rank_season_gate.py` (3 tests) covering active-season
  fallback, warEnded-skips-fallback, and preparation-state-is-active. Docs: added a dated note
  to `qapbot/docs/DATABASE_ARCHITECTURE.md`'s `league_rank` history entry.
  Tests: 1406 passed, 5 deselected.
  Files changed: qapbot/cache_manager.py (_process_league_group_response),
  tests/unit/test_cwl_league_rank_season_gate.py (new), qapbot/docs/DATABASE_ARCHITECTURE.md.

2026-07-25 (4)
- Fixed: Registering by player NAME (e.g. "Killer") when the name wasn't yet in the
  war-history cache incorrectly reported "Player #KILLER could not be found in Clash of
  Clans" instead of finding the player via a live clan-roster search.
  Root cause: `normalize_clan_tag()`'s validation pattern (`^#[A-Z0-9]{5,10}$`) also matches
  short all-letter/digit player names with no explicit '#' prefix (e.g. "Killer" -> 6
  uppercase letters -> passes as a "valid tag"). `PlayerSubstringModal.on_submit()`
  (qapbot/ui_registration.py) tried the direct-tag interpretation BEFORE the live CoC API
  name search across the guild's clans, so a plain name that happened to fit the tag pattern
  hijacked the flow and skipped the name search entirely.
  Fix: reordered the fallback — an explicit leading '#' is now required to prioritize the
  direct-tag path; otherwise the live API name search (across `self.clans_in_guild`) runs
  first, and only falls back to interpreting the input as a raw tag if that search finds
  nothing. This is a pure interaction-order fix; `normalize_clan_tag()` itself is unchanged
  since it's still needed and correct for genuine tag input.
  Also audited every location that reads `member_clans`/`member_families` from guild config
  for missing family-expansion ("family-blind") bugs. Found and fixed one: the role-sync
  trigger in `qapbot/coc_cache.py` (`_maybe_trigger_role_sync`) only checked
  `clan_tag in config.get("member_clans", [])`, so guilds configured with ONLY a clan family
  (no individual member clans — like the reporter's server) never got CoC-role/clan-role
  syncs triggered for clan-member updates. Fixed to also expand `member_families` into their
  constituent clan tags, matching the pattern already used correctly everywhere else
  (`get_guild_clans_including_member_config`, `is_player_in_member_clans`,
  `guild_role_manager.sync_roles_for_user`, `cache_manager._is_clan_tracked`, etc.) — all of
  which were confirmed already family-aware and needed no changes.
  Files changed: qapbot/ui_registration.py (PlayerSubstringModal.on_submit),
  qapbot/coc_cache.py. All 1403 tests pass.

2026-07-18 (11)
- Fixed: `/whois player <name>` was inserting a bogus placeholder row into the `clans` table
  for the *reported player's own tag*, polluting the table with fake "clans" (name='Unknown').
  Root cause: `leaderboard_messages.clan_tag` has no FK constraint on purpose — it's reused to
  store clan tags, family tags, AND (for `mode == "whois_player"`) a player tag — but
  `_save_leaderboard_message_impl()` in `qapbot/db_manager.py` unconditionally called
  `_ensure_clan_exists(clan_tag)` whenever clan_tag was truthy, which can't distinguish a
  player tag from a clan tag and silently created a placeholder `clans` row for it.
  Fix: removed the erroneous `_ensure_clan_exists()` call from `_save_leaderboard_message_impl()`
  (the column has no FK, so nothing needs "ensuring").
  Added: self-healing cleanup so bogus/orphaned `clans` rows don't accumulate going forward.
  `db_manager.is_clan_tag_referenced()` / `delete_clan_if_unreferenced()` (+
  `CACHE.purge_clan_if_orphaned()` wrapper) hard-delete a `clans` row once `_mark_clan_deleted()`
  (QBhelperfunctions.py) confirms via the CoC API that a clan_tag no longer exists (404
  NotFound) — but ONLY if nothing else in the database still refers to it (checks
  clan_family_members, user_players.current_clan_tag, guild_member_clans, guild_clan_roles,
  subscriptions, leaderboard_messages, and historical war_summary/war_attacks in both the hot
  and history DB schemas). Previously such clans were only soft-deleted (`is_deleted=True`)
  and left in the table forever.
  Added: `qapbot/scripts/cleanup_orphaned_clans.py` — one-off maintenance script to remove
  existing bad placeholder rows from PROD (dry-run by default, `--execute` to delete;
  candidates = `name='Unknown' AND last_checked_via_api IS NULL`, a pattern that only ever
  occurs via the placeholder-insert path, so real clans are never affected).
  Files changed: qapbot/db_manager.py, qapbot/cache_manager.py, QBhelperfunctions.py,
  qapbot/scripts/cleanup_orphaned_clans.py.
  All 1401 tests pass.
  FOLLOW-UP FIX (same day): PROD dry run showed 2 of 9 bogus rows were incorrectly kept as
  "REFERENCED" — e.g. #890JPCR00 matched a leaderboard_messages row with mode='whois_player',
  but that row's clan_tag column holds the SAME reported player's tag (the exact bug that
  created the bogus clans row in the first place). Treating a whois_player match as a real
  reference made `is_clan_tag_referenced()` circularly protect the bogus rows forever.
  Fix: `is_clan_tag_referenced()` now excludes `mode = 'whois_player'` rows when checking
  leaderboard_messages (`AND mode != 'whois_player'` in the query) — only genuine clan/family
  leaderboard-mode rows count as a real reference. Affects both the self-healing routine and
  cleanup_orphaned_clans.py (they share this method). All 1401 tests still pass.

- Improved: nightly DB maintenance sequencing, logging, and /admin command scope (QapBot.py,
  QBdiscordcmds.py, translations). Investigated from a PROD log showing [ARCHIVE-MOVE] starting
  literally 6ms after "[CYCLE-END] Update cycle completed" — overlapping with that same cycle's
  own [COC-CACHE-CLEANUP]/gc.collect() post-cycle cleanup, both running concurrently on separate
  worker threads and contending for server-machine disk I/O and CPU.
  1. Fixed: relocated the entire nightly-maintenance scheduling block (03:00 UTC due-check +
     `asyncio.create_task(_nightly_maintenance_task())` + monthly migration due-check) from
     immediately after "[CYCLE-END] Update cycle completed" to immediately before "Sleeping for
     N seconds" — i.e. after `_post_cycle_cleanup()` (gc.collect/cache cleanup) and memtrace have
     already finished, and after the maintenance_pending/optimize_db_pending/force_cycle_pending
     early-`continue` checks (which now also correctly prevent nightly maintenance from ever
     racing a concurrent /admin Maintenance Start shutdown or an immediate-next-cycle request —
     a latent bug in the old ordering, now fixed as a side effect). Maintenance now only starts
     once the cycle has truly finished and is about to enter its sleep wait.
  2+3. Added `[NIGHTLY-MAINTENANCE] START` / `[NIGHTLY-MAINTENANCE] END — total duration X.Xs`
     log markers wrapping the whole routine (archive move + optional monthly migration + WAL

     ([ARCHIVE-MOVE], [DB-MAINT]) had their own timing, with no single marker for the nightly
     routine as a whole.
  4. Investigated /admin Optimize DB before changing it: confirmed it only ever called
     `nightly_db_maintenance()` (WAL checkpoint/REINDEX/VACUUM/ANALYZE) — it never ran the
     archive-move step or the monthly hot->history migration step that the *scheduled* nightly
     task performs, so admin-triggered runs were doing strictly less than the real nightly
     routine. Fixed: extracted the full routine into a new shared
     `run_nightly_maintenance_routine(db_mgr, run_migration)` (QapBot.py) plus a shared
     `is_monthly_migration_due()` helper (hydrates + atomically claims the day-1 migration flag,
     shared between the scheduled task and the admin command so neither double-runs migration
     the same day) — both the scheduled task and both /admin code paths (deferred-while-cycle-
     running, and immediate-when-idle) now call the exact same routine. Renamed the Discord-facing
     command choice from "Optimize DB" to "Execute Nightly Maintenance" (internal `action_norm`
     value "OPTIMIZE_DB" and the `optimize_db_pending`/`QBcore` flag names deliberately left

2026-07-18 (8)
- Fixed: unyielded ~26K-clan scan loop in PHASE 3B candidate-building (QapBot.py `main()`).
  Follow-up to the CWL DB-blocking investigation: PHASE 3B's candidate-building loop
  (`for safe_tag in _temp_files_by_clan:`, deciding which passive clans need temp-file
  finalization) iterates every clan with a temp file (~26K in PROD) with ZERO yield points —
  same class of bug as the earlier clan-categorization-loop fix. Tier 1 (skip-until dict) and
  Tier 2 (in-memory temp_war_metadata) are cheap, but any clan with no temp_war_metadata entry
  (or a state Tier 2 doesn't cover) falls straight through to Tier 3, which does a real
  `os.path.getmtime()` syscall per clan — a genuine blocking disk syscall directly on the
  event-loop thread, potentially thousands of times per cycle with no yields in between.
  Fix: added `await asyncio.sleep(0)` every 2000 clans (same pattern as the categorize-loop
  fix), plus `[PHASE-3B-SCAN-TIMING] Scanned N clan(s) in X.XXXs (tier3_stat_calls=N,
  candidates=N)` INFO logging to measure the real Tier-3 hit rate and cost going forward
  (previously invisible — no timing existed for this loop at all). Files changed: QapBot.py.
  All 1401 tests pass. Next step: read the next PROD capture's [PHASE-3B-SCAN-TIMING] line to
  see how often Tier 3 actually fires and whether further optimization (e.g. extending Tier 2's
  metadata coverage to more states) is worth pursuing.

2026-07-18 (7)
- Fixed: blocking synchronous DB calls in CWL-related async code paths (QBhelperfunctions.py).
  User asked to check whether any DB writes during the update cycle are blocking, specifically
  flagging that CWL season (archived wars + additional CWL tables) makes this more expensive.
  Found 6 direct, unwrapped calls to `_sync`-suffixed db_manager methods (plain `sqlite3`, not
  aiosqlite) inside `async def` functions that are part of the hot update-cycle path — each one
  blocks the event loop (Discord heartbeat/interactions) for its I/O duration every time it runs,
  and these are exactly the CWL-specific checks that fire most often during CWL season:
  1. `generate_cwlinfo_embeds()` (~line 1715) — `is_latest_cwl_season_ended_sync()`, called every
     cycle while posting the "cwlinfo" leaderboard for every subscribed clan.
  2. `_find_active_cwl_war_for_clan()` Guard B (~line 5421) — `is_latest_cwl_season_ended_sync()`,
     called from the Phase-1 hot path for every clan needing the CWL fallback.
  3+4. `fetch_clan_war_data()`'s two notInWar CWL-fallback branches (~lines 6396, 6436) — same
     `is_latest_cwl_season_ended_sync()` check, called for every clan every cycle.
  5. `fetch_clan_war_data()`'s "Layer 2 pre-save" guard (~line 6460) —
     `get_cwl_round_for_war_tag_sync()`, called for every CWL-active clan every cycle.
  6. `process_orphaned_cwl_wars()`'s `fetch_and_update_orphan()` (~line 7048) — same
     `get_cwl_round_for_war_tag_sync()` check, called once per orphaned CWL war inside an
     `asyncio.gather()` (up to 20 concurrent via Semaphore) — the most CWL-season-heavy of the six.
  All 6 were harmless when CWL-related activity was low (fast enough not to notice), but scale
  with CWL season's higher CWL-clan/orphaned-war counts — exactly the "gets pretty expensive"
  scenario flagged. Fix: wrapped each in `await asyncio.to_thread(...)`, matching the existing
  pattern already used correctly elsewhere in the same functions (e.g. `save_war_object` calls
  right next to several of these). One occurrence (~line 4579, inside `_process_war_history`
  called from `manage_war_files`) was already safe — confirmed it runs inside a call chain
  already dispatched via `asyncio.to_thread(_with_war_batch, ...)` from QapBot.py Phase-3, so it
  was correctly left unwrapped (wrapping it again would spawn a redundant nested thread-pool call).
  All DB WRITE paths during the cycle (war_attacks/war_summary appends via `add_war_data_sync`/
  `flush_pending_war_writes`, `bulk_update_clan_timestamps`, `upsert_cwl_league_data`) were also
  audited: writes either use aiosqlite natively (async, non-blocking by design) or run inside an
  `asyncio.to_thread(_with_war_batch, ...)`-wrapped call chain — all confirmed already
  non-blocking. Files changed: QBhelperfunctions.py. All 1401 tests pass.

- Analyzed: full update-cycle time-gap sweep via qapbot/scripts/log_time_gaps.py against
  data/logs/qapbot.log (190K lines, ~9h of PROD-scale activity) to find further blocking
  segments beyond the gc.collect() fix earlier today. Found two recurring, previously-silent
  gaps that repeated on EVERY cycle (confirmed via ~90-100 occurrences each in the top-400
  gap list), independent of the already-excluded nightly-maintenance/startup windows:
  1. "Starting clan war info updates..." → next log line: a consistent ~4.1-4.2s gap on
     literally every cycle, regardless of active/inactive clan counts (300 to 5300+).
     Root cause: the clan categorization loop in main() (QapBot.py) does
     `for clan_tag in list(CACHE.clan_name_cache.keys())` with ZERO yield points. This
     cache holds ~380K entries in PROD (confirmed via "[DB-READ] Loaded 379620 clans from
     database" in rotated logs — every clan ever encountered via CWL family harvesting,
     not just this cycle's counts), so the loop's ~380K synchronous dict-lookup/datetime-
     parse iterations ran as one uninterrupted block, freezing Discord heartbeat/gateway
     processing and slash-command handling for ~4s every single cycle (~5min), all day.
     Fix: added `await asyncio.sleep(0)` every 2000 iterations (~190 yields/cycle,
     negligible overhead) so the event loop can interleave other tasks throughout the
     loop instead of being frozen for its entire ~4s duration. Also added
     `[CATEGORIZE-TIMING] Categorized N clan(s) in X.XXXs` INFO log to make the total
     cost visible going forward without needing DEBUG.
  2. "Clan updates complete: ..." → "[ROLE-SYNC] Starting guild-wide role sync...": a
     consistent 8-26s silent gap on every cycle (only 120 user_accounts / ~21 active wars
     — too small for the in-memory work alone to plausibly take that long; root cause not
     yet pinpointed from static code review). The only code that runs in this window is
     check_wars_for_notifications() (qapbot/war_notifications.py). That function already
     yields via `await asyncio.sleep(0)` between wars/sub-steps, so it likely isn't a raw
     "frozen event loop" bug like #1, but the *wall-clock* cost is still large and
     unexplained (observed even when zero notifications are sent this cycle — 20 of 21
     wars have no players to notify, yet the loop still costs ~0.7s/war on average before
     reaching the one war that does need a reminder).
     Fix (partial — diagnostics only, root cause pending real PROD data): added detailed
     timing instrumentation:
       · `[NOTIFY-TIMING] index_build=... get_active_wars=... war_loop=... total=...
         (active_wars=N, slowest=war_id:X.XXXs)` — logged at the end of every call.
       · `[NOTIFY-WAR-TIMING] war=... get_reminders=... get_attacks_remaining=...
         send_channel=... total=...` — logged per-war whenever that single war's
         processing exceeds 0.3s, to pinpoint which sub-step (likely
         `_send_channel_war_notification`'s per-guild `CACHE.subscriptions` iteration,
         suspected but unconfirmed) is the actual cost driver.
     Next step once deployed: read the next cycle's [NOTIFY-TIMING]/[NOTIFY-WAR-TIMING]
     lines to confirm the culprit sub-step, then apply a targeted fix (index the
     subscriptions-by-clan-tag lookup, and/or move any confirmed synchronous hot loop to
     asyncio.to_thread()).
  Excluded from this analysis per explicit scope: nightly DB maintenance (REINDEX/VACUUM,
  already has its own EXCLUSIVE-lock + db_maintenance_mode guard) and bot startup routine.
  Files changed: QapBot.py (categorize-loop yields + timing), qapbot/war_notifications.py
  (NOTIFY-TIMING / NOTIFY-WAR-TIMING instrumentation). All 1401 tests pass.
